issues.title: file_read tool accepts paths not in the current commit, driving review to status: partial
issues.body:
## OpenCodeReview Version

- Reproduced on `v1.9.4 (f7344e79) windows/amd64` (production)
- Also affected on `v1.9.5 (ea1de41a windows/amd64)` (local)
- Installed via `npm install -g @alibaba-group/open-code-review`

## Operating System

Windows (Jenkins agent on Windows Server; reproducible from any platform)

## Installation Method

npm (global)

## LLM Provider / Model

`deepseek` / `deepseek-v4-flash` (also seen to reproduce on other providers per #287)

## Bug description

During `ocr review --commit <sha>` on a focused change, the LLM independently calls its `file_read` tool with paths that **do not exist in the commit at all**. OCR executes the read via `git show <commit>:<path>`, git returns "fatal: path ... does not exist in <sha>", and the failed tool call is reported back to the LLM. When the hallucination is severe enough (or when the LLM is persistent), the review run goes from `status: complete` to `status: partial`, and the Jenkins pipeline fails OCR Review.

Three consecutive failed builds on the same Gerrit Change 4700 (different patchsets rebased on top of each other) all failed with the same root cause, in slightly different ways:

| Patchset | Commit SHA | Hallucinated path (file_read) | File actually exists? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `b087039` | `DOC/云配置项/project.yct` | **Never existed** (path entirely invented by LLM) |
| 4 | `d86b0f1` | `App/MID/RF/CendricApp/src/phscaCendricCadsApp.c` | **Deleted in this commit** (file lived in history but this PR removed the entire Cendric tree) |
| 4 | `d86b0f1` | `App/MID/RF/CendricSwTimer/src/phscaCendricCadsSwTimer.c` | **Deleted in this commit** (same) |

The hallucination has two distinct mechanisms:

1. **Imagined paths** that were never in the repo (e.g. `DOC/云配置项/project.yct` — possibly extrapolated from the commit subject's mention of "切换 RF 芯片").
2. **Deleted-in-this-commit paths** that the LLM remembers from the project's history / training data (e.g. Cendric legacy files — this commit removes the Cendric tree, but the LLM still calls file_read on its members).

OCR executes the read either way, and each call that fails contributes to driving the run into `partial`.

## Steps to reproduce

The exact conditions are LLM-specific, but a high-rate reproduction recipe:

1. Pick a focused commit that touches a small number of files in one area, AND that **removes or renames** other files elsewhere in the repo.
2. Run `ocr review --commit <sha> --provider deepseek --model deepseek-v4-flash --format json --timeout 30` (or any comparable review).
3. After ~5–10 minutes, observe:
   - `status: partial` instead of `status: complete`
   - In the logs: `✘ file_read failed: file "<hallucinated path>" not found: git show <sha>:<path>: ... fatal: path '<path>' does not exist in <sha>` — one or more such entries
   - No `code_comment` tool call on the actually-changed files; the LLM has burned the LLM budget retrying the missing file or pivoted away

A simpler deterministic repro: hand-craft a prompt that says "review this commit" while seeding the LLM with a "looks like a project config file at `DOC/云配置项/project.yct>"-style misdirection. The model will call `file_read("DOC/云配置项/project.yct")` and OCR will fail it.

## Expected behavior

The `file_read` tool is supposed to be a fallback for the LLM to inspect a file it has been told about (typically the changed files in the diff, or files referenced by changed code). It is **not** supposed to allow free-form exploration of unrelated paths in the commit's history.

Desired properties:

- `file_read` accepts only paths that **actually exist in the current commit** (the diff's `Ref`); a non-existent path is rejected up-front, not after a wasted `git show` call.
- Optionally, `file_read` is constrained to the changed files in the diff (or to a small allowlist provided by the user via `--include`). A focused `ocr review` of a 10-file commit should never let the model fetch a 200-file tree.
- The `--exclude` / `--path` family of flags already exists for `ocr scan`; review mode should expose the same controls (`--include` for review, or a path allowlist knob).
- When a `file_read` call is rejected, OCR should report it as a deterministic structural error, not a transient failure that the retry loop can re-attempt. (Today, a hallucinated path makes `status: partial` because the retry treats it as flaky.)
- `existing_code` matching and the diff/filter pipeline should not be perturbed; the constraint is purely on the input side.

## Proposed direction

Add a path-validity check on `file_read` (and the related read-oriented tools) before the git call, against the same `Ref` the read is intended to resolve into. Two reasonable shapes:

1. **Hard allowlist**: read paths must be a subset of the changed files in the diff (or a user-supplied `--include` set). Anything else returns a clean "path is not in this review scope" and is not retried.
2. **Soft guard**: read paths must be a path that exists at the ref. If it does not, return a one-line "no such file" error and do not contribute to the partial status (or trigger retry).

Either shape kills the hallucination-driven partial-status path. The hard allowlist is closer to what `ocr scan --path` already supports; the soft guard is a smaller change.

A related improvement, separately tracked in #981, is bounding `file_read_diff` output size; the two are complementary and should not be conflated.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `file_read` request for a path that does not exist in the current commit's tree returns a deterministic structural error and is **not** retried by the partial-status retry loop.
- [ ] A `file_read` request for a path that is not in the diff's changed files (and not in a user-supplied allowlist) is rejected with a clear "out of review scope" message.
- [ ] The 3 reproduction patterns above (imagined path, deleted-in-commit path) no longer drive `ocr review` to `status: partial`.
- [ ] Normal review flow on focused commits is unchanged (existing legitimate reads still work).
- [ ] A focused test exercises each reproduction pattern and asserts the review run ends in `status: complete` with the expected comment set.

## Affected Area

Built-in Tools (file_read, code_search, etc.); review pipeline (partial-status retry policy).

## See also

- **#287** — `file_read` call failures in a monorepo (closed as completed, no functional fix shipped). Different root cause (relative path resolution in subdirectory) but the same symptom: `file_read` produces a "fatal: path ... does not exist" message, and the run goes partial.
- **#981** — `file_read_diff` output is unbounded and can exhaust the LLM context window. Same tool family, different overflow mode.
- **#167** — Near-duplicate comments with wrong filenames. Different category but tangentially related to model/filename mismatches.

## Logs

Sample (Patchset 4, v1.9.4, `deepseek-v4-flash`):

```
11:14:40  [OCR] attempt 1/2 status=partial elapsed=541s, retrying…
11:15:18  [ocr]   ✘ file_read failed: file "App/MID/RF/CendricApp/src/phscaCendricCadsApp.c" not found: git show d86b0f1:App/MID/RF/CendricApp/src/phscaCendricCadsApp.c: exit status 128: fatal: path 'App/MID/RF/CendricApp/src/phscaCendricCadsApp.c' does not exist in 'd86b0f1'
11:15:18  [ocr]   ✘ file_read failed: file "App/MID/RF/CendricSwTimer/src/phscaCendricCadsSwTimer.c" not found: git show d86b0f1:App/MID/RF/CendricSwTimer/src/phscaCendricCadsSwTimer.c: exit status 128: fatal: path 'App/MID/RF/CendricSwTimer/src/phscaCendricCadsSwTimer.c' does not exist in 'd86b0f1'
11:24:25  [ERROR] OCR 未完整结束,status=partial
```
issues.triage_reason: The scope is ambiguous: a hard allowlist vs. a soft guard in internal/tool/file_read.go and filereader.go needs a maintainer decision, and it is unclear that a failed file_read is what actually causes status=partial in the llmloop retry policy.
issues.skip_reason: coder gave up: file_read now returns a structural 'Error: ... does not exist in this review's commit and is out of review scope' result when the ref's tree (checked via git ls-tree, not localized stderr) lacks the path, so these no longer surface as tool failures. Not done: the diff-changed-files allowlist for paths that exist at the ref, and a review-level test that the run ends in status complete.
issues.feedback:
Attempt 1:
Reviewer rejected:
- existsAtRef treats every git cat-file error (timeout, cancelled context, bad ref, runner failure) as 'file does not exist', so transient failures are misreported to the model as deterministic missing-file results; only a genuine not-found should map to this message
- The issue's allowlist criterion is not implemented: reads outside the diff's changed files are not rejected with an out-of-review-scope message
- Nothing verifies that the partial-status/retry behaviour actually changes; the tests only check Execute's return value, not that a review ends in status complete
- cat-file -e call lacks --end-of-options, unlike the existing git show calls, and adds an extra git process per read
- Tests are redundant (Execute assertion duplicated) and miss the existing-path, range-mode and non-not-found failure cases

Attempt 2:
Reviewer rejected:
- The issue's second acceptance criterion is still not implemented: a file_read for a path outside the diff's changed files (or a user allowlist) is not rejected with an 'out of review scope' message. Only non-existent paths get a softer message. This was raised in round 1 and ignored.
- No test shows that a review ends in status complete instead of partial. The tests only check Execute's return value. Nothing shows that the partial/retry path is affected, or that the returned string is treated as non-retryable. The imagined-path and deleted-in-commit cases are not tested as a review run with an expected comment set.
- IsPathNotFound matches English git stderr text ('does not exist in', 'exists on disk, but not in'). Production git runs without LC_ALL=C, so under a localized git the match fails and the old failing behavior returns silently. Detect not-found without parsing localized text, for example by checking the path with git ls-tree or cat-file --end-of-options at the ref. Or force LC_ALL=C on the git command.
- The git show stderr is now appended to every non-not-found error in readLinesFromGitShow. That changes error text for all callers without a test.
issues.summary: file_read now maps git's genuine 'path does not exist in <ref>' failure (detected from git stderr, no extra process) to a structural 'Error:' result instead of a tool failure, so hallucinated or deleted paths no longer count as failed calls; timeouts, cancellation, bad refs and runner errors still surface as errors. Soft-guard option only: no changed-files allowlist or --include flag, and no end-to-end test of review status complete or the retry loop. Added unit tests for commit/range/runner modes, bad ref and the matcher.
issues.repro_notes: file_read in commit mode for a path absent from the commit returns a Go error wrapping 'git show ...: exit status 128' instead of a clean structural 'Error:' result; the test fails on that assertion.

issues.title: fix(llm): preserve opaque tool-call fields across OpenAI-compatible turns
issues.body:
## Version

OCR v1.9.4 and current `main` (`b8bee971849d1fee2536e91a6b716168ccb9ed29`).

## Problem

Some OpenAI-compatible providers attach opaque metadata to assistant tool calls that must be echoed unchanged on later turns. Vertex AI's OpenAI-compatible Gemini endpoint returns a thought signature under `tool_calls[].extra_content`. OCR maps the response to its own `ToolCall` with only `id`, `type`, and `function`, so the next request drops `extra_content` and the provider rejects it with HTTP 400.

This affects normal repository tools: turn one can call `file_read`, but turn two fails before the model can continue the review.

## Reproduction

1. Configure the OpenAI Chat Completions protocol against Vertex AI's OpenAI-compatible endpoint with Gemini 3.
2. Run a review that causes a repository tool call.
3. The first completion succeeds and returns `tool_calls[].extra_content.google.thought_signature`.
4. OCR executes the tool but omits `extra_content` from the assistant tool-call history.
5. The second completion returns HTTP 400.

A provider-independent reproduction is a two-request fake OpenAI server: return an unknown `extra_content` object on the first tool call, then require it on the second request.

## Expected behavior

OCR should preserve unknown, valid JSON fields from provider-returned function tool calls and echo them on subsequent turns. Reserved standard fields (`id`, `type`, `function`) must remain owned by OCR, malformed data must not be forwarded, and opaque fields should not be written to normal review/session logs.

## Proposed fix

Keep the unknown tool-call fields as non-serialized raw JSON on OCR's internal `ToolCall`, then use the OpenAI SDK's supported `SetExtraFields` mechanism when rebuilding assistant history. Add an end-to-end adapter regression test that proves an opaque nested field survives response mapping and the next request.
issues.triage_reason: internal/llm/client.go already replays `extra_content` via ToolCall.ExtraContent and SetExtraFields. The issue asks to generalize this to arbitrary unknown fields (toolCallExtraContent, the history build, session/history.go persistence and copying), which is doable but needs design judgement and touches several places.

Your token may still be valid. Check your network connection and try again.

To authenticate, you can use any of the following methods:
  • Start 'copilot' and run the '/login' command
  • Set the COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  • Run 'gh auth login' to authenticate with the GitHub CLI
issues.feedback:
Attempt 1:
Reviewer rejected:
- Streaming path never captures ExtraFields: the accumulator drops unmodeled tool-call fields (the reason extra_content is captured separately from toolDelta.JSON.ExtraFields), so streamed tool calls lose opaque fields like vendor_meta and turn two still fails. Capture and map them per tool-call index in the stream loop, with a streaming regression test.
- Session persistence (internal/session/history.go toolCallJSON and the entry map near line 533) carries ExtraContent but not ExtraFields, so saved or resumed sessions drop them. Persist them there, or deliberately handle them, keeping in mind the issue's requirement not to write opaque fields to normal logs.
- Missing tests for the new streaming and session code, and for copyToolCalls deep-copy of ExtraFields.

Attempt 2:
Reviewer rejected:
- Non-streaming toolCallExtraFields forwards every non-reserved key, including a provider-returned "index" on tool calls (not modeled by the SDK's non-stream tool-call type), and echoes it back on the next request; strict OpenAI-compatible providers can reject this with HTTP 400, regressing providers that work today. Exclude index (and any other standard/streaming-only keys) from replay and add a test covering a non-streaming response containing "index".
issues.summary: Preserve unknown tool-call fields (non-streaming and streaming) as non-serialized ToolCall.ExtraFields and replay them via SetExtraFields; reserved fields incl. index excluded; not persisted in sessions but deep-copied; tests added.
issues.repro_notes: An unknown tool_calls[] field (vendor_meta) returned by the provider is not replayed in the rebuilt assistant history; only extra_content is preserved today. The test fails with: assistant tool-call history dropped unknown field.

issues.title: Default ocr_version 'latest' changes review behavior even under a fully pinned Action reference
issues.body:
## Problem

Split out of #816 so that issue can close with the part everyone agrees on (SHA-pinning the internal `actions/*` references, #836). This issue tracks the remaining open design question.

With the Action fully SHA-pinned, review behavior still changes over time because the CLI is installed at run time with `ocr_version` defaulting to `latest`:

```bash
npm install -g "@alibaba-group/open-code-review@${OCR_VERSION}"  # default: latest
```

A breaking or behavior-changing CLI release reaches every default-configured workflow immediately — including workflows whose owners deliberately pinned `uses: alibaba/open-code-review@<sha>` — and "run the same review as last week" is not reproducible without knowing to also pin `ocr_version`.

## Positions so far (from the #816 discussion)

**Maintainers** ([comment](https://github.com/alibaba/open-code-review/issues/816#issuecomment-5240732038)): keep `latest` as the default so most consumers pick up bug fixes and new detectors automatically; flipping the default would silently strand workflows on old CLI versions unless users bump `ocr_version` each release. Preference: make the pinning path more discoverable in the README instead.

**Reporter**: default the CLI version to the Action's own release (`v1.8.10` action → `ocr_version: 1.8.10`), keep `latest` as an explicit opt-in, and offer a floating major (`@v1`) so compatible fixes auto-follow while breaking changes require a deliberate `@v2`. Comparable actions mostly avoid unbounded `latest` for the tool itself (trivy-action pins an exact default; goreleaser defaults `~> v2`; codeql recommends `@v4` major floating) — detailed comparison in [#816](https://github.com/alibaba/open-code-review/issues/816#issuecomment-5241004371).

## Current state

#836 documents the dual pin (Action SHA + `ocr_version`) in a "Reproducible pinning" section of the GitHub Actions example README — the maintainers' discoverability suggestion. The default itself is unchanged; whether it should be is this issue.

No code change should land here until maintainers pick a direction.
issues.triage_reason: The issue is an unresolved design decision: maintainers want to keep `ocr_version` defaulting to `latest`, and the issue says no change should land until they choose. Any change would also touch the Action definition or README under .github/ or similar paths the bot cannot edit.
issues.skip_reason: triage: not feasible: The issue is an unresolved design decision: maintainers want to keep `ocr_version` defaulting to `latest`, and the issue says no change should land until they choose. Any change would also touch the Action definition or README under .github/ or similar paths the bot cannot edit.

issues.title: Release cut is not a reviewable repository change
issues.body:
## Problem

The current maintainer-pushed **v*** tag is a valid release decision, but the decision is not represented as a reviewable repository change: the next version, changelog, release contents, and publication timing are only visible after the tag is pushed.

This issue is **not** proposing that CI publish every merge, build arbitrary HEAD snapshots, or create rolling tags. Ordinary pull requests should continue to merge without publishing anything.

There are two separate approvals:

- merging a feature/fix PR approves that code for main;
- cutting a release approves a specific batch of changes, version, changelog, and a set of irreversible registry writes.

*(The npm publication-atomicity defects that were originally part of this issue — a failed publish leaving a public partial release, and existence-only resume — are concrete workflow bugs independent of this process question, and now live in #840.)*

## Non-goals

- No automatic publication for every merge to main.
- No HEAD, nightly, or moving snapshot tag.
- No Git tag or changelog per platform package.
- No independently versioned platform packages.
- No attempt to roll back or overwrite an immutable npm version.

## Proposed design

### 1. Keep one logical product and one version

Treat OpenCodeReview as one Go CLI release: one committed product version, one changelog, one **vX.Y.Z** Git tag, one GitHub Release, and seven npm registry artifacts at the same exact version (six platform packages + the root wrapper, as implementation artifacts of npm's platform-selection model rather than separate release units).

### 2. Add an explicit release cut

Use Release Please only for the version/changelog PR layer, configured as one root Go/CLI release:

- Normal merges update or open the release PR; they do not publish.
- A maintainer merges the release PR when the accumulated changes are ready — that merge is the explicit release approval, reviewable as an ordinary diff (version bump + changelog + contents).
- Release Please does not publish the GitHub Release itself; the existing release workflow does, after artifact publication and verification (see #840 for the ordering requirements).

Release Please fits because the repository already uses Conventional Commit titles and has one logical product. It does not replace the native build or npm publisher.

### 3. Reduce duplicated release metadata

Keep one machine-readable target list (Go OS/arch, npm package name, npm os/cpu, artifact name, packaged binary filename) consumed by the build matrix, npm package generator, checksum verifier, fallback downloader, and smoke tests.

### 4. Use short-lived publication identity

Move npm publication to Trusted Publishing/OIDC with provenance, protected by the release environment, instead of a long-lived NPM_TOKEN in the self-hosted runner's home directory.

## Why not Changesets as the publisher?

Changesets is a good version-intent tool, but it does not build native targets or replace the custom publisher this repository needs either way. A root-only Changesets setup would add per-PR fragments without removing that publisher. For a single-product Conventional Commit repository, Release Please is the smaller version/changelog layer.

## Acceptance criteria

- Ordinary merges never publish.
- A maintainer can review the exact version, changelog, and contents before the release happens.
- One release creates exactly one product tag and one GitHub Release.
- All binaries and npm packages carry the same version.
- No long-lived npm token is required by the release job.

## Large-project references

- Trivy: Release Please for the release cut, followed by a custom multi-platform GoReleaser pipeline: https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy/blob/main/.github/workflows/release-please.yaml
- Turborepo: one version source, generated platform packages, native-first/root-last publication: https://github.com/vercel/turborepo/blob/main/.github/workflows/turborepo-release.yml
- esbuild: platform packages first, root package and public release last: https://github.com/evanw/esbuild/blob/main/Makefile
- Oxlint/Oxc: generated NAPI packages, product-level tags, post-publish cross-platform smoke tests: https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/blob/main/.github/workflows/release_apps.yml
issues.triage_reason: Release-process redesign (Release Please, OIDC npm publishing, shared target list) lives in .github/workflows, scripts/ and package.json, which the bot may not edit, and it needs maintainer decisions.
issues.skip_reason: triage: not feasible: Release-process redesign (Release Please, OIDC npm publishing, shared target list) lives in .github/workflows, scripts/ and package.json, which the bot may not edit, and it needs maintainer decisions.

issues.title: Support --provider flag in ocr review/scan commands for runtime LLM provider override
issues.body:
### Problem Statement

Currently, changing the LLM provider or model requires running `ocr config set provider <name>` and `ocr config set model <name>` to persist the configuration globally. This is inconvenient for users who:

1. Want to quickly test different models/providers for a single review without affecting the default configuration
2. Need to run multiple reviews with different providers in CI/CD pipelines
3. Want to avoid accidentally changing the global default when testing
4. Need to override provider/model in automation scripts

Currently, `ocr review` only supports `--model` but not `--provider`, making it impossible to dynamically switch providers at runtime.

### Proposed Solution

Add `--provider` and `--model` command-line flags to `ocr review` and `ocr scan` commands to allow dynamic provider/model specification without modifying the configuration file.

Proposed syntax:
```bash
# Specify both provider and model at runtime
ocr review --from main --to feature-branch --provider anthropic --model claude-opus-4-6
ocr review --commit abc123 --provider openai --model gpt-4o
ocr scan --provider deepseek --model deepseek-v4-flash

# Use existing default if not specified
ocr review --from main --to feature-branch --model claude-3.5-sonnet  # uses current provider
ocr review --from main --to feature-branch --provider openai  # uses provider's default model
```

Behavior:
- Runtime flags override the configuration file defaults
- Do not modify `~/.opencodereview/config.json`
- Support both built-in and custom providers
- Validate provider/model existence before starting review
- When resuming sessions, use the runtime-specified provider/model (not the original session's provider)

### Alternatives Considered

1. Use environment variables to override provider/model - but this doesn't provide per-command granularity
2. Continue with current approach - force users to use `ocr config set` for temporary changes
3. Add a temporary config file option - more complex and less intuitive than CLI flags

### Affected Area

CLI / Commands, Configuration

### Additional Context

Related observations:
- Session resume only saves `Model`, not `Provider`, making provider changes during resume potentially unsafe
- Consider also documenting whether resumed sessions should use the original or new provider/model
- This feature would be particularly useful for CI/CD integrations where different steps might need different models

Example use case:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# First pass: quick review with fast model
ocr review --from main --to feature --provider deepseek --model deepseek-v4-flash --timeout 5

# Second pass: detailed review with high-quality model if needed
if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
  ocr review --from main --to feature --provider anthropic --model claude-opus-4-6
fi
```
issues.triage_reason: --provider and --model are already implemented via addProviderFlag/addModelFlag in cmd/opencodereview/shared_flags.go and wired in review_cmd.go and scan_cmd.go; the issue is largely already resolved, and any leftover gap (e.g. resume provider handling) is unspecified and needs a maintainer decision.

issues.title: Support using Claude Code's existing login session (Team/Pro plan) instead of requiring a separate Anthropic API key
issues.body:
### Problem Statement

Currently, ocr requires a standalone LLM credential to be configured via ocr config set llm.auth_token ... (or OCR_LLM_TOKEN). This works for users who have a pay-as-you-go Anthropic API key, but it doesn't work for users like myself who access Claude only through a Claude Code Team/Pro plan subscription.
Claude Code itself authenticates via an OAuth/session login (not a raw API key), and that login is tied to the subscription's included usage rather than metered API billing. Since open-code-review supports being invoked as a Claude Code plugin/skill (/open-code-review), I expected it could reuse Claude Code's existing authenticated session to make model calls — but based on the docs, the ocr CLI still makes its own independent request using llm.auth_token, completely separate from Claude Code's login state. This means Team/Pro plan users can't use this tool without also purchasing separate API credits.

### Proposed Solution

When open-code-review is run inside a Claude Code session (e.g. via the plugin/slash-command integration), allow it to delegate the actual review generation to Claude Code's own agent/model-call mechanism instead of requiring ocr to independently authenticate to api.anthropic.com with its own key. For example:

A mode where the Skill/Plugin instructs Claude Code itself to perform the diff analysis and produce review comments (using Claude Code's own tool-use loop), rather than ocr shelling out to a separately-configured LLM endpoint.
Or, at minimum, documentation clarifying whether/how Team or Pro plan users (without a separate API key) can use this tool.

### Alternatives Considered

Purchasing a separate Anthropic API key just for this tool — works, but means paying twice for the same underlying model access.
Writing my own custom Claude Code Skill that performs the review logic natively so it runs entirely on the Team plan's included usage — functional, but duplicates work that open-code-review already does well.

### Affected Area

Review Agent / LLM interaction

### Additional Context

It would be great if the README could explicitly state which integration modes (if any) work purely on a Claude Code subscription login vs. which strictly require a standalone API key with llm.auth_token. Right now this isn't obvious from the docs and could be a source of confusion for other Team/Pro plan users.
issues.triage_reason: Delegation Mode (`ocr delegate`, `/open-code-review:delegate-review`) already covers the request, so only a docs clarification is needed in plugins/open-code-review/README.md and README.md, with the four docs/i18n/README.*.md files synced. The bot can't edit pages/, and the wording needs some judgement.

issues.title: Feature request: richer review context — auto-include AGENTS.md + spec↔file mapping
issues.body:
## Context: we've integrated `ocr` into "devloop"

[devloop](https://github.com/qiankunli/devloop) is an agent plugin (Claude Code today) for an **aggregate-workspace dev loop** — a state bus + hard guards that drive `enter → develop → commit/MR → human merge`. We've wired **`ocr` in as a lifecycle hook**: when an MR is created, a background

```
ocr review --from origin/<target> --to HEAD --format json --repo <repo>
```

runs (fire-and-forget, doesn't block commit), and we post the result as an **MR comment** (so each MR accumulates a review history) plus surface it back to the agent session. `ocr` keeps its own LLM config; this has worked really well — thank you for the tool. 🙏

We're now focused on **review accuracy**, and the main lever is **giving `ocr` more context**. We already auto-pass `--background` (commit messages + MR title/description). Two further context sources would help a lot but need `ocr`-side support:

---

## 1. Auto-include the repo's `AGENTS.md` as review context

Many repos keep their conventions / architecture in an **`AGENTS.md`** (commonly at the repo root, or `server/AGENTS.md` / `backend/AGENTS.md`). These are exactly the "house rules" a reviewer must know: layering boundaries, mandatory timeouts/connection-pool config, SQL-dialect portability, naming, etc.

**Request:** if `ocr` detects an `AGENTS.md` in the repo (or the resolved code dir), automatically include its content as review context (alongside `--background` / rules), ideally with a sensible cap or summary.

Today we *can* stuff it into `--background`, but that's per-file and token-heavy, and not first-class. Native support — e.g. auto-detect `AGENTS.md`, or a config like `context_files` — would be cleaner and benefit everyone, not just our integration.

---

## 2. Spec-aware review via a spec ↔ file mapping

`ocr`'s pipeline today is `diff → changed files → per-file review`. A big accuracy win would be: for each changed file, also feed the **spec(s) that file implements**, so the review can ask *"does this change still satisfy the spec / requirement?"* — not only *"is this code locally OK?"*.

This needs two things:
1. **A spec format/ruleset** (requirements + scenarios, or a pointer to spec files).
2. **A declared spec ↔ file mapping** — which spec governs which files/paths — analogous to how `.opencodereview/rule.json` maps path globs → rules. For example a path-glob → spec-file(s) mapping, and `ocr` includes the matched specs as context for those files.

This would make `ocr` **requirement-aware**, a step beyond purely code-local review — and pairs naturally with spec-driven workflows.

---

Happy to discuss design and contribute a PR for either if you're open to it. Thanks again for `ocr`!

issues.title: feat(contracts): allow converting a contract between organization-level and project-level
issues.body:
## Problem

A workflow contract's level is fixed when the contract is created. It is either an organization-level contract or a project-level contract. You cannot convert an existing organization-level contract into a project-level contract, or a project-level contract into an organization-level contract.

Because organization-level contracts are reserved for organization admins, a token that is not an org admin fails with `you can not manage a global contract` (see `checkContractAccess` in `app/controlplane/internal/service/workflowcontract.go`). For example, the contract sync job in this repository (`.github/workflows/sync_contracts.yml`) fails because 5 of the 6 contracts in `.github/workflows/contracts/` are organization-level. The only fix today is to delete those contracts and create them again, which loses their revision history and their links to workflows.

## Proposal

Let users convert an existing contract between the two levels:

- **Organization-level → project-level**: convert an organization-level contract into a project-level contract.
- **Project-level → organization-level**: convert a project-level contract into an organization-level contract.

The contract keeps its name, revision history and workflow associations.

Out of scope: moving a project-level contract from one project to another.

## Authorization

- Only **organization admins** can convert a contract from organization-level to project-level.
- Only **organization admins** can convert a contract from project-level to organization-level.
- All checks go through `biz.AuthzUseCase`.

## Open questions

issues.title: Trace: record context window usage and compactions in AI coding session evidence
issues.body:
## Problem

The `CHAINLOOP_AI_CODING_SESSION` evidence does not record how full the model context window was during the session. `data.usage` has only session totals. The cache-read total adds the context of every turn, so it does not show the context size.

Today, a consumer must walk `raw_session.*[].message.usage` and add `input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens` for each turn. The evidence does not record the window size, so the consumer cannot calculate a percentage. For example, the model ID `claude-opus-5-5` does not show whether the session used a 200K or a 1M window.

Example session (`sha256:3a0250e44d4b4a2ca0744c5203e8707f4c668b38c5941f5275cbbf0fb5239fd5`): the main transcript peaks at 134,778 tokens and the Explore subagent at 60,594 tokens. That is about 67% of a 200K window or 13% of a 1M window. The evidence cannot tell which one is correct.

## Proposal

Investigate how each Trace provider (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi, Codex) can supply this data. Then add it to the evidence schema:

- `context_window_tokens`: the window size that the agent used.
- `context_peak_tokens` and `context_peak_pct`: the largest context of a turn in the session.
- `context_final_tokens` and `context_final_pct`: the context of the last turn.
- `compaction_count`: the number of times the agent compacted the context. If possible, record the turn of each compaction.
- The same fields for each subagent.

## Why

With these fields, policies can do these checks without a walk of the raw transcript:

- Warn when a session ends above a context threshold, for example 80%.
- Warn when a session makes a large change (`ai_lines_added` above a limit) after a compaction.

The AI Session Score can also use the fields as a signal for context quality.

## Related observation

In the same session, `git_context.commit_start` and `commit_end` are both `76c8c508`, the commit that the session made. `commit_start` is probably the parent commit. Examine this at the same time.

🤖 _Posted by Maximus bot (Claude Code) on behalf of @migmartri_
issues.triage_reason: Large, multi-provider schema extension in pkg/attestation/crafter/materials/aicodingsession/aicodingsession.go and the app/cli/internal/trace providers. Window size isn't derivable from transcripts, and field design and the commit_start question need maintainer decisions.

Not done: window size and percentages, the turn of each compaction, other providers (Cursor, OpenCode, Pi, Codex), and the git_context.commit_start question.
issues.feedback:
Attempt 1:
Reviewer rejected (the test must be rewritten):
- The patch only adds struct fields to `Usage` in aicodingsession.go. Nothing computes or fills them. No provider (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi, Codex) records the window size, per-turn peak or final context, or compaction count, so the evidence will never contain these values. The issue asks for the data to be recorded, so this hides the symptom.
- The issue asks for the same fields on each subagent and, if possible, the turn of each compaction. Neither is implemented. The `git_context.commit_start` question is not examined either.
- Add provider parsing that derives these values from the transcripts: the per-turn context sum, the window size, and compaction detection. Add unit tests that feed transcript fixtures through that parsing.
- The regression test only unmarshals JSON that already contains the fields and marshals it back. It would pass for any struct with matching tags and does not exercise the reported behaviour. Its unused `path` field is dead code. It should be replaced with tests of the computation from transcripts.
- Update the trace documentation in `app/cli/internal/trace/README.md` and the evidence schema or docs if they list the fields.

issues.title: Migrate the generated TypeScript bindings from ts-proto to protobuf-es v2
issues.body:
## Summary

Migrate the generated TypeScript bindings of the control plane API from ts-proto to [protobuf-es v2](https://github.com/bufbuild/protobuf-es) (`@bufbuild/protobuf` v2). Use [Connect-ES v2](https://github.com/connectrpc/connect-es) (`@connectrpc/connect` v2) for the clients.

## Current state

`app/controlplane/api/buf.gen.yaml` generates the TypeScript bindings with ts-proto:

```yaml
- remote: buf.build/community/stephenh-ts-proto:v1.151.1
  out: ./gen/frontend
  opt:
    - outputClientImpl=grpc-web
    - esModuleInterop=true
    - useOptionals=messages
```

- The output goes to `app/controlplane/api/gen/frontend`.
- The output contains the control plane, attestation, workflow contract, `errors` and `jsonfilter` protos.
- The output also contains third-party imported protos. Examples: `protoc-gen-openapiv2/options/annotations.ts`, `protoc-gen-openapiv2/options/openapiv2.ts`, `buf/validate/...` and `google/api/...`.
- The generated code depends on `@improbable-eng/grpc-web`, `browser-headers` and `protobufjs/minimal`.

This is the only `buf.gen.yaml` in the repository that emits TypeScript. The other files (`app/artifact-cas/api`, `pkg/attestation/crafter/api`, `pkg/credentials/api`, the plugin SDK and the `conf` packages) emit Go only. So the scope is this one file and its output folder.

## Motivation

- ts-proto with the improbable-eng grpc-web transport is in maintenance mode.
- protobuf-es v2 and Connect-ES v2 are the stack that Buf maintains. They have a smaller runtime, first-class ESM and TypeScript support, and they pass the Protobuf conformance tests.
- Some downstream consumers already generate their own protos with protobuf-es v2 into the same source tree. Today they get two different generated files for the same imported proto. For example, `protoc-gen-openapiv2/options/annotations.ts` from ts-proto sits next to `annotations_pb.ts` from protobuf-es. The consumers must filter files out when they sync the bindings. One generator for all bindings removes this problem.

## Proposed implementation

### 1. Replace the generator plugin

protobuf-es v2 also generates the service descriptors. A separate connect-es plugin is not necessary.

```yaml
- remote: buf.build/bufbuild/es:v2.16.0
  out: ./gen/frontend
  opt: target=ts
  include_imports: true
```

`include_imports: true` generates the imported dependencies (openapiv2 options, `buf/validate`, `google/api`) as `*_pb.ts` files. Consumers then get a self-contained set of files.

### 2. Changes in the generated code

- File names change to `<name>_pb.ts`.
- Messages are plain types. Create them with `create(FooSchema, {...})`.
- Serialize with `toBinary`, `fromBinary`, `toJson` and `fromJson` from `@bufbuild/protobuf`.
- Enums are TypeScript enums.
- Oneofs use the `{ case, value }` form.
- Use `@bufbuild/protobuf/wkt` for `Timestamp` (`timestampDate`, `timestampFromDate`).

### 3. Clients

- Create clients with `createClient(Service, transport)` from `@connectrpc/connect` v2.
- Use `createGrpcWebTransport` from `@connectrpc/connect-web` v2. The transport stays gRPC-web, so the server needs no change.
- Remove the `@improbable-eng/grpc-web`, `browser-headers` and `protobufjs` dependencies.

```ts
import { createClient } from "@connectrpc/connect";
import { createGrpcWebTransport } from "@connectrpc/connect-web";
import { WorkflowService } from "./controlplane/v1/workflow_pb";

const transport = createGrpcWebTransport({ baseUrl: "https://cp.example.com" });
const client = createClient(WorkflowService, transport);
```

### 4. Transition

- This is a breaking change for every consumer of `gen/frontend`.
- If a transition period is necessary, emit the protobuf-es output to a new folder first (for example `gen/frontend-es`). Keep the ts-proto output in `gen/frontend` until the consumers migrate. Then remove the ts-proto plugin.

### 5. Regeneration and CI

- Run `make api` from the repository root (it runs `buf generate` in `app/controlplane/api`) and commit the new output.
- Remove the old ts-proto files from the output folder. `buf generate` does not delete stale files.
- The `test.yml` workflow runs `make api` and fails if the tree is dirty. The regenerated files must be in the same pull request.

## Acceptance criteria

- `app/controlplane/api/buf.gen.yaml` uses `buf.build/bufbuild/es` v2 with `target=ts` and `include_imports: true`.
- The generated output has no imports of `@improbable-eng/grpc-web`, `browser-headers` or `protobufjs`.
- The generated output contains the imported third-party protos as `*_pb.ts` files.
- `make api` produces no diff in CI.
- The release notes state the breaking change for consumers of `gen/frontend`.

issues.title: Add Pacto and Pacto Evidence material types
issues.body:
Hola Chainloop team!

I'd like to propose adding two native material types for [Pacto](https://pacto.run/):

* `PACTO` — Pacto contracts
* `PACTO_EVIDENCE` — runtime [evidence](https://pacto.run/latest/evidence-protocol/) produced by Pacto

### What is Pacto?

[Pacto](https://pacto.run/) is an open-source contract system for cloud-native services. A Pacto contract is a machine-readable description of what a service is supposed to look like: ownership, interfaces, dependencies, configuration, workload, capabilities, etc. Contracts are versioned and distributed as OCI artifacts. For example:

```yaml
pactoVersion: "2.0"

service:
  name: payments
  version: 2.3.0
  owner:
    team: payments

interfaces:
  - name: api
    type: openapi
    ref: interfaces/openapi.yaml
```

The [contract documentation](https://pacto.run/latest/contract-reference/sections/) has the full model.

### The interesting part: runtime evidence

Pacto is not only about declaring the contract. Collectors observe the actual runtime and produce a common `EvidenceSet`. The Pacto evaluator then compares:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    C[Pacto Contract] --> E[Pacto Evaluator]
    X[Runtime] --> K[Pacto Collector]
    K --> ES[EvidenceSet]
    ES --> E
    E --> F[Findings]
```

The important bit for this proposal is that Pacto can now persist that evidence as a **content-addressed OCI artifact**  (see [evidence OCI storage](https://pacto.run/latest/evidence-oci-storage/) and [collectors](https://pacto.run/latest/collectors/) for the details). So we now have two different OCI artifacts:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    C[Pacto Contract] --> O1[OCI Artifact]
    E[Pacto Evidence] --> O2[OCI Artifact]
```

### Why Chainloop?

This looks like a natural fit for Chainloop's material model. A release could contain:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    R[Release] --> I[Container Image]
    R --> S[SBOM]
    R --> P[Provenance]
    R --> C[PACTO]
    R --> E[PACTO_EVIDENCE]
```

This gives Chainloop a way to connect the usual software supply-chain artifacts with runtime information about the service. For example, a `PACTO_EVIDENCE` artifact can reference the exact Pacto contract it was collected against by digest. This makes it possible to establish:

> this runtime evidence was collected for this exact contract.

And Chainloop can then apply its own policies to the attestation, for example:

* a production release must contain a Pacto contract;
* it must contain Pacto runtime evidence;
* the evidence must reference the same contract digest;
* the evidence must not be stale.

Those are Chainloop-level policies. Pacto remains responsible for interpreting the contract and evidence and producing its own findings.

### Proposed material types

I think the initial implementation could be quite small:

**`PACTO`**

Accept a Pacto OCI artifact and expose basic metadata such as:

* service name/version
* owner
* Pacto version
* digest

**`PACTO_EVIDENCE`**

Accept a Pacto Evidence OCI artifact and expose:

* subject/service
* contract digest
* collector/source
* observation timestamp
* evidence digest

The underlying artifacts should remain content-addressed and be handled through Chainloop's existing material/CAS mechanisms.

The existing generic `EVIDENCE` material type could technically be used for this, but I think [Pacto](https://pacto.run/) is a good candidate for a native type because both the contract and evidence have a defined format and semantics, and the relationship between the two is important.

### References

* [Pacto](https://pacto.run/)
* [Pacto architecture](https://pacto.run/latest/architecture/)
* [Pacto collectors](https://pacto.run/latest/collectors/)
* [Pacto Evidence OCI storage](https://pacto.run/latest/evidence-oci-storage/)
* [Chainloop material types](https://docs.chainloop.dev/concepts/material-types)
* [Chainloop policies](https://docs.chainloop.dev/concepts/policies)

Happy to contribute the Pacto side and work with the Chainloop team on the material type implementation.

issues.title: Pagination support everywhere it's applicable
issues.body:
Particularly in light of configurable limits to server-side memory-usin' things (#1471), we need to make sure that clients can still retrieve all the data they need.

For example, log retrieval already supports `tail`, which is adequate in all but the most pathological cases (e.g. a multi-MiB log line) as a client bouncing off a size limit can repeat the request with a smaller `tail`.

For counterexample, today `resources_list` has no mode to retrieve less than "everything" (in a namespace, if applicable). If "everything" is bigger than a configured cap, the call fails, and there's no recourse.

KAS `List()` calls already support pagination (`Limit`, `Continue`) and the MCP spec already knows how to use it. Plumb it in, e.g. by exposing `Limit`/`Continue` as tool call params.

issues.title: Fix awkward enabled_tools/disabled_tools semantics
issues.body:
Today, `enabled_tools` implicitly denies all tools except those listed. That's cool if all tools are enabled by default; but in some cases, as in #1442, tools are filtered out by default for other reasons. This means that, if I want to enable all tools *including* a by-default-disabled one, I have to *list all tools explicitly* in `enabled_tools`. This is impractical and ugly, and also means I have to manually update that list e.g. if new tools are added on upgrade.

Today, `disabled_tools` removes the listed tools from the rendered list after `enabled_tools` is applied. Practically, this just means that, if a tool is listed in both places, `disabled` wins. Do we really need to support the scenario where the same tool is listed in both places? What harm in treating that as a config error? (Perhaps it has to do with use cases that load multiple configs...?)

**Ideas:**
- **Wildcarding**
 
At its simplest, `enabled_tools` accepts an entry spelled `"*"` which inverts the default behavior. So `enabled_tools = ["*", "configuration_view"]` would satisfy the above scenario. Except one could be forgiven for assuming `"*"` means "everything including otherwise-disabled things -- so maybe it's spelled `"<default>"` instead?

Or maybe we invert the default behavior of `enabled_tools`, and to get the current behavior you would do something like:
```toml
disabled_tools = ["*"]
enabled_tools = ["...", "..."] # these are the *only* tools enabled
```
...and then you can do the "default plus normally-disabled" thing with simply
```toml
enabled_tools = ["configuration_view"]  # Because no disabled_tools, this gets defaults *plus* configuration_view
```

Note that this last is breaking, so we would want to do it on a major release boundary.

- **A new knob**

...like:
```toml
enabled_normally_disabled_tools = ["configuration_view"]  # yeah, the key name needs work :)
```

- **Your idea here**
issues.triage_reason: The issue offers several mutually exclusive designs (wildcard, inverted semantics that break compatibility, or a new key) and leaves the choice open. The code is in pkg/config/config.go and pkg/mcp/mcp.go, but the semantics need a maintainer decision first.

issues.title: Add a test to catch tools that forget to declare RBAC metadata
issues.body:
Follow-up from #1407, which added the `io.kubernetes-mcp-server/rbac` metadata to tools (starting with the `core` toolset). Other toolsets will get this metadata in follow-up PRs.

**The gap:** right now, if a tool doesn't set `RBAC`, nothing fails — it just silently ships without RBAC metadata. There's no way to tell "nobody added this yet" apart from "this tool intentionally needs no RBAC."

**Proposal:** once all toolsets have RBAC metadata, add a test (e.g. `TestAllToolsHaveRBACMetadata`) that loops through every registered tool and fails if any of them have `RBAC == nil`. This way, if someone adds a new tool later and forgets to set RBAC, CI catches it instead of it slipping through review.

cc @Cali0707
issues.triage_reason: RBAC metadata now appears across all toolsets under pkg/toolsets; a small suite test (e.g. in pkg/toolsets or pkg/mcp) can iterate registered toolsets' GetTools and assert RBAC != nil. Some judgement is needed for the ToolsetContext and for any tools still missing RBAC.
issues.summary: Added TestAllToolsHaveRBACMetadata in pkg/mcp/toolsets_test.go, which fails if any registered tool has RBAC == nil. Placed in pkg/mcp because it imports all toolsets; currently passes for all 77 tools.
issues.pr_title: test(mcp): fail when a tool has no RBAC metadata
issues.pr_body:
Fixes #1435

Adds `TestAllToolsHaveRBACMetadata` in `pkg/mcp/toolsets_test.go`. It goes through every tool of every registered toolset and fails if a tool has `RBAC == nil`. A new tool that forgets to declare RBAC metadata will now fail CI.

The test is in `pkg/mcp` because that package imports all toolsets. Each tool runs as its own subtest named `<toolset>/<tool>`, so a failure shows which tool is missing the metadata.

## Testing

- `TestAllToolsHaveRBACMetadata` passes for all 77 registered tools.
- The project checks pass.
issues.repro_notes: All registered tools already declare RBAC metadata, so the proposed TestAllToolsHaveRBACMetadata passes. The issue is a guard test, not a reproducible bug. No changes made.

issues.title: docs(configuration): fix default toolsets contradiction and document missing proxy and OAuth CLI options
issues.body:
### Problem Description

While reviewing the documentation in [`docs/configuration.md`](https://github.com/containers/kubernetes-mcp-server/blob/main/docs/configuration.md) and cross-referencing it with the code implementation in `pkg/config/` and `pkg/kubernetes-mcp-server/cmd/root.go`, I identified three discrepancies and omissions:

---

### Identified Issues

#### 1. Contradiction in Default `toolsets`
- In `docs/configuration.md` (line 347), the Toolsets configuration field table states:
  > `| toolsets | string[] | ["core", "config", "helm"] | List of toolsets to enable. |`
  This indicates that `helm` is enabled by default.
- However, in the "Available Toolsets" table immediately below (lines 353–363), `helm` is **not** marked with a checkmark (`✓`) as default.
- Looking at the source code in [`pkg/config/config_default.go:17`](https://github.com/containers/kubernetes-mcp-server/blob/main/pkg/config/config_default.go#L17):
  ```go
  Toolsets: []string{"core", "config"},
  ```
  The upstream base default only enables `core` and `config`. Line 347 should be corrected to `["core", "config"]` to eliminate the contradiction.

#### 2. Undocumented `trust_proxy_headers` Configuration
- The codebase defines the `TrustProxyHeaders` configuration option in [`pkg/config/config.go:131`](https://github.com/containers/kubernetes-mcp-server/blob/main/pkg/config/config.go#L131) and implements reverse proxy header forwarding (`X-Forwarded-*`, `X-Real-IP`).
- This option is essential for running the MCP server in production behind reverse proxies (Ingress, Nginx, Traefik, OpenShift Router, AWS ALB, etc.), but it is currently completely absent from the configuration reference table in `docs/configuration.md`.

#### 3. Missing OAuth CLI Flags in "CLI Configuration Options" Table
- The command-line flags in [`pkg/kubernetes-mcp-server/cmd/root.go`](https://github.com/containers/kubernetes-mcp-server/blob/main/pkg/kubernetes-mcp-server/cmd/root.go) implement several OAuth-related flags that appear in `--help`:
  - `--require-oauth`
  - `--oauth-audience`
  - `--authorization-url`
  - `--skip-jwt-verification`
  - `--server-url`
  - `--certificate-authority`
- However, none of these flags are listed in the "CLI Configuration Options" reference table at the bottom of `docs/configuration.md`.

---

### Proposed Solution

Update `docs/configuration.md` to:
- Correct the default value of `toolsets` on line 347 to `["core", "config"]`.
- Document `trust_proxy_headers` in the HTTP / Security configuration section with a clear explanation of its purpose when running behind a reverse proxy.
- Add the missing OAuth flags (`--require-oauth`, `--oauth-audience`, `--authorization-url`, `--skip-jwt-verification`, `--server-url`, `--certificate-authority`) to the "CLI Configuration Options" reference table.

I would be happy to submit a pull request addressing these documentation improvements.

issues.title: llminternal: a live connection that drops while a tool runs ends the session or loses the tool response
issues.triage_reason: The unclassified tool-response write in RunLive (internal/llminternal/base_flow.go ~L703) can be routed through isResumable and re-sent after reconnect. The issue itself asks maintainers to pick between sender-goroutine routing and re-send, and to decide how to handle duplicates, so it is a live-flow design call rather than a clear small fix.
issues.skip_reason:
gave up after 3 attempts; last: Reviewer rejected (the test must be rewritten):
- The attempt-2 objection about clearing `unanswered` is still open. `sawAnswer` is set by any event with non-nil Content and no function calls after the response is written. In-flight output from the turn that was already running (an audio chunk, then `turnComplete`) therefore sets `sawAnswer` and then clears `unanswered` before the model has seen the response. A drop after that loses the response, which is the bug in the issue. The code comment says the output 'began after the response was written', but the code cannot know that, so the comment is not true of the code. Clear only on a signal that shows the model processed the response, or document and test why this heuristic is safe. There is no test with in-flight content and `turnComplete` after the response write.
- No test covers a failing resend write. The attempt-2 feedback asked for one explicitly, so the resend goroutine's `report(err)` path is untested.
- There is no test for parallel or multiple function responses in one turn, even though `unanswered` is now a slice. There is also no test for the TCP-reset case where the resend fails.
- The new tests are timing-dependent: `time.Sleep(100ms)` on conn 2, a 300ms read deadline on conn 3, and a 50ms sleep to force the drop. `TestRunLive_AnsweredToolResponseNotResent` relies on conn 2 dropping implicitly when its handler returns, which is fragile. The tests also do not show that conn 3's resend check actually ran.
issues.feedback:
Attempt 1:
Reviewer rejected:
- unansweredResponse is cleared on any event with non-nil Content. This includes model output that was already in flight before the model saw the tool response, such as streaming audio or text from the same turn. In that case the response is dropped and never resent after a drop, which is the bug in the issue. It should be cleared only when the model has actually responded to the function response, or the clearing rule should be explained and tested.
- Only the last function response is retained (`unansweredResponse = respEv...` is overwritten). If an earlier response in the same turn or in parallel calls was written and then lost in a drop, it is never resent. The model's call is left unanswered, which the issue says must not happen.
- The write error from SendContent is now silently discarded (`_ =`). The patch relies on the reader goroutine to surface the failure. If the write fails and the reader does not report an error, for example after a context cancel or a non-resumable write error, the session continues with the response lost and nothing reported. The error should be routed to errChan, which is the first fix the issue suggests, so isResumable classifies it in one place.
- The regression test covers only a hard close and a 1008 close frame. It does not cover the TCP reset (SetLinger(0)) case, where the write fails with 'broken pipe' and the session ended before the fix. It also has no test that the response is not resent after the model answers, or that parallel calls are handled. The duplicate-send tradeoff on resume, which the issue asks a maintainer to decide, is not tested.

Attempt 2:
Reviewer rejected (the test must be rewritten):
- Clearing `unanswered` on any `TurnComplete` repeats the earlier objection in a narrower form. A `turnComplete` for output that was already in flight when the function response was written clears the response before the model has seen it. A drop after that loses the response, which is the bug in the issue. Clear only on an event that shows the model processed the response, or document and test why `TurnComplete` is a safe signal.
- TestRunLive_DropWhileToolRunsResendsEveryResponse does not prove that a response is not resent after the model finishes its turn. It never asserts that a third connection was dialed. If connection 3 never happens, the `t.Errorf("function response sent again...")` check is never reached and the test passes without checking anything. Assert that connection 3 was reached, and that the reads in the connection 3 handler actually ran.
- That test is timing-dependent and weak. It uses a fixed `time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)`, and a 50ms sleep to force the second drop. `pongs` is counted but never asserted. It calls `t.Errorf` from the server handler goroutine, which can run after the test finishes. The duplicate-send tradeoff on resume, which the issue asks a maintainer to decide, is not tested: nothing checks that a response which already reached the server is sent a second time.
- The resend loop after a reconnect and the new write-error goroutines both report through `errChan` with a hand-copied `go func(){select{...}}()` block, duplicated twice. They also sit before the reader goroutine starts. Unify them in one small helper, and add a test where the resend write itself fails, so that path is exercised and not only reasoned about.
issues.summary: Route tool-response write errors through errChan (shared report helper) so isResumable classifies them, and keep unanswered function responses across connections, resending them after reconnect until the model answers; added tests for no-resend-after-answer and resend-of-unanswered. No test yet for a failing resend write or for in-flight output before the response.
issues.repro_notes: Drop while a tool is running: hard close -> function response never sent on conn 2; TCP reset -> session ends with 'failed to send tool response: ... broken pipe'; close 1008 -> ends with 'failed to send tool response: websocket: close sent'. All three subtests fail on current code.

issues.title: Port planners (BuiltInPlanner, PlanReActPlanner) from adk-python
issues.body:
adk-python has `planners/` (`BasePlanner`, `BuiltInPlanner`, `PlanReActPlanner`) and runs them from `flows/llm_flows/extensions/_planning.py`. In adk-go, `nlPlanningRequestProcessor` and `nlPlanningResponseProcessor` in `internal/llminternal/other_processors.go` are still TODO stubs.

#318 tried this on the pre-v2 tree. Before anyone writes a new version, maintainers need to decide wether adk-go wants a public `planner` package, and what the names are (`Planner` or `BasePlanner`, `PlanReActPlanner` or `ReActPlanner`).

I checked #318 against adk-python 2.11.0. A port needs to match Python on these points, which #318 did not:

- Keep every leading parallel function call. Python uses `first_fc_part_index >= 0` and tests it in `test_preserves_all_leading_parallel_function_calls`.
- Run `build_planning_instruction` and clear thoughts for every planner except `BuiltInPlanner`, so user-defined planners work.
- Persist state a planner writes in `process_planning_response`. Python yields a state-update event when `callback_context.state.has_delta()`.
- Strip the ReAct tags from the text it keeps,and still mark bare-tag parts as thoughts (`_strip_planning_tags`).
- Copy `ThinkingConfig` per request instead of sharing the planner's pointer, so a `BeforeModelCallback` cannot race on it.

The port also needs flow-level tests like `tests/unittests/flows/llm_flows/extensions/test_planning.py`, since the tests in #318 all passed with both processors stubbed out. One behavior also needs a decision. A plan-only ReAct reply is all thought parts, and main's `Flow.Run` calls the model agian on thought-only turns, up to 10 times. Python makes one call.
issues.triage_reason: Adding a public planner package and filling the nlPlanning processor stubs in internal/llminternal/other_processors.go is a large API-shaping feature. The issue itself says maintainers must first decide the package, the type names and the thought-only retry behavior in Flow.Run.

issues.title: No way to reserve runway before a hard deadline and finish with a partial answer
issues.body:
## Problem

An invocation runs inside whatever deadline the caller's context carries. In a served deployment that is usually an expiring credential, a proxy timeout, or a platform request limit, and it is measured in minutes rather than seconds.

When that deadline passes mid-invocation, the run ends in `context.DeadlineExceeded`. Everything the agent established up to that point is discarded, and the caller receives a transport error rather than a partial answer. An agent that has completed most of a multi-step task and has ten seconds left behaves exactly like one that has just started: it begins another tool call, and that call is what kills the request.

The framework has no notion of a time budget. It does not know that the last stretch of an invocation needs to be reserved for the model to write an answer, it will start a tool call it cannot finish, and it offers no way to end an invocation deliberately with what has been gathered so far.

The result an operator wants is the ordinary one for any system under a deadline: stop taking on new work in time, wind down what is running, and spend the remainder producing something useful. A partial answer that names what was completed and what was not is worth far more to a user than an error, and today every adopter has to build that themselves.

## Current state

Most of this is reachable from the public API today, so this is unstandardized rather than blocked. `ctx.Deadline()` is readable on tool and callback contexts, `BeforeToolCallback` can refuse a call, and `BeforeModelCallback` can alter the request that produces the final turn.

Bounding a tool call that is already running is the part not reachable from a plugin callback, because the framework calls `tool.Run`, not the callback. Doing it today means wrapping the tool, which runs into #1594 and #1595.

## Constraints any solution meets

These are properties of the framework and of Go, not requirements on a particular design. They are listed because each one is cheap to discover late and expensive to discover in production.

A deadline is present only when the caller supplies one. Nothing in the framework injects a deadline, so behavior when the context carries none has to be decided rather than assumed.

Bounding a tool by shortening its context changes what every nested reader of the remaining time sees. A guard nested inside a bounded call measures against the shortened value rather than the real deadline, and will act earlier than intended unless the real deadline is carried alongside.

A goroutine cannot be cancelled from outside in Go. A tool that does not observe its context cannot be stopped, only abandoned, and abandoning it leaks whatever it holds until it returns on its own.

Removing the tools a model can see is not the same as clearing the dispatch registry. [`LLMRequest.Config.Tools`](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/b21b83f2faa71e2794b0966eec05c0365717fe31/model/llm.go#L32-L38) carries the declarations sent to the model, while `LLMRequest.Tools` is the map used to resolve a call back to a Go value and is marked `json:"-"`. Emptying the second hides nothing from the model and turns a function call that still arrives into a `tool not found` response, in the exact turn that was meant to produce a clean summary.

## Acceptance criteria

- An invocation that would otherwise exceed its deadline ends with a model-authored response that states what was completed and what was not, instead of a transport error.
- A tool call that cannot finish within the remaining time is not started.
- A tool call already running when the budget is exhausted stops consuming the reserve, and the model is told that it was cut short rather than that it failed.
- Behavior is defined when the context carries no deadline.

## Environment

- ADK version: `main` at [b21b83f](https://github.com/google/adk-go/commit/b21b83f2faa71e2794b0966eec05c0365717fe31)
- Go: 1.26.5
issues.triage_reason: Large, design-open feature (deadline budget plugin/config touching runner, tool execution and LLMRequest.Config.Tools); needs maintainer decisions on API shape, no-deadline behavior, and depends on issues #1594/#1595.

issues.title: auth/gcp: a UserID contained in the ContinueURI leaves most of the URI in error text
issues.body:
The error-body scrub in `auth/gcp` removes the request's own `UserID` and `ContinueURI` from service error text before that text is quoted into an error. Where the `UserID` is a substring of the `ContinueURI` and the service echoes the URI with `\/` escapes, the scrub cannot match the URI at all, matches the short `UserID` inside it, and writes `[redacted]` into the middle of the URI. What comes back shows 31 of the URI's 34 characters, so the redirect URI is effectively disclosed. This is on the error-redaction path added in #1520 and is not present on `main`.
Reproduction — go test -run TestContinueURISurvivesTheUserIDMarker ./auth/gcp/ ```go func TestContinueURISurvivesTheUserIDMarker(t *testing.T) { srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) { w.WriteHeader(http.StatusForbidden) _, _ = io.WriteString(w, `error at https:\/\/my-app.test\/oauth\/callback`) })) defer srv.Close() _, err := newTestClient(t, srv).RetrieveCredential(t.Context(), Request{ Resource: authProviderResource, UserID: "app", ContinueURI: "https://my-app.test/oauth/callback", }) t.Logf("%v", err) } ```
It logs: ``` gcp: credentials service returned status 403: "error at https:\\/\\/my-[redacted].test\\/oauth\\/callback" (resource "projects/p/locations/l/authProviders/ap") ``` A `UserID` of `alice` with a `ContinueURI` of `https://cb.test/u/alice/done` behaves the same way. The acting user itself is redacted correctly in every shape tried, so what escapes is the redirect URI. Two properties of the current code constrain any solution. - `recoverable` splits the text on the literal marker at [redact.go:183](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/09e55ec3bd44585dd0844c2093d6ab77f58870c0/auth/gcp/redact.go#L183) before decoding it, so a value that spans the marker is examined as two halves and neither half matches. Dropping the split is not free: the marker is text this package inserted rather than anything the service disclosed, and treating it as disclosed would report a secret in text that carries none. - The doc comment at [redact.go:393-399](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/09e55ec3bd44585dd0844c2093d6ab77f58870c0/auth/gcp/redact.go#L393-L399) says overlapping candidates are resolved earliest-first then longest, "which is what keeps a ContinueURI carrying the user id from being split by the user id". That holds for the unescaped spelling. The escaped URI never becomes a candidate, so the resolution has nothing to order, and the comment reads as covering a case it does not reach. The letter of the documented contract is not broken. It promises that no secret is recoverable from the returned string by this package's decoder, and the decoder does not reconstruct the URI from that text. A person reading the error does. A fix should demonstrate that the URI is not left partially visible when the `UserID` is a substring of it, in the escaped and unescaped spellings alike, and that a body naming only the `UserID` still comes back with the `UserID` redacted rather than withheld entirely.
issues.triage_reason: The fix is in auth/gcp/redact.go (redactedForError/recoverable/redactLowered). The logic is intricate and heavily constrained: the marker split, fuzz and reference tests, and a documented known limitation tied to #1539. Choosing a design (withhold, or match the escaped URI) takes maintainer-level judgement.
issues.feedback:
Attempt 1:
Reviewer rejected:
- Fix only handles the literal `\/` escape via withEscapedSlashes; other escapings of the ContinueURI (e.g. \u002f, partially escaped slashes) still leave the UserID marker splitting the URI and exposing most of it, so the reported problem is only partly fixed
- Doc comment on overlap resolution and the remaining escaped-spelling remarks still imply a general guarantee the code does not provide
- Regression test only probes a few hard-coded fragments and only the `\/` spelling; it does not assert the whole URI is gone, and the UserID-only-body case is tested only in a separate redact_slash_test.go, duplicating coverage
- No evidence each new branch (case-insensitive containment, w != v guard) is pinned by a test that fails when removed

Attempt 2:
Reviewer rejected (the test must be rewritten):
- When the UserID is a substring of the ContinueURI, redactedForError now scrubs and returns the fully decoded text instead of the original body. A body that merely contains `\u0041` or `\/` comes back decoded, so the error text changes for existing users. If any part of the body does not decode, the whole body is withheld, even when it names only the UserID or has no secret at all. A narrower fix would find the escaped URI itself, or scrub it as a unit, and leave the rest of the body in its original spelling. The change needs to state this behaviour change and keep it as small as it can.
- The new comment in truncated/overlap docs says the escaped spelling 'is never a candidate; redactedForError decodes the text first when one secret contains another'. This holds only for spellings the package decoder handles. A partly decodable body is withheld wholesale, and the comment does not say so.
- The regression test in client_test.go is weak. It checks a few hard-coded fragments such as 'my-', 'done' and 'cb.test' instead of asserting that the whole URI is absent from the error. The UserID leak check (`userID+"\\/"` or `/userID/`) is a narrow pattern, so it would miss most leaks. It does not cover other escapings such as `\u002f`. It also does not check, through RetrieveCredential, that a body naming only the UserID comes back redacted rather than withheld.
- The extra file redact_slash_test.go duplicates the coverage of the regression test and sits in a separate file, apart from the existing tests. The UserID-only-body case belongs in the same regression test as the URI cases. Nothing shows that the containsAnother case-insensitivity or its `i != j` guard is pinned by a test that fails when removed. The `TestRedactedForErrorUserIDCaseDiffersFromContinueURI` test only uses `cb` as its leak marker.
issues.summary: When a UserID is a substring of the ContinueURI and the service echoes the URI in an escaped spelling the scrub can't match, redactedForError now withholds the response (new splitsContainer check) instead of leaving most of the URI visible around a [redacted] marker. UserID-only and unescaped bodies are still scrubbed and shown. Updated the doc comment and added a test that fails with the change reverted.
issues.pr_title: fix(auth/gcp): withhold error text that splits an escaped ContinueURI
issues.pr_body:
**Please ensure you have read the [contribution guide](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) before creating a pull request.**

### Linked issue

- Closes: #1539

Fixes #1539

**Problem:**
The error-body scrub in `auth/gcp` removes the request's `UserID` and `ContinueURI` from service error text. When the `UserID` is a substring of the `ContinueURI` and the service echoes the URI with escapes such as `\/`, the scrub cannot match the whole URI. It matches the short `UserID` inside it and writes `[redacted]` in the middle. A reader sees most of the redirect URI. For example, `https://my-app.test/oauth/callback` with `UserID` `app` came back as `https:\/\/my-[redacted].test\/oauth\/callback`.

**Solution:**

issues.title: telemetry: ToolUsePromptTokenCount is never recorded, so input_tokens under-reports tool-use calls
issues.body:
### What happens

`UsageMetadata.ToolUsePromptTokenCount` is never read by `internal/telemetry`. Two consequences on every `generate_content` span for a call that used a server-side tool (Google Search grounding, Maps, code execution):

1. **`gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` under-reports.** It is set to `PromptTokenCount` alone:

   https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/f322a15/internal/telemetry/telemetry.go#L136

   Gemini reports tool-use prompt tokens *separately* from `PromptTokenCount` rather than folding them in, and they are billed at the input rate. The semantic-conventions reference implementation for google-genai adds the two together for exactly this reason:

   ```python
   # Tool-use tokens are reported separately from prompt_token_count, so add
   # them to get the total input token count.
   tool_use_tokens = getattr(um, "tool_use_prompt_token_count", None) or 0
   if um.prompt_token_count:
       attrs["gen_ai.usage.input_tokens"] = um.prompt_token_count + tool_use_tokens
   ```

   — [reference/scenarios/google-genai/scenario.py](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/main/reference/scenarios/google-genai/scenario.py)

   Note the contrast with `CachedContentTokenCount`, which *is* already inside `PromptTokenCount` (the same reference notes "prompt_token_count already includes cached content"). So cache-read tokens are correctly reported as a subset today, while tool-use tokens are simply missing from the total.

2. **The breakdown is unrecoverable.** There is no attribute carrying `ToolUsePromptTokenCount`, so a consumer cannot separate grounding-driven input from ordinary prompt input. `cache_read.input_tokens` and `reasoning.output_tokens` both report their share of their respective totals; tool-use has no equivalent.

### Why it matters

Server-side tool use is a significant and highly variable share of spend on grounded calls. With the total short and no breakdown, per-call cost derived from ADK spans is both wrong and un-debuggable — you cannot tell a cheap call from an expensive grounded one, or reconcile a span against a billing line.

### Impact

Only calls that use a server-side tool are affected. Everything else reports `ToolUsePromptTokenCount == 0` and is unchanged.

### Proposed fix

- `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` = `PromptTokenCount + ToolUsePromptTokenCount`, matching the reference implementation.
- Add `gen_ai.usage.tool_use_prompt_tokens` so the share stays recoverable.

The attribute has no semantic-conventions registry entry yet, so the name is open to discussion — a `gcp.vertex.*` namespace would also be reasonable while it is unregistered, and I am happy to rename.

Out of scope: `recordUsage` in `internal/telemetry/compaction.go` sets `input_tokens` from `PromptTokenCount` the same way, but compaction is a tool-free summarization call, so it reports zero in practice and I left it alone.

### Environment

`main` at `f322a15`. Verified against `google.golang.org/adk/v2 v2.3.0` in production as well.

I have a PR ready for this.
