issues.title: mcp: a resource update cannot be delivered to one session, and the caller's context never reaches the sending middleware
issues.body:
I found this auditing my MCP server against the specification. Every line number below is from `main` at 5bc078a, and I checked each one against that tree.

### What the protocol scopes to one subscriber

On 2025-06-18 a subscription is a relationship between one client and one URI: "Clients can subscribe to specific resources and receive notifications when they change". The same page puts the access decision on the server, per resource: "Access controls **SHOULD** be implemented for sensitive resources" and "Resource permissions **SHOULD** be checked before operations".

On 2026-07-28 the scoping is explicit. SEP-2575 removed `resources/subscribe` and says clients "declare the resources they want updates for in the `notifications` param of the `subscriptions/listen` request. The server sends `notifications/resources/updated` on the listen stream for matching resources." Each subscription is identified by the JSON-RPC request id of its listen request, and "every notification delivered as part of an active subscription **MUST** include the subscription's request ID in `_meta`".

In both revisions the unit of delivery is one subscriber's subscription, and the SDK models the subscribing side exactly that way. `ServerOptions.SubscribeHandler` (`mcp/server.go:109`) is called with the session that subscribed, and the table it fills is `resourceSubscriptions map[string]map[*ServerSession]jsonrpc.ID`, "uri -> session -> requestID" (`mcp/server.go:63`, written at `mcp/server.go:1228`).

### What the SDK offers on the delivery side

`Server.ResourceUpdated` (`mcp/server.go:1183`) is the only exported way to send `notifications/resources/updated`. It takes the whole subscriber set for the URI (`mcp/server.go:1185`), splits it by protocol version (`mcp/server.go:1189-1195`) and notifies all of it: legacy sessions through `notifySessions` (called at `mcp/server.go:1198`, defined at `mcp/shared.go:472`), and 2026-07-28 sessions through `notifySubscribedSessions` (called at `mcp/server.go:1201`, defined at `mcp/server.go:810`). `docs/server.md:401-402` states it plainly: it "notifies every session subscribed to that URI".

`ServerSession` has no equivalent. Its exported senders are `NotifyProgress` (`mcp/server.go:1520`), `Ping` (`:1631`), `ListRoots` (`:1643`), `CreateMessage` (`:1664`), `CreateMessageWithTools` (`:1710`), `Elicit` (`:1729`), `NotifyElicitationComplete` (`:1796`) and `Log` (`:1817`). Nothing sends a resource update.

Application code cannot assemble the 2026-07-28 frame on its own either, because the one value that frame requires is not reachable from outside the package. The listen request id is read from `ctx.Value(idContextKey{})` at subscribe time (`mcp/server.go:1212`) and stored in the unexported subscription table; `idContextKey` is unexported (`mcp/streamable.go:1188`); `injectMetaSubscriptionID` is unexported (`mcp/server.go:832`); and `ServerRequest` (`mcp/shared.go:623`) carries `Session`, `Params` and `Extra`, but not the request id. `MetaKeySubscriptionID` is exported (`mcp/protocol.go:2376`), and the value that belongs under it is not.

The caller's context does not reach the sender either. Both delivery paths build a fresh one: `mcp/shared.go:479` and `mcp/server.go:814` each do `context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)`. `Server.ResourceUpdated` accepts a `ctx` at `mcp/server.go:1183` and its body never uses it, so nothing a caller attaches to that context is visible to the sending middleware that eventually writes the frame (`mcp/shared.go:179`, `mcp/shared.go:130`).

### The observation that found it

I share one `mcp.Server` between credentials: one server per configuration shape, with the GitLab client bound per request, because building a catalog of about a thousand tools per token is not viable. Resource watchers are per credential, since the first read of a resource is the authorization check. Delivery turned out to be the only part of that design with no per-credential seam. The SDK's subscription table is keyed by URI and session and has no notion of a credential, so two credentials subscribed to the same resource each receive the other's notifications, produced by the other's polling, and a credential whose access was revoked keeps being told the resource changed by somebody else's watcher.

I am not presenting that as a defect in the SDK's intended design. A single-tenant server is served correctly by the fan-out, and the fan-out is the natural reading of the older revision. It is a deployment the exported API has no way to express.

The shape reproduces with two ordinary sessions:

```go
server := mcp.NewServer(&mcp.Implementation{Name: "s", Version: "v1"}, &mcp.ServerOptions{
	SubscribeHandler:   func(context.Context, *mcp.SubscribeRequest) error { return nil },
	UnsubscribeHandler: func(context.Context, *mcp.UnsubscribeRequest) error { return nil },
})
server.AddResource(&mcp.Resource{URI: "file:///r1"}, readR1)

csA := connect(server) // csA.Subscribe(ctx, &mcp.SubscribeParams{URI: "file:///r1"})
csB := connect(server) // csB.Subscribe(ctx, &mcp.SubscribeParams{URI: "file:///r1"})

// A's watcher found the change. There is no way to say "tell A".
server.ResourceUpdated(ctx, &mcp.ResourceUpdatedNotificationParams{URI: "file:///r1"})
// Both ResourceUpdatedHandlers fire.
```

`TestSubscriptionsListen_MultipleSessions` in `mcp/mcp_test.go` already asserts that shape for the list-changed notifications, under the comment "A single change fans out to BOTH sessions, each tagged with that session's own ack ID".

### What a server built on the SDK cannot do today

It cannot deliver a resource update to a subset of the sessions subscribed to a URI, on either protocol revision.

It cannot give a delivery a deadline, a cancellation, a trace span or a request-scoped logger, because the context the sender sees is a fresh `context.Background()` with a fixed ten second timeout.

What it can do is filter on the way out, which is what I ship today: a sending middleware added with `AddSendingMiddleware` (`mcp/server.go:1845`) sees `req.GetSession()` and can drop the notification for a session it does not want. That works, and it has two sharp edges worth naming because both were bugs for me first.

The routing key has to travel in the params, since the context cannot carry it. I stamp the owning pool entry into the notification's `_meta` before calling `ResourceUpdated`, filter on it in the middleware, and hand the frame on with a copy of the map that no longer holds my private key. A key in `_meta` is not where a routing decision belongs, and the notification is built and marshalled before it is dropped.

A middleware also has to read the params through the interface. The two paths instantiate the request differently: `notifySessions` is called with a `*ResourceUpdatedNotificationParams` (`mcp/server.go:1198`), so `newRequest` yields `*ServerRequest[*ResourceUpdatedNotificationParams]`, while `notifySubscribedSessions` calls `makeParams() Params` (`mcp/server.go:810`, `:817-819`), so the same notification arrives as `*ServerRequest[Params]`. A type assertion on either concrete type silently matches one revision and drops the other. `req.GetParams()` is the only portable read.

### Proposal

I would like a per-session sender, symmetric with the ones `ServerSession` already has:

```go
// ResourceUpdated notifies the client on this session that the resource
// identified by params.URI has changed. If this session is not subscribed to
// that URI, ResourceUpdated does nothing and returns nil.
func (ss *ServerSession) ResourceUpdated(ctx context.Context, params *ResourceUpdatedNotificationParams) error
```

What it reads, and from where: it takes `ss.server.mu`, looks up `ss.server.resourceSubscriptions[params.URI][ss]` (`mcp/server.go:63`), and releases the lock before sending. If the session is absent it returns nil. If present, it chooses the frame the way `Server.ResourceUpdated` already chooses it at `mcp/server.go:1189-1195`: a session below `protocolVersion20260728` gets the legacy notification, and a 2026-07-28 session gets a copy of the params with that session's own recorded request id stamped by `injectMetaSubscriptionID` (`mcp/server.go:832`). It then calls `handleNotify` with the caller's `ctx`, so the middleware sees the context the caller built.

`Server.ResourceUpdated` can then be expressed as a loop over the subscriber set calling the per-session method, which keeps its behaviour and gives the fan-out path the caller's context as well. That also composes with #1227 and #1228: whoever makes delivery concurrent has one place to do it, and a server author who wants per-session deadlines can build them without waiting for that.

Two semantics I would want maintainers to settle rather than assume: whether "not subscribed" should be a nil return or an exported sentinel error, and whether the method should be allowed on a session that has an entry for the URI recorded by `subscribe` but no live listen stream. My own preference is nil for the first, matching `Server.ResourceUpdated` returning nil when nobody is subscribed, and the second is answered by the table, since `mcp/server.go:1245-1250` removes the entry when the subscription ends.

The second, independent change is to propagate the caller's context. Both signatures are unexported, so this is not an API break:

```go
func notifySessions[S Session, P Params](ctx context.Context, sessions []S, method string, params P, logger *slog.Logger)
func (s *Server) notifySubscribedSessions(ctx context.Context, subscribers map[*ServerSession]jsonrpc.ID, method string, makeParams func() Params)
```

`Server.ResourceUpdated` already has a `ctx` to pass. The ten second bound would become `context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)`, so a caller can shorten it and cancellation reaches the sender. One caller has no caller context to offer: `changeAndNotify` fires `s.notifySessions` from a `time.AfterFunc` (`mcp/server.go:761`), and that path keeps `context.Background()`. It is also a behaviour change worth being explicit about, since a caller who cancels would now stop delivery mid fan-out where today it always completes.

### Alternatives I considered

A generic `ServerSession.SendNotification`, as asked for in #745 and implemented in #1146, does not close this. The send side there wraps a custom method behind the `x-notifications/` prefix, and `SendSubscriptionNotification` reads the subscription id out of the caller's context, so it works from inside the listen handler and not from the goroutine that noticed the resource changed. Neither sends the standard `notifications/resources/updated`, and neither consults the subscription table, so a raw sender would happily deliver to a session that never subscribed. I think the two are complementary rather than overlapping.

Exposing the table instead, something like `Server.Subscribers(uri string) iter.Seq[*ServerSession]`, would let a caller pick recipients but leave it unable to build the 2026-07-28 frame for them, which is the half that cannot be done from outside the package. It would pair with the sender above, not replace it.

A recipient filter in `ServerOptions`, a callback consulted per session per notification, keeps delivery inside the SDK but puts the policy in a place a reader has to go looking for, and it still gives the caller no way to say which update this is. A sender the caller drives is easier to reason about.

Keeping my middleware is the do-nothing option. It works today and I am not blocked. What I dislike about it is that a routing decision travels in `_meta` on the wire format, and that its correctness depends on two details of the delivery paths that are not part of the documented API.

Of these I prefer the per-session sender, because it puts the choice of recipient where the caller already knows the answer, it needs no `_meta` key of its own, and it makes the context propagation fall out for the path that matters most to me. The context change is worth doing on its own merits even if the sender is rejected, and the two are independent.

I am happy to open a pull request for either shape, with tests, once you say which one you want. If the answer is that a multi-credential server should not be sharing one `mcp.Server` in the first place, I would rather hear that than send code.


Part of #1257.

issues.title: Index: nine findings from one audit of a large MCP server against the specification
issues.body:
I maintain a GitLab MCP server built on this SDK: about 865 tools on its individual surface, three tool surfaces, stdio and streamable HTTP, resource subscriptions and OAuth. I audited it against the MCP specification and against the SDK, and recorded every finding that belongs upstream rather than in my own code. Nine of them concern this SDK, and none had a fix when I opened this index: each was reproduced against a real deployment or against the compiled binary driven over its own transport, each names the specification clause, documentation page or semantic convention it fails, and each is pinned by a test I can hand you.

I am filing them as separate issues so that each can be triaged, labelled and closed on its own. This one is the index, so you can see the set at once and see that it comes from one audit rather than from nine unrelated reports. I checked every finding against current main before filing; the individual issues give the version I first observed it on.

### Specification conformance, with a fix offered

Each of these four is a conformance defect with a pull request against it: a minimal change in the SDK's own style, a test that fails before it and passes after, and `go test ./...` green. Two of them have merged.

- #1258 mcp: the declared protocol version, not the negotiated one, decides what a session is served. A client that asks for a newer revision and is negotiated down to an older one is still served the newer interaction. The pull request is #1266, open.
- #1259 A cancelled request is still answered. A response goes out for a request the peer cancelled, which the specification says a receiver should not send. The pull request is #1267, open, now scoped to stdio-style transports on 2026-07-28 and later; this issue gets closed with a note on that scope once it merges.
- #1260 mcp: an unknown protocol version in per-request `_meta` is not answered with `UnsupportedProtocolVersionError`. An unrecognised version is misclassified instead of being refused with the error the versioning page requires. The pull request is #1268, merged.
- #1261 mcp: a receiving middleware cannot tell whether a request carried params. The predicate that answers the question is unexported, so middleware outside the package cannot distinguish an omitted params member from a present one. The pull request is #1269, merged.

### Found during review of the pull requests above

Two defects that the review of #1266 turned up rather than the original audit, each filed with a pull request in the same shape as the four above. Both have merged.

- #1271 mcp: three methods are served on a legacy session before the initialize handshake. The gate lives in one branch of the method switch, so `logging/setLevel`, `resources/subscribe` and `resources/unsubscribe` skip it; subscribe is the one that reaches state. The pull request is #1273, merged.
- #1272 mcp: the negotiated protocol version is recorded on one path of four, so stdio accepts batches a SEP-2575 session forbids. The pull request is #1274, merged.

### Already filed

- #1254, the cancellation reason discarded before any handler sees it. Its pull request, #1255, is merged.

### API the SDK does not expose, proposal only

These four cannot be closed without new exported API, so they went out as proposals rather than as pull requests: each body states the requirement, cites the SDK code that stands in the way, and offers a concrete Go signature together with the alternatives I considered. Three of them, #1263, #1264 and #1265, are waiting on your decision about the shape, and I will write the pull request once you say which one you want.

- #1262 mcp: an SSE response keeps `http.Server.WriteTimeout` armed, so a long-lived stream dies before its first notification. A stream that stays idle is cut by the server's own write deadline before it ever sends anything. #1232 added the keep-alive, and #1293 proposed extending the write deadline on every write to that stream. You decided not to take that change, since `http.Server.WriteTimeout` is the operator's setting and a middleware can handle it, and closed both on 2026-10-14.
- #1263 mcp: a server cannot send the `notifications/cancelled` that 2026-07-28 requires when it tears down a `subscriptions/listen` stream. The protocol asks for that notification on teardown and application code has no way to send it.
- #1264 proposal: mcp: expose the JSON-RPC request id to receiving middleware and handlers. There is no accessor for the id of the message being handled.
- #1265 mcp: a resource update cannot be delivered to one session, and the caller's context never reaches the sending middleware. Delivery goes to every session subscribed to the URI, and nothing a caller puts on its context arrives at the middleware that sends it.

### Filed since

- #1299 mcp: the streamable client does not start a new session after a 404, which the 2025-11-25 transport requires.
- #1359 mcp: Unsubscribe followed by Subscribe can leave a 2026-07-28 session subscribed to nothing. A listen's teardown removes the subscription a later listen on the same session made. The pull request #1360 has merged and fixes the unsubscribe and subscribe again case, and the issue was closed as fixed by it on 2026-10-15.

Every finding above is now filed. The nine of the original audit link back here.
issues.triage_reason: Tracking index of many separate issues (#1258-#1359). Most are already fixed or have PRs, and the rest need new exported API or maintainer decisions, so there is no single actionable change.

issues.title: proposal: auth: support SEP-2350 request-time scope challenges
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

`auth.RequireBearerToken` can't produce a SEP-2350 conformant insufficient-scope challenge, for two separate reasons.

1. Smaller/Possible Bug: On the 403 path the middleware builds a `WWW-Authenticate` header from `resource_metadata` and `scope`, but never adds `error="insufficient_scope"`. RFC 6750 §3.1 requires the `error` param, and a client that switches on it sees an unlabelled challenge and can't tell a scope problem from anything else.
2. Larger/Structural: `RequireBearerTokenOptions.Scopes` is fixed when the middleware is constructed, so a server has exactly one required scope set for every request. SEP-2350 is about advertising the scope a *particular operation* needs, so a low-privilege client can step up for the one tool that requires more. With a construction-time set there's no way to express "`read` for most tools, `admin-write` for this one", and the `scope=` the challenge advertises is the server-wide set rather than what the operation actually needed.

SEP-2350 is merged and labelled final (`modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol#2350`), so this might no longer be a tracking a draft?

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Two changes, separable, and would be happy to land only the first if the second needs more discussion.

1. Add `error="insufficient_scope"` to the challenge on the 403 branch. Non-breaking in any way that matters, and imo it is a bug fix rather than a proposal.

2. Let the required scopes vary per request. The smallest thing that could work is a callback on the options struct, leaving `Scopes` as the static fallback:

```go
type RequireBearerTokenOptions struct {
    // ...
    // ScopesForRequest returns the scopes required for this particular
    // request. When nil, Scopes applies to every request.
    ScopesForRequest func(*http.Request) []string
}
```

The middleware would use its result both for the containment check and for the `scope=` it advertises, so the challenge names what the operation needed rather than what the server requires in general.

One thing we want to deep dive a bit more is that `RequireBearerToken` is a generic `net/http` middleware and runs before the JSON-RPC body is dispatched, so a `ScopesForRequest` callback cannot see which tool is being called without the implementer parsing the body themselves.  While this may be (coz it keeps the auth package free of MCP concepts and puts the choice in the caller's hands) if the preference is for the scope requirement to live next to the tool it guards then this is a different and larger design touching the `mcp` package.  Would prefer to hear yall's thoughts on which which direction to take.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

* *A typed error from the handler.* Let a tool handler return something like `auth.ErrInsufficientScope{Scopes: []string{"admin-write"}}` that the HTTP layer maps to a 403 plus challenge. This puts the requirement next to the tool, which reads better, but it means the check happens after dispatch rather than in middleware, and it couples `mcp` to `auth`.
* *Leave it to implementers.* Callers can write their own middleware today. It works, but every implementer re-derives the RFC 6750 challenge format, and the SDK already owns that formatting for the 401 case, so the knowledge is half here already.
* *Do nothing until the TypeScript SDK settles.* Genuinely possible, see below.

**Additional context**

The main question I have before writing any code is whether we want to wait for the TypeScript SDK?`modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk#1624` is the reference implementation for this, open since March, currently with changes requested. `auth.go` notes that `RequireBearerToken` is based on that SDK's `bearerAuth.ts`, so if you'd rather track their final API shape than diverge, that's a fair call.  Id love to know now than send a PR prematurely.

Also from a conformance angle `modelcontextprotocol/conformance#481` adds a server-side scope-challenge scenario covering `tools/call`, static and templated `resources/read`, and `prompts/get`. When it merges, the Go SDK will either fail it or need a new exclusion line in `conformance/baseline.yml` alongside the DPoP and WIF ones. IMO doing this now keeps it ready then.

Some prior-art - I've implemented the equivalent in another Go MCP library (`panyam/mcpkit#1353`, request-time challenges across all primitives) and it passes that scenario 17/17 with no warnings. So I have a design that's been through the conformance suite and I'm happy to write the PR here.  Just want to make sure the extension point/design first with yall.
issues.triage_reason: Part 2 (ScopesForRequest in auth.RequireBearerTokenOptions) is an exported API change needing an accepted proposal and a maintainer design decision. Only the small `error="insufficient_scope"` addition in auth/auth.go RequireBearerToken is doable, and it wouldn't fully resolve the issue.

issues.title: Dual-era servers serve modern Tool schemas unchanged to legacy clients
issues.body:
## Summary

The Go SDK supports both legacy MCP (`2025-11-25` and earlier) and modern MCP (`2026-07-28`), but a server registers one static `Tool.InputSchema` and appears to return that same schema from `tools/list` regardless of the negotiated/requested protocol version.

That can make a dual-era server emit a schema that is valid under `2026-07-28` but outside the `2025-11-25` `Tool.inputSchema` envelope.

## Specification boundary

In [`2025-11-25`](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/main/schema/2025-11-25/schema.ts), `Tool.inputSchema` permits only:

```ts
{
  $schema?: string;
  type: "object";
  properties?: { [key: string]: object };
  required?: string[];
}
```

[SEP-2106](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/main/seps/2106-json-schema-2020-12.md), shipped in [`2026-07-28`](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/main/schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts), changes this to:

```ts
{ $schema?: string; type: "object"; [key: string]: unknown }
```

This explicitly permits root composition keywords such as `anyOf`, `oneOf`, and `allOf` for modern clients.

## Reproduction shape

1. Create a Go SDK server using the normal dual-era/default protocol support.
2. Register a tool whose root input schema contains `type: "object"` plus `anyOf`.
3. Connect a client using protocol version `2025-11-25`.
4. Call `tools/list`.
5. Observe that the modern schema is returned unchanged even though root `anyOf` was not representable by the legacy `Tool.inputSchema` definition.

A concrete downstream incident is documented in [github/github-mcp-server#3126](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/issues/3126#issuecomment-5353596920). That incident also involved a model-provider restriction, but this issue is specifically about MCP protocol-era conformance.

## Expected SDK behavior / API

The SDK should provide a deliberate way for dual-era servers to remain schema-conformant. Possible approaches:

1. Validate tool schemas against every enabled protocol version at registration/startup and reject modern-only schemas unless the server supplies a legacy representation.
2. Provide a version-aware tool/schema callback or `tools/list` projection hook so applications can supply a legacy-compatible representation.
3. Document that dual-era servers must keep canonical tool schemas within the legacy intersection unless they opt into version-specific representations.

I do **not** think the SDK should silently strip modern keywords, because removing constraints can change tool semantics.

## Immutability and concurrency

Any version-specific representation should:

- deep-clone or use copy-on-write per inventory/list response;
- never mutate shared `Tool`, `InputSchema`, `Properties`, or nested schema maps in place;
- remain safe when legacy and modern requests are served concurrently;
- preserve the canonical modern schema for modern clients and caches.

## Provider compatibility is separate

This issue should not attempt to solve Anthropic/OpenAI tool-schema subsets. A client using modern MCP may still need a provider-specific schema adapter before forwarding tools to an LLM API. That is independent of the MCP protocol version selected between client and server.

## Existing issues checked

- #990 implemented SEP-2106 for the modern protocol.
- #455 addressed decoding incompatible schemas from older JSON Schema drafts.

I did not find an issue covering version-specific `tools/list` schema representations for a dual-era server.
issues.triage_reason: The issue leaves the design open (reject at registration, add a version-aware tools/list hook, or document), and the hook options need new exported API and an accepted proposal. The registration-time validation option is a behavior change that also needs a maintainer decision. The relevant code is the tools/list handler and AddTool in mcp/server.go.

issues.title: Docs site: umbrella UI/UX issues
issues.body:
The docs site has a set of UI defects that are easier to track together than one at a time. Everything below was measured on the deployed site (https://agent-sandbox.sigs.k8s.io, Hugo 0.163.3, `main`, 2026-09-15). They are independent, so they can be picked off one at a time.

## Content unreachable

- [x] **The navbar never collapses.** (https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/pull/1659) At a 390px viewport, `.navbar-collapse` computes to `display:flex` at 983px wide and `.navbar-toggler` to `display:none`, so the document is 1118px wide and six of eight nav links are off-screen with no way to reach them. Cause: [`site/layouts/partials/navbar.html#L6-L9`](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/blob/main/site/layouts/partials/navbar.html#L6-L9) is a fork of the Bootstrap 4 Docsy navbar (`collapse navbar-collapse` plus a `data-toggle` button), while current Docsy ships `.td-navbar .navbar-collapse { display: flex !important }` and `.td-navbar .navbar-toggler { display: none }` outside any media query. The fork gets neither behaviour. Fix: drop the custom partial, or move it to Docsy's current markup (`td-navbar-nav-scroll`, no toggler). 

- [x] **Tables spill off the right edge and cannot be scrolled.** (https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/pull/1660) On [/docs/use-cases/examples/openclaw-fleet-gke/](https://agent-sandbox.sigs.k8s.io/docs/use-cases/examples/openclaw-fleet-gke/) at 390px, `THEAD`, `TBODY` and `TR` all reach x = 598, which is 208px past the edge, and the clipped columns are unreachable. [/docs/api/](https://agent-sandbox.sigs.k8s.io/docs/api/) is worse: 31 tables, the widest hiding 386px. Not only mobile, three of the API tables are clipped and unreachable at 1280 as well, hiding 117px, 117px and 95px. Cause: the dark-table override at [`_styles_project.scss#L707-L713`](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/blob/main/site/assets/scss/_styles_project.scss#L707-L713) sets `display: block` and then `overflow: visible !important`, which cancels the scroll half of Docsy's responsive-table treatment while keeping the block half. Fix: drop the `overflow` override and let `overflow-x: auto` apply.

## Type scale and hierarchy

- [ ] **Section-index cards are inverted: the description is 1.75x the title.** (https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/pull/1781) At 1280px, `.description` measures 31.36px at weight 400 against a 17.92px, weight 700 `.title`. Below 768px it inverts the other way, with 0.84rem titles (smaller than body text) against 1.12rem descriptions. Cause: [`_styles_project.scss#L817-L841`](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/blob/main/site/assets/scss/_styles_project.scss#L817-L841). Fix: make the title the largest thing on the card at both breakpoints.

- [x] **Docs page titles render at 51.2px (1280) / 57.6px (1440),** (https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/pull/1764) with a 22.4px site-title eyebrow above them and a 20px page description. Root font is 16px, so this is not zoom. Cause: [`site/layouts/docs/single.html#L3-L5`](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/blob/main/site/layouts/docs/single.html#L3-L5) puts `display-1` and `display-6` on every docs page, and [`_styles_project.scss#L301-L310`](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/blob/main/site/assets/scss/_styles_project.scss#L301-L310) sizes `.display-1` with `clamp(1.6rem, 4vw, 3.6rem)`, a cover-block scale. Fix: stop stamping the display classes in the docs layout and let `.td-content > h1` carry its own size. Note: Don't fix this by editing the clamp. The rule is a shared selector list (`.td-cover-block, .td-content`), so shrinking it there also shrinks the homepage hero headline, which is the one place the large size is wanted.

- [ ] **Homepage Quickstart code renders at 20px.** Related but a different cause: the shortcode renders inside the cover block's `<div class="pt-3 lead">` and `<pre>` inherits Bootstrap's `1.25rem`. Fix: pin the font size on `.quickstart-container pre, .quickstart-container code`.

- [ ] **Sidebar items are visually indistinguishable.** Across all 96 links at 1280px: 16px at every nesting level, weight 500 on 94 of them, `rgba(255,255,255,0.9)` on all of them, and link widths of 101-149px, so 2-4 line wraps are routine. The `padding-bottom` between items is 6px against a 24px line-height, meaning the space inside a wrapped item is 4x the space between two different items. A four-line entry reads as four entries. Nearly every page here is an `_index.md`, so Docsy's `__page` lightening almost never applies, and the `col-xl-2` column inside the [1200px container cap](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/blob/main/site/assets/scss/_styles_project.scss#L50-L52) squeezes level-3 items to about 100px, which guarantees the wrap. Fix needs all three: smaller type (14px), item spacing larger than line spacing, and some weight or color distinction per level. A wider column would help as much as any of them.

## Layout

- [x] **Docs pages overflow horizontally by 12px at 1280.** (https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/pull/1659) `scrollWidth` 1292 against `innerWidth` 1280, so there's a stray horizontal scrollbar at a very common laptop width. Homepage is fine at 1265. Suspect the `-15px` margins on `.td-sidebar-nav` escaping the container cap.

- [ ] **Docs pages still overflow between 992px and about 1208px.** #1659 fixes the 1280 case, but `scrollWidth` is 1208 against `innerWidth` 1000 (208px over) and 1199 (9px over). Cause: Docsy wraps the horizontal nav scroller in `media-breakpoint-down(lg)`, which stops at 991.98px, so through the 992 to 1199 band the nav row lays out at its natural 1208px with nothing to scroll it.

- [ ] **About 192px of dead space above the mobile hero** (`padding-top: 8rem` plus `margin-top: 4rem`), so the first screenful of the homepage is mostly empty on a phone.

## Accessibility and gaps

- [x] **No visible focus on the homepage card links.** (https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/pull/1762) `.link-card` and `.use-case-card` start with `all: unset`, which removes the focus ring, and only `:hover` is restyled. Nine of the homepage's main links are unusable by keyboard (WCAG 2.4.7).

- [ ] **Link color fails WCAG AA.** `$primary: #2B6AA2` is also `$link-color` and the sidebar active-item color, and measures about 3.6:1 on the black sections against a 4.5:1 threshold.

- [ ] **No site search.** `gcs_engine_id` is commented out in `hugo.yaml`, while `content/search.md` ships a results page nothing can reach.

/kind bug
/kind documentation
/help

issues.title: Support a Codex-native mode that can use the current Codex session as the LLM runner
issues.body:
### Problem Statement

First of all, thank you for open-sourcing Open Code Review and for adding Codex skill/plugin support. The project is very useful, especially the deterministic diff handling and structured review workflow.

I would like to use Open Code Review from inside Codex via the installed skill/plugin. Today, the Codex integration invokes the local `ocr` CLI, and `ocr` still requires a separately configured LLM endpoint/API key. For users who already have a Codex subscription or token allowance, this means the Codex integration cannot use their existing Codex quota and requires another provider setup or extra API billing.

This is a bit confusing from a user perspective because the workflow is launched inside Codex, but the actual model calls are still managed outside Codex.

### Proposed Solution

It would be great to have a Codex-native mode for the Codex integration.

Possible shape:

- A documented mode such as `ocr review --audience agent --llm-runner codex`, or a dedicated Codex skill/plugin path.
- In this mode, Open Code Review could keep the deterministic parts of the pipeline, such as diff/file selection, grouping, rules, and output formatting.
- The LLM judgment/review step would be delegated to the current Codex session, so users can use their existing Codex quota instead of configuring `OCR_LLM_URL` / `OCR_LLM_TOKEN`.

If direct access to the Codex model runner is not technically possible, another helpful option might be to expose an `ocr` command that only prepares the deterministic review context as JSON/Markdown. The Codex skill could then ask Codex itself to perform the review from that context.

### Alternatives Considered

Current workarounds I found:

- Configure a separate OpenAI/Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible endpoint for `ocr`.
- Use a local model through Ollama/LM Studio.
- Use Codex's native code review without Open Code Review.

These work, but they either require extra provider setup/cost, or they lose the Open Code Review pipeline that makes this project valuable.

### Affected Area

Review Agent / LLM interaction

### Additional Context

Related docs/PRs I looked at:

- The README says the Codex plugin registers a skill that runs `ocr review --audience agent`.
- PR #69 notes that the Codex integration does not make Codex the internal LLM runner for OCR.

I completely understand there may be product/API limitations here. Even a short documentation note explaining the limitation and recommended Codex-native workaround would be very helpful. Thanks again for the great project!

issues.title: code_search fails with exit 128 when a regex-mode search term contains an unbalanced parenthesis
issues.body:
### OpenCodeReview Version

open-code-review v1.12.4 (f1101fd7f) darwin/arm64, built at 2026-09-16T09:58:39Z

### Operating System

macOS (Apple Silicon)

### Installation Method

npm (global)

### LLM Provider

Other OpenAI-compatible endpoint

### Bug Description

In regex mode (`use_perl_regexp: true`), `code_search` passes the model's `search_text` verbatim to `git grep -P`. A search term containing an unbalanced `(` fails PCRE compilation, so the tool returns exit 128 instead of running the search.

Models search for literals like `Set("gorm:` when reviewing GORM code, so this comes up often. In one review run, 31 of 348 `code_search` calls failed this way (about 9%); in another, 11 of 236.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `ocr review -f json --audience agent` on a changeset that leads the model to search for a literal containing `(`. A Go codebase using GORM's `db.Set("gorm:...")` triggers it quickly.
2. Or run the underlying command directly, in any repo:

```console
$ git grep -P -e 'Set("gorm:'
fatal: -e option, 'Set("gorm:': missing closing parenthesis
```

The same term under default BRE does not error, because a bare `(` is a literal there. Only the `-P` path fails, and `-P` is what regex-mode `code_search` uses.

### Expected Behavior

Either run the search as a literal match (for example fall back to `git grep -F` when the regex fails to compile), or validate the regex first and return an error the model can act on.

### Logs / Error Output

```
[ocr]   ✘ code_search failed: git grep failed: exit status 128: fatal: -e option, 'Set("gorm:': missing closing parenthesis
[ocr]   ✘ code_search failed: git grep failed: exit status 128: fatal: -e option, 'ray.method(': missing closing parenthesis
```

### AI/LLM Disclosure

An AI coding agent working for me collected the failure counts from ocr's session logs. The reproduce command and its output above were run and verified directly in a terminal.

### Additional Context

Failures return in milliseconds, so nothing stalls. The cost is one wasted agent round-trip per failure: the model retries with different terms or falls back to reading files chunk by chunk, which slows the review and weakens the search. Escaping all metacharacters is not a good fix, since regex mode is intentional and models pass alternations like `a|b|c`. Falling back to `git grep -F` on a compile error, and telling the model about the fallback, keeps both uses working. Related earlier `git grep` argument-handling bugs in `code_search`: #645, #53.
issues.pr_title: fix(tool): retry code_search as literal when regex fails to compile
issues.pr_body:
## Description

In regex mode, `code_search` runs `git grep -P` with the model's `search_text`. A term with an unbalanced parenthesis, such as `Set("gorm:`, fails PCRE compilation and git exits with 128, so the model gets an error instead of results.

Now, when `git grep -P` exits 128 with a pattern-compile error that names the search text, `code_search` retries the same search as a literal match (`-F`). The retry keeps the ref and `--no-index` settings. A successful retry prepends this note to the result: `Note: search_text is not a valid regular expression; searched as literal text instead.` If the literal search finds nothing, the result is the note followed by `No matches found`. Any other failure keeps the original error. Valid regexes such as `a|b|c` behave as before.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] CI / Build / Tooling

## How Has This Been Tested?

`TestGitGrep_PerlRegexp_InvalidPattern_ReturnsError` is replaced by `TestGitGrep_PerlRegexp_InvalidPattern_FallsBackToLiteral`. It covers workspace, commit-ref and runner modes, each with a literal match and a no-match case. It checks that the note is present, that the match is found or `No matches found` is returned, and that no error is returned.

I added `TestGitGrep_PerlRegexp_InvalidPattern_NoIndexFallback` for a directory outside a git repo (`--no-index`).

Falling back to a literal search keeps the review going and tells the model what happened, so it can adjust its next query. issues.title: [Enhancement] Return structured Kubernetes status for tool execution errors
issues.body:
## Problem

Kubernetes API errors returned by core resource tools are currently reduced to server-specific text in an MCP `CallToolResult` with `isError: true`. For example, the `resources_create_or_update` and `resources_get` handlers wrap the underlying Kubernetes error with `fmt.Errorf` and return it through `api.NewToolCallResult`.

That loses the machine-readable fields from `metav1.Status` / `apierrors.StatusError`, including:

- HTTP status code
- Kubernetes reason (`NotFound`, `Forbidden`, `Invalid`, `Conflict`, etc.)
- resource and name details
- field causes and other structured details

Downstream clients must parse prose such as `field is immutable` or `not found`. This is brittle across server versions, Kubernetes libraries, alternate MCP servers, and gateway formatting.

## Proposal

When a Kubernetes operation fails, include a structured Kubernetes `Status` object in the MCP tool result `structuredContent`, while retaining the existing text content and `isError: true` response for backward compatibility.

Example:

```json
{
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "kind": "Status",
  "status": "Failure",
  "reason": "Invalid",
  "code": 422,
  "message": "...",
  "details": {
    "group": "batch",
    "kind": "Job",
    "name": "example"
  }
}
```

The structured payload should preserve the original Kubernetes status information where available, including `details.causes` for validation failures. It should apply consistently to the core resource operations (`resources_get`, `resources_list`, `resources_create_or_update`, `resources_delete`, and `resources_scale`).

## Compatibility and semantics

- Keep the current human-readable `TextContent` response for existing clients.
- Keep `isError: true` for tool execution failures.
- Do not reinterpret `resources_create_or_update` errors as `AlreadyExists`: that tool is documented as server-side apply and should retain the actual Kubernetes reason/code. A separate create-only tool would be a distinct enhancement if Kubernetes `Create` semantics are needed.
- Add tests covering at least `NotFound`, `Forbidden`, `Invalid`, and conflict/status payloads.
- Document the structured error contract so clients do not need to parse server-specific prose.

## Downstream motivation

Kubernaut currently needs to translate remote MCP errors into controller-runtime-compatible errors. The downstream hardening is tracked in [PR #2435](https://github.com/jordigilh/kubernaut/pull/2435), but a structured upstream response would remove the need for any text-based fallback.

## References

- MCP tool result structured content: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools#structured-content
- Kubernetes `metav1.Status`: https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1#Status

issues.title: test(model/gemini): continuation tests miss a MAX_TOKENS stop after CONTINUATION and requests that set maxOutputTokens
issues.body:
After #1815, the Gemini model resumes only a `CONTINUATION` stop and returns a `MAX_TOKENS` stop as it is. The continuation tests in `model/gemini` do not pin that rule in two situations, so a change that breaks it can pass the whole package suite.

**A `MAX_TOKENS` stop that follows a `CONTINUATION` pause.** This is the case #1815 fixes: with genai v1.74.0 and no `maxOutputTokens`, a long answer pauses with `CONTINUATION` and then stops with `MAX_TOKENS` and a token once the default budget is spent. Resuming that stop returns a 400. The two tests that pin `MAX_TOKENS` ([unary](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/f0386eabbf40a4b96bd903109a47fa0441e8f446/model/gemini/continuation_test.go#L295-L307), [streamed](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/f0386eabbf40a4b96bd903109a47fa0441e8f446/model/gemini/continuation_test.go#L379-L402), at the PR's head f0386ea) both stop on the first request. If `continuationToken` resumed a `MAX_TOKENS` stop only after an earlier `CONTINUATION`, the 400 would come back and every test in the package would still pass.

**Requests that set `maxOutputTokens`.** #1815 removed the cases that set it: `CONTINUATION with maxOutputTokens` ([unary](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/bd421447f90c60bfe08a411f4f7a2bf805075169/model/gemini/continuation_test.go#L324-L340), [streamed](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/bd421447f90c60bfe08a411f4f7a2bf805075169/model/gemini/continuation_test.go#L455-L463)) and `maxOutputTokens spent` ([unary](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/bd421447f90c60bfe08a411f4f7a2bf805075169/model/gemini/continuation_test.go#L341-L352), [streamed](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/bd421447f90c60bfe08a411f4f7a2bf805075169/model/gemini/continuation_test.go#L446-L454)), linked here at main before the PR. All four still pass against the PR's code. Without them, two regressions go unnoticed: a `CONTINUATION` stop not resumed when `maxOutputTokens` is set, which is how #1715 is used, and a `MAX_TOKENS` stop resumed when it is set.

The property the tests should hold, in unary and streaming mode: a `MAX_TOKENS` stop is never resumed, wherever it falls in the generation, and a `CONTINUATION` stop with a token is resumed whatever `maxOutputTokens` says.

**Done when** each of these changes to `continuationToken` makes a test in `model/gemini` fail:

- resuming a `MAX_TOKENS` stop with a token after an earlier `CONTINUATION`
- not resuming a `CONTINUATION` stop when the request sets `maxOutputTokens`
- resuming a `MAX_TOKENS` stop with a token when the request sets `maxOutputTokens`

**Please ensure you have read the [contribution guide](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) before creating a pull request.**

### Linked issue

Fixes #1816

- Closes: #1816

**Problem:**
After #1815, the Gemini model resumes only a `CONTINUATION` stop and returns a `MAX_TOKENS` stop as it is. The continuation tests did not pin this in two cases: a `MAX_TOKENS` stop that follows a `CONTINUATION` pause, and requests that set `maxOutputTokens`. A change to `continuationToken` could break the rule and the package tests would still pass.

**Solution:**
Add one table-driven test, `TestContinuation_ResumesOnlyContinuationStops`, in `model/gemini/continuation_test.go`. It runs each case in unary and streaming mode. The cases are:

- `MAX_TOKENS` after `CONTINUATION`: the stop is not resumed.
- `CONTINUATION` with `maxOutputTokens` set: the stop is resumed.
- `MAX_TOKENS` with `maxOutputTokens` set: the stop is not resumed.
- `MAX_TOKENS` after `CONTINUATION`, with `maxOutputTokens` set: the stop is not resumed.

Each case checks the final finish reason and the continuation tokens sent in the requests.

### Behavior change

**What behaves differently for someone already on the current release?**

Nothing. Only a test file changes.

**Unit Tests:**

- [x] All unit tests pass locally.

New test: `TestContinuation_ResumesOnlyContinuationStops` (8 subtests: 4 cases, unary and streamed). It passes against the current code.

No source change was made, so there is nothing to revert. I did not mutate `continuationToken` to confirm the three failures listed in the issue, because it lives in the genai SDK in the module cache, outside this repo. issues.title: toolconfirmation: a repeated approval runs the confirmed tool again
issues.body:
**Describe the Bug:**

If the same tool confirmation response is sent more than once, the confirmed tool runs again each time. The user approves once, and the tool runs once per delivery of that approval. This can happen with a client retry of `/run_sse`, a double-submitted approval button, or a redelivered A2A message. No new confirmation is requested and the model is not involved. The original arguments simply run again.

`RequestConfirmationRequestProcessor` decides whether a confirmed call has already run by looking for its function response only in events after the latest user event ([request_confirmation_processor.go#L216-L230](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/82ca4c62/internal/llminternal/request_confirmation_processor.go#L216-L230)). When the approval is delivered again, it becomes the latest user event, and the tool result from the first resume is now before it, so the check misses it and the call is dispatched again.

For a `RequireConfirmation` tool that sends money, deletes data or sends an email, a single approval should not be usable more than once.

**Steps to Reproduce:**

`functiontool` with `RequireConfirmation: true`, `runner.New` with the in-memory session service, and a fake model that calls the tool once and then answers with text:

```go
transfer, _ := functiontool.New(functiontool.Config{Name: "transfer", RequireConfirmation: true},
	func(ctx agent.Context, a args) (map[string]any, error) {
		executed++
		return map[string]any{"status": "sent"}, nil
	})
```

1. Run "send 100": the agent asks for confirmation (`adk_request_confirmation`)
2. Send the approval: `FunctionResponse{Name: "adk_request_confirmation", ID: <confirmation id>, Response: {"confirmed": true}}`
3. Send the same approval again

**Expected Behavior:**

An approval resumes the call once. Delivering it again does not run the tool a second time.

**Observed Behavior:**

```text
-- user: send 100
  confirmation requested, id adk-57cefeeb-bf51-4cb2-86d8-5dce35540215
-- user approves
  >>> TRANSFER EXECUTED amount=100 (total executions=1)
-- same approval delivered again (client retry)
  >>> TRANSFER EXECUTED amount=100 (total executions=2)
-- and again
  >>> TRANSFER EXECUTED amount=100 (total executions=3)
```

The session ends up with three `transfer` results for the one `call-1`.

**Environment Details:**
 - ADK Library Version: main (82ca4c62)
 - OS: macOS
 - Go Version: 1.27

**Model Information:** N/A (fake model)

**Additional Context:**

The fix is to look for the call's result in every event after the confirmation request, not only after the latest user event. The "requires confirmation" placeholder result is written before the request event, so it is not counted and the first approval still runs. I have a fix with a test and will open a PR.

adk-python has the same problem: `_RequestConfirmationLlmRequestProcessor` also only checks the events after the last user event. Filed there as google/adk-python#7434.

**How often has this issue occurred?:** Always
issues.pr_title: fix(llminternal): do not rerun a confirmed tool on repeated approval
issues.pr_body:
Fixes #1752

- Closes: #1752

**Problem:**
`RequestConfirmationRequestProcessor` checks whether a confirmed call already has a function response only in events after the latest user event. If the same approval is delivered again (client retry, double submit, redelivered message), it becomes the latest user event. The result of the first resume is then before it, the check misses it, and the tool runs again with the original arguments.

**Solution:**
Look for the call's function response in every event after the confirmation request, not only after the latest user event. The "requires confirmation" placeholder result is written before the request event, so it is not counted and the first approval still runs. The `confirmationEventIndex` variable is no longer used, so it is removed.

### Behavior change

A tool confirmation that is delivered more than once now resumes the call once. Before, the tool ran again for each delivery. Single approvals behave as before.

### Testing Plan

**Unit Tests:**

fix(llminternal): do not rerun a confirmed tool on repeated approval

Fixes #1752

- Closes: #1752

**Problem:**
`RequestConfirmationRequestProcessor` checks whether a confirmed call already has a function response only in events after the latest user event. If the same approval is delivered again (client retry, double submit, redelivered message), it becomes the latest user event. The result of the first resume is then before it, the check misses it, and the tool runs again with the original arguments.

**Solution:**
Look for the call's function response in every event after the confirmation request, not only after the latest user event. The "requires confirmation" placeholder result is written before the request event, so it is not counted and the first approval still runs. The `confirmationEventIndex` variable is no longer used, so it is removed.

### Behavior change

A tool confirmation that is delivered more than once now resumes the call once. Before, the tool ran again for each delivery. Single approvals behave as before.

issues.title: mcptoolset: non-text tool-result content blocks are silently dropped (EmbeddedResource, ResourceLink, Image, Audio)
issues.body:
## Summary

`tool/mcptoolset/tool.go`'s result conversion in `mcpTool.Run` keeps only `*mcp.TextContent` blocks. Every other content-block class — `EmbeddedResource`, `ResourceLink`, `ImageContent`, `AudioContent` — is silently discarded:

```go
textResponse := strings.Builder{}
for _, c := range res.Content {
    textContent, ok := c.(*mcp.TextContent)
    if !ok {
        continue
    }
    ...
}
```

The same text-only loop is used for the `IsError` path, and when `res.StructuredContent` is non-nil the content blocks are ignored entirely.

## Real-world impact

GitHub's official MCP server (github/github-mcp-server, also the hosted api.githubcopilot.com endpoints) returns `get_file_contents` file bodies as an `EmbeddedResource` block alongside a status-line `TextContent` (`pkg/utils/result.go` `NewToolResultResource`). Through mcptoolset, the model therefore receives only:

```
successfully downloaded text file (SHA: …)
```

with no file content at all — the agent is effectively blind to every file it reads, with no error or indication anything was dropped. Directory listings (plain text) survive, which makes the loss non-obvious. Files ≥ 1MB come back as `ResourceLink`, also dropped.

Related: #1352 covers the "no text content in tool response" error, which is what a result consisting *only* of non-text blocks currently produces — the two issues are adjacent but distinct.

## Suggested behavior

At minimum, flatten `EmbeddedResource` with textual content (`Resource.Text`, or `Resource.Blob` with a text-like MIME type) into the text output, and represent `ResourceLink`/binary resources legibly (URI + MIME + size) rather than dropping them. Ideally, image/audio blocks would map to genai `inlineData` parts.

## Workaround

Supplying `Config.Client` with a custom `*mcp.Client` carrying an `AddSendingMiddleware` that rewrites `EmbeddedResource`/`ResourceLink` blocks into `TextContent` before the conversion runs restores the content losslessly. Happy to upstream a PR along those lines if useful.

Observed on v2.2.0; `main` is currently identical for this file.
issues.pr_title: fix(mcptoolset): keep non-text blocks when result has structured content
issues.pr_body:
**Please ensure you have read the [contribution guide](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) before creating a pull request.**

### Linked issue

Fixes #1391

- Closes: #1391
- Related: #1352

**2. Describe the change:**

**Problem:**
When an MCP tool result has `StructuredContent`, `mcpTool.Run` returned only `{"output": StructuredContent}` and ignored `res.Content`. Servers such as the GitHub MCP server send file bodies as an `EmbeddedResource` block next to the structured data, so the model never saw the file content.

**Solution:**
When `StructuredContent` is set and `res.Content` has at least one block that is not `*mcp.TextContent`, `Run` now also returns a `"content"` key. Its value is the output of the existing `formatMCPContent`, so embedded resources, resource links, images and audio are formatted the same way as in the non-structured path. Text-only content is still left out, because it usually repeats the structured output. A small helper, `hasNonTextContent`, makes this check.

This change does not add new handling for the non-structured path, and it does not map image or audio blocks to genai inline data parts.

### Behavior change

**What behaves differently for someone already on the current release?**

For MCP results that have `StructuredContent` and also non-text content blocks, the returned map now has an extra `"content"` key with the formatted text of the blocks. The `"output"` key is unchanged. Results with structured content and only text blocks, and results without structured content, are unchanged.

### Testing Plan

**Unit Tests:**

- [x] All unit tests pass locally.

Added `TestMCPToolRunStructuredContentKeepsContentBlocks` in `tool/mcptoolset/tool_test.go`. It runs a tool whose result has `StructuredContent` and an `EmbeddedResource` with text, and checks that the file text is in the result. I also updated the expected value of the existing mixed structured/embedded-resource case in `TestMCPToolRunContent`, which now includes the `"content"` key.

**With your source change reverted and your tests kept, which test fails?**

`TestMCPToolRunStructuredContentKeepsContentBlocks` fails, and so does the updated mixed case in `TestMCPToolRunContent`, because the result has no `"content"` key.

**Manual End-to-End (E2E) Tests:**

Not run. No live MCP server was used.

issues.pr_title: fix(waypoint): set AttachedRoutes on waypoint gateway listeners
issues.pr_body:
# Description

Fixes #14553

Waypoint Gateways are translated by the waypoint plugin (`ContributesGwTranslator`), not the core translator. Because of this, `setAttachedRoutes` never ran for them and `AttachedRoutes` was always 0.

The waypoint translator now sets `AttachedRoutes` on each listener after `buildServiceChains`. The count is the number of unique routes, taken from both gateway-level routes and service-level routes.

Testing:
- Added the test case `HTTPRoute on Gateway and Service` (`httproute-mixed`) to `waypoint_translator_test.go`. It has routes attached to both the Gateway and a Service.
- Updated the existing waypoint golden output files to include the new `AttachedRoutes` values.

# Change Type

/kind fix

# Changelog

```release-note
Fix waypoint Gateways always reporting 0 AttachedRoutes on their listeners.
```

# Additional Notes

The waypoint translator skips the core translator, so a step was missed without anyone noticing. I added the count and a test so it cannot break again quietly.

fix(waypoint): set AttachedRoutes on waypoint gateway listeners

# Description

Fixes #14553

Waypoint Gateways are translated by the waypoint plugin (`ContributesGwTranslator`), not the core translator. Because of this, `setAttachedRoutes` never ran for them and `AttachedRoutes` was always 0.

The waypoint translator now sets `AttachedRoutes` on each listener after `buildServiceChains`. The count is the number of unique routes, taken from both gateway-level routes and service-level routes.

Testing:

# Change Type

/kind fix

# Changelog

```release-note
Fix waypoint Gateways always reporting 0 AttachedRoutes on their listeners.
```

# Additional Notes

The waypoint translator skips the core translator, so a step was missed without anyone noticing. I added the count and a test so it cannot break again quietly.

issues.title: mcp: SSEClientTransport ties the event stream to the context passed to Connect
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`SSEClientTransport.Connect` opens the long-lived event stream with `http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "GET", c.Endpoint, nil)`, using the context given to `Client.Connect` (`mcp/sse.go`; present in v1.8.0 and on `main` at 53effc0). Callers usually bound the handshake with a timeout:

```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
defer cancel()
session, err := client.Connect(ctx, &mcp.SSEClientTransport{Endpoint: url}, nil)
```

The session works until `cancel` runs or the timeout fires. After that the stream is closed and every later call fails. `StreamableClientTransport` detaches its connection from the `Connect` context, so the same code works on one transport and silently breaks on the other.

**To Reproduce**

1. Connect to an SSE server with a context that has a short timeout, as above.
2. Let the timeout fire (or call `cancel`).
3. Call `session.ListTools`: it fails because the event stream is gone.

**Expected behavior**

The stream's lifetime is tied to the connection, ended by `Close`, as with the streamable transport. If the current behavior is intended, document it on `Client.Connect` and `SSEClientTransport`. Happy to send a PR.

**Additional context**

Found while moving [PromptKit](https://github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit)'s MCP client onto go-sdk v1.8.0 ([AltairaLabs/PromptKit#2141](https://github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/pull/2141)). We work around it by passing `Connect` a context that outlives the handshake: [`dial`](https://github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/blob/5a3fa31e0f33792d92d2e1d46042cc4f77e6cca3/runtime/mcp/client.go#L153-L160).
issues.pr_title: mcp: detach SSE client event stream from the Connect context
issues.pr_body:
Fixes #1331

SSEClientTransport.Connect used the context passed to it for the long-lived event stream. If the caller bounded the handshake with a timeout or cancelled it afterwards, the stream closed and later calls failed. StreamableClientTransport does not behave this way.

This change makes the stream independent of the Connect context. The context now only bounds the handshake: if it is cancelled before the handshake completes, Connect returns the error and cleans up the request. After Connect returns, the stream is cancelled only by Close.

Testing: added `TestSSEClientConnectContextCanceled` in `mcp/sse_test.go`. It cancels the Connect context after connecting and checks that a later Ping succeeds. The test and the project's checks pass.

I use the usual pattern of a timeout context for Connect, and it broke the SSE session without any warning. The streamable transport works with the same code, so I wanted both to behave the same.

issues.title: MCP execute_command: bound returned output and report truncation
issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Add a configurable output budget to the MCP `execute_command` tool, defaulting to approximately **30,000 Unicode characters across stdout and stderr combined**. When output exceeds the budget, retain **equal-sized head and tail excerpts**, insert the number of omitted characters between them, and return truncation metadata.

Currently, the tool waits for the SDK result and returns `exit_code`, `stdout`, and `stderr` unchanged. It has no tool-level output limit, truncation metadata, or full-output file reference. The SDK's `ExecutionResult` has no output-file reference either. The existing `download_file` tool reads files already present in the sandbox; it does not automatically save command output and currently reads the whole file.

Proposed behavior:

1. **Bound output by default.** Use a configurable, combined 30,000-character budget for stdout and stderr. Leave short output unchanged. Count Unicode code points and include omission markers in the budget. This bounds the returned output text, not model tokens or the complete serialized MCP response.
2. **Keep the beginning and end.** Preserve stdout and stderr as separate fields, allocate the shared budget between them, and redistribute unused capacity. When a stream exceeds its allocation, reserve space for a marker such as `[... N characters omitted ...]`, then divide the remaining space equally between its beginning and end.
3. **Report truncation explicitly.** Return each stream's original character count and whether it was truncated. Calculate the omitted count from the original characters actually removed. Preserve the command's exit code; truncation alone should not turn the result into a tool error.

**Optional follow-up:** Save full output and return a readable file path. Storage location, retrieval, and cleanup would be designed separately and are outside this initial change.

I'd like to agree on the default budget, excerpt behavior, and compatibility approach before implementation. Enabling truncation by default changes existing callers' returned text, and the metadata extends the response schema.

Truncation would happen after the SDK has received the complete result, so it would not reduce peak memory used to capture command output. Runtime-level output limits can be handled separately.

### Why is this needed?

Agents use `execute_command` to install dependencies, build projects, and run tests. These commands can produce enough output to overwhelm a tool response and consume a large share of the model's context. Silently cutting that output can also make a partial result look complete.

A default budget works even when the caller does not request a limit. Head-and-tail excerpts retain both initial context and final diagnostics, while omission markers and metadata make the missing content explicit.

Validation should cover:

- Unchanged short output; oversized output fits the combined budget and retains the correct head and tail with accurate omission counts.
- Allocation between stdout and stderr, empty streams, Unicode, marker overhead, and custom-budget boundaries.
- Preserved nonzero exit codes and exactly one execution of the original command.
- Consistent FastMCP results, tool descriptions, and README documentation.

Current implementation:

- [execute_command](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/blob/29852c834d7be2547ac219e6ac11ea1edebbcac2/clients/integrations/mcp-server/k8s_agent_sandbox_mcp_server/tools/execute_command.py)
- [SDK ExecutionResult](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/blob/29852c834d7be2547ac219e6ac11ea1edebbcac2/clients/python/agentic-sandbox-client/k8s_agent_sandbox/models.py#L28)
- [download_file](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/blob/29852c834d7be2547ac219e6ac11ea1edebbcac2/clients/integrations/mcp-server/k8s_agent_sandbox_mcp_server/tools/download_file.py)

The issue also asks for maintainers to agree on the default budget and the response-schema change before implementation.
