issues.title: sandboxd: as PID 1 it does not reap orphaned processes, so zombies accumulate for the sandbox's lifetime
issues.body:
### What happened

`sandboxd` runs as PID 1 in the sandbox container (`ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/sandboxd"]` in `packages/sandboxd/Dockerfile`), but it does not reap orphaned processes. Any process re-parented to PID 1 stays `<defunct>` for the life of the sandbox.

`sandboxd` does reap its own direct children: 50 plain `exec` calls left no zombies. The leak is grandchildren whose parent exits or is killed first: a killed process group, a double-forked daemon, a shell that backgrounds work and exits.

### Reproduction (v1.0.7, GKE Sandbox / gVisor, warm-pool claim)

1. Through the exec API, start a tree (`sh` → children → grandchildren, including a double-forked `sleep`) and kill the tree's process group, or let the parent shell exit first.
2. In a fresh exec, run `ps -eo pid,ppid,stat,comm | awk '$3 ~ /Z/'`.

Observed output (abridged; 51 zombies after one probe run, all with PPID 1):

```
   45     1 Z    [sleep] <defunct>
   53     1 Z    [sh] <defunct>
   55     1 Zs   [sleep] <defunct>
  130     1 Zs   [sh] <defunct>
  ...
```

Expected: PID 1 reaps adopted children, as an init does, so the count stays at 0.

### Impact

Each zombie holds a PID until the sandbox is deleted. A long-lived or reused sandbox that runs test suites (which routinely spawn and kill process trees) accumulates them, and eventually hits `pid_max` or a pids cgroup limit, at which point `fork` fails inside the sandbox.

### Possible fixes

- Make `sandboxd` reap adopted children when it is PID 1: a `SIGCHLD` handler that calls `wait4(-1, WNOHANG)`, coordinated with `os/exec` so it does not steal the exit status of processes `sandboxd` itself started (the usual approach is to reap only PIDs it is not tracking).
- Or ship the image with a minimal init (for example `tini` or `catatonit`) as PID 1 in front of `sandboxd`, and document it.
- Meanwhile, documenting `shareProcessNamespace: true` (so the pause container reaps) as a workaround would help users who cannot rebuild the image.

I found no existing reaping code in `packages/sandboxd` on `main`, and no open issue covering this.
issues.triage_reason: Needs a design choice between an in-process reaper in packages/sandboxd/cmd/sandboxd/main.go (which must coordinate with cmd.Wait in pkg/server/process.go) and adding tini to the Dockerfile. The reaper is racy and hard to unit test.

issues.title: A connection reset after the 200 headers fails the request, but a truncated body is re-sent once
issues.body:
### OpenCodeReview Version

v1.12.11 (a758d9c) linux/amd64. Also reproduced on main at 375f64c.

### Operating System

Linux (x86_64)

### Installation Method

npm (global)

### LLM Provider

Other OpenAI-compatible endpoint

### Bug Description

When the TCP connection is reset after the provider has sent the 200 response headers, `OpenAIClient.CompletionsWithCtx` returns the error at once and does not re-send the request. The request is non-streaming. In review, the group then fails in round 1 and all of its files go to `failed` coverage.

OCR already recovers from two failures that are close to this one:

- If the server closes the connection with a FIN, the SDK returns `io.ErrUnexpectedEOF`, and the recovery from #670 re-sends the request once (`internal/llm/client.go:713` at v1.12.11, `:723` on main).
- If the reset comes before the headers, the openai-go retry loop retries it, because `shouldRetry` returns true when there is no response.

A reset after the headers falls between these two cases. openai-go reads the body after its retry loop (`internal/requestconfig/requestconfig.go:676` in v3.51.0), and the OCR recovery matches only `io.ErrUnexpectedEOF`.

The retry report also records the failed attempt as a success: the attempt shows `outcome: success` and `status_code: 200`, and the request shows `outcome: failed`. The cause is that `classifyBoundaryError` (`internal/llm/retry_boundary.go:45-63`) does not recognize a `*net.OpError`. One acceptance criterion of #785 is that failures after a 200 are not recorded as successful attempts.

On HTTP/2 the effect is larger. All concurrent requests share one connection, so one reset fails every group that is waiting for a response.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Save this test as `internal/llm/reset_test.go`:

```go
package llm

import (
	"bufio"
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"sync/atomic"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

func TestBodyCutAfterHeaders(t *testing.T) {
	const body = `{"id":"c","object":"chat.completion","model":"m","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"ok"},"finish_reason":"stop"}]}`
	for _, cut := range []string{"fin", "rst"} {
		t.Run(cut, func(t *testing.T) {
			ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			defer ln.Close()
			var requests atomic.Int32
			go func() {
				for {
					conn, err := ln.Accept()
					if err != nil {
						return
					}
					go func(conn net.Conn) {
						defer conn.Close()
						req, err := http.ReadRequest(bufio.NewReader(conn))
						if err != nil {
							return
						}
						_, _ = io.Copy(io.Discard, req.Body)
						fmt.Fprintf(conn, "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: %d\r\n\r\n", len(body))
						if requests.Add(1) > 1 {
							fmt.Fprint(conn, body)
							return
						}
						fmt.Fprint(conn, body[:20])
						time.Sleep(300 * time.Millisecond)
						if cut == "rst" {
							_ = conn.(*net.TCPConn).SetLinger(0)
						}
					}(conn)
				}
			}()
			client := NewOpenAIClient(ClientConfig{URL: "http://" + ln.Addr().String() + "/v1", APIKey: "k", Model: "m"})
			_, err = client.CompletionsWithCtx(context.Background(), ChatRequest{Messages: []Message{{Role: "user", Content: "ping"}}})
			t.Logf("%s: requests=%d err=%v", cut, requests.Load(), err)
		})
	}
}
```

2. Run `go test ./internal/llm -run TestBodyCutAfterHeaders -v`.
3. The output is the same on v1.12.11 and on main:

```
fin: requests=2 err=<nil>
rst: requests=1 err=error reading response body: read tcp 127.0.0.1:45952->127.0.0.1:33543: read: connection reset by peer
```

Streaming does not avoid the problem. With `extra_body.stream: true`, a FIN or a reset after the stream opens is not re-sent either. This issue does not ask to change the streaming path.

### Expected Behavior

A transport error while reading a 2xx body gets the same single re-send as `io.ErrUnexpectedEOF`, and the retry report records the first attempt as `network` / `response_decode`.

A possible change that keeps the current rules:

- Widen the condition at `client.go:713` so that it also matches a transport error from the body read, using error types and the status only. For example, capture the response with `option.WithResponseInto`, require a 2xx status, and exclude context errors and JSON decode errors. A narrower form is `errors.As(err, &opErr)` with `*net.OpError`.
- Keep the rest of the recovery unchanged: one re-send only, the `ctx.Err()` checks, and `reviseAttempt(..., ErrorClassNetwork, FailurePhaseResponseDecode)` before the re-send. The request then counts as retried, and `Finalize` still runs once.
- Add the same type to `classifyBoundaryError`, so that a reset on the re-send is recorded as an error attempt and not as a success.
- Context errors stay excluded, so the documented rule does not change: "An expired per-request deadline ends the call without automatically replaying it".
- Scope: non-streaming Chat Completions only, the same scope as #670. The Anthropic and Responses clients have no EOF recovery either, and this issue leaves them out.

### Logs / Error Output

```
[ocr] Subtask error for group "<group A>": LLM completion error: error reading response body: read tcp <local>-><provider>:443: read: connection reset by peer
[ocr] Subtask error for group "<group B>": LLM completion error: error reading response body: read tcp <local>-><provider>:443: read: connection reset by peer
Error: review failed: all N file review(s) failed — check your LLM configuration and API key
```

In the retry report, each failed request shows one attempt that is recorded as a success:

```json
{"outcome": "failed", "attempts": [{"attempt": 1, "outcome": "success", "status_code": 200}]}
```

In the same event, a request whose headers had not arrived yet failed in the `transport` phase, and the SDK retried it with success. On the same reset, timing alone decides whether a request recovers or fails.

### AI/LLM Disclosure

- [ ] I didn't use AI/LLM to assist or generate the content above.
- [x] I actually used Claude Code to read the code, write and run the reproduction, and draft this text. I reviewed the result, understand it and can explain it.

### Additional Context

- The resets come from the provider side, on connections that are in use, so they are not idle timeouts. They are not frequent, but each one fails every group in flight, and the only recovery is a full new run.
- Cost: a provider can bill a non-streaming request even when the client disconnects, so the re-send costs one more turn. Today the same reset costs the whole group.
- Related: #664 and #670 (EOF recovery), #785 (retry report), #1635 and #1646 (group retry on a deadline only), #1717 (a stalled body, a different signature).
- Alternatives considered:
  1. A fix in openai-go. The body read is outside its retry loop in v3.51.0 and in the current release, and anthropic-sdk-go v1.63.1 has the same structure. #670 already put this recovery at the OCR client boundary.
  2. A group-level retry such as #1646. It replays the whole conversation, which costs much more than one turn.
  3. `stream: true`. The streaming path does not re-send either.
issues.triage_reason: Widen the io.ErrUnexpectedEOF recovery in OpenAIClient.CompletionsWithCtx (internal/llm/client.go ~723) and classifyBoundaryError (internal/llm/retry_boundary.go) to also match *net.OpError (excluding context errors), with tests based on the issue's repro; small, with a clear spec and a minor design choice.
issues.feedback:
Attempt 1:
Reviewer rejected (the test must be rewritten):
- isBodyReadNetError never excludes context errors, although the issue and the documented rule ("An expired per-request deadline ends the call without automatically replaying it") require that. The code relies only on the later parent ctx.Err() check. An SDK-internal per-request timeout (WithRequestTimeout) or a read-deadline failure wrapped in a *net.OpError would still be re-sent, because the parent context is not expired. Add an explicit errors.Is(err, context.Canceled/DeadlineExceeded) exclusion in isBodyReadNetError, and a unit test case for it.
- The tests do not verify the retry-report behaviour the issue asks for. The reset regression test never uses a retry collector, so it does not check that the first attempt is revised to network/response_decode or that the request counts as retried. Nothing checks that a reset on the re-send is recorded as an error attempt and not as a success. TestClassifyBoundaryError_NetOpError only covers the classifier in isolation. Add an end-to-end test with a retry collector that covers both the first attempt and a second reset.
issues.summary: Re-send a non-streaming OpenAI completion once when reading a 2xx body fails with a *net.OpError (e.g. connection reset), excluding context errors; revise the attempt to network/response_decode and classify net.OpError in classifyBoundaryError so a reset on the re-send is recorded as an error attempt. Added unit tests for the helper.
issues.pr_title: fix(llm): re-send completion once on net error after 200 headers
issues.pr_body:
Fixes #1789

## Description

A non-streaming OpenAI completion now gets one re-send when reading a 2xx response body fails with a `*net.OpError`, such as a connection reset by peer. Before this change, only `io.ErrUnexpectedEOF` was re-sent, so a reset after the headers failed the request at once.

- The re-send follows the same rules as the existing EOF recovery. It happens once only, the `ctx.Err()` checks stay, and the first attempt is revised to `network` / `response_decode`.
- Context errors are excluded, so an expired deadline still ends the call without a replay.
- `classifyBoundaryError` now recognizes `*net.OpError`. A reset on the re-send is recorded as an error attempt and not as a success.
- Scope is non-streaming Chat Completions only. The streaming, Anthropic and Responses paths are unchanged.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] CI / Build / Tooling

## How Has This Been Tested?

Added tests in `internal/llm`:

- `TestIsBodyReadNetError` (`body_read_error_test.go`) covers the new helper.
- `TestBoundaryRecoversConnectionResetAfterHeaders` checks that a reset after the 200 headers is re-sent once and the request succeeds.
- `TestBoundaryRecordsSecondConnectionResetAsError` checks that a reset on the re-send is recorded as an error attempt.
- `TestClassifyBoundaryErrorNetOpError` covers the new classification.

- [x] `make test` passes locally
- [ ] Manual testing (describe below)

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project's coding style (`go fmt`, `go vet`)
- [ ] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes
- [ ] I have updated the documentation accordingly (if applicable)
- [ ] I have signed the CLA
- [ ] I did not use AI/LLM to create this PR, or I disclosed the tool/model below and reviewed its output; I did not attribute commits to AI and will answer maintainer questions and review comments myself without AI/LLM.

issues.title: agentanalytics: terminal rows still misreported in some cases after #1787
issues.body:
After [#1787](https://github.com/google/adk-go/pull/1787), the BigQuery Agent Analytics plugin still writes the wrong terminal row in these cases. Some of them can't be fixed without a runner-level error signal (the issue about `AfterRunCallback`), and for those the fix here is to list them as known limitations in the `popUnclosedAgentSpans` doc comment.

- **First streamed chunk rejected.** An agent-level `AfterModelCallback` rejects the first streamed chunk that has content, and the run ends `INVOCATION_COMPLETED` although `runner.Run` yielded the error. `afterModel` marks the call as streamed and the agent as responded before agent callbacks have accepted the chunk ([bigquery_agent_analytics_plugin.go#L743-L756](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/947395cd8aee3ea228cf8deb00371a987eb9a84c/plugin/agentanalytics/bigquery_agent_analytics_plugin.go#L743-L756), [trace_manager.go#L1478-L1510](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/947395cd8aee3ea228cf8deb00371a987eb9a84c/plugin/agentanalytics/trace_manager.go#L1478-L1510)). Rejecting a later chunk falls into a class the code already documents as undetectable. The first chunk does not.
- **The partial-event flag covers the whole invocation.** `lastEventPartial` is one flag for the whole invocation, and it turns off the failure checks for every activation ([trace_manager.go#L193-L197](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/947395cd8aee3ea228cf8deb00371a987eb9a84c/plugin/agentanalytics/trace_manager.go#L193-L197), [#L1330](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/947395cd8aee3ea228cf8deb00371a987eb9a84c/plugin/agentanalytics/trace_manager.go#L1330)). Example: a custom root yields a partial event, then runs a sub-agent whose `BeforeModelCallback` fails. When the caller stops at that error the run ends `INVOCATION_COMPLETED`. Before the last two commits of [#1787](https://github.com/google/adk-go/pull/1787) it ended `INVOCATION_ERROR`.
- **Errors that ADK handles internally still fail the run.** A model error that the framework handles itself still ends the run `INVOCATION_ERROR` while `runner.Run` yields nothing. Two examples, neither reproduced yet:
  - a `ModeSingleTurn` agent installed as a tool, whose failure becomes a function response ([base_flow.go#L1606-L1607](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/c7ed87daa909e7563d3167e57daedee55f557d91/internal/llminternal/base_flow.go#L1606-L1607));
  - a workflow node retried by `RetryConfig` that then succeeds ([scheduler.go#L869](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/c7ed87daa909e7563d3167e57daedee55f557d91/workflow/scheduler.go#L869)).

  Errors recorded for a retired activation are never cleared ([trace_manager.go#L187-L191](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/947395cd8aee3ea228cf8deb00371a987eb9a84c/plugin/agentanalytics/trace_manager.go#L187-L191)).
- **A failed custom child under a sequential root.** When a sequential root runs a custom child whose Run yields an error and no events, and the caller reads to the end, the run ends `INVOCATION_COMPLETED` ([trace_manager.go#L1069-L1097](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/947395cd8aee3ea228cf8deb00371a987eb9a84c/plugin/agentanalytics/trace_manager.go#L1069-L1097)).
- **Parallel root stopped mid-stream.** The caller stops partway through a stream while a sibling's model call is in flight. When cancelled, a real model returns the context error, so the run ends `INVOCATION_ERROR` "context canceled", with `AGENT_ERROR` rows for the sibling and the parallel agent. The parallel case of `TestRunner_StopReadingMidStream_IsNotAnError` passes only because its fake model returns silently on cancellation ([trace_manager_test.go#L5500-L5512](https://github.com/google/adk-go/blob/947395cd8aee3ea228cf8deb00371a987eb9a84c/plugin/agentanalytics/trace_manager_test.go#L5500-L5512)).

Each case should either report the right row, with a test that goes through `runner.Run`, or be listed as a known limitation.
issues.triage_reason: Five separate misreporting cases in plugin/agentanalytics/trace_manager.go (popUnclosedAgentSpans, lastEventPartial, afterModel) that need subtle state-machine changes and runner.Run tests, some not yet reproduced; only the doc-comment limitation part is small and clear.

issues.title: Runner.Run does not resume direct WorkflowAgent graph root after RequestInput interrupt with native join
issues.body:
### Summary `Runner.Run` does not resume a direct `WorkflowAgent` graph root after a `RequestInput` interrupt when the workflow uses a native join. Supplying the matching `FunctionResponse` on a subsequent `Runner.Run` resolves nothing at the workflow level: the prior child agent is selected instead of the root, `Workflow.Resume` at the root is never reached, the native join never reevaluates, and downstream nodes never execute. ### Versions Reproduced on `google.golang.org/adk/v2` **v2.1.0** and **v2.3.0**. The reproduction module below pins v2.3.0. ### Reproduction Graph (fake agents, no models, no network): ```text B ----\ → join → D C ----/ ``` `b` interrupts with `RequestInput`, `c` completes normally, `d` should run after the join once `b` is resumed. ```bash cd /tmp/adk_root_repro # module adk-root-repro, requires adk/v2 v2.3.0 GOCACHE=/tmp/digital-garden-gocache \ go test -run TestRunnerResumeDoesNotResumeGraphRoot -count=1 -v ```
main_test.go (self-contained; only ADK + genai deps) ```go package repro import ( "context" "iter" "testing" "google.golang.org/adk/v2/agent" "google.golang.org/adk/v2/agent/workflowagent" "google.golang.org/adk/v2/model" "google.golang.org/adk/v2/runner" "google.golang.org/adk/v2/session" "google.golang.org/adk/v2/workflow" "google.golang.org/genai" ) func scripted(name, output string, interrupt bool) agent.Agent { a, err := agent.New(agent.Config{Name: name, Run: func(ctx agent.InvocationContext) iter.Seq2[*session.Event, error] { return func(yield func(*session.Event, error) bool) { if interrupt { if _, ok := workflow.ResumeOrRequestInput(agent.Promote(ctx), func(ev *session.Event) error { yield(ev, nil); return nil }, session.RequestInput{InterruptID: name, Message: "approve"}); ok != nil { return } yield(&session.Event{LLMResponse: model.LLMResponse{Content: genai.NewContentFromText(output, genai.RoleModel)}}, nil) return } ev := session.NewEvent(ctx, ctx.InvocationID()) ev.Content = genai.NewContentFromText(output, genai.RoleModel) yield(ev, nil) } }}) if err != nil { panic(err) } return a } func TestRunnerResumeDoesNotResumeGraphRoot(t *testing.T) { b := scripted("b", "B", true) c := scripted("c", "C", false) d := scripted("d", "D", false) bNode, _ := workflow.NewAgentNode(b, workflow.NodeConfig{}) cNode, _ := workflow.NewAgentNode(c, workflow.NodeConfig{}) dNode, _ := workflow.NewAgentNode(d, workflow.NodeConfig{}) join := workflow.NewJoinNode("join") root, err := workflowagent.New(workflowagent.Config{Name: "root", SubAgents: []agent.Agent{b, c, d}, Edges: []workflow.Edge{ {From: workflow.Start, To: bNode}, {From: workflow.Start, To: cNode}, {From: bNode, To: join}, {From: cNode, To: join}, {From: join, To: dNode}, }}) if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) } svc := session.InMemoryService() r, err := runner.New(runner.Config{AppName: "repro", Agent: root, SessionService: svc, AutoCreateSession: true}) if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) } ctx := context.Background() for ev, err := range r.Run(ctx, "u", "s", genai.NewContentFromText("start", genai.RoleUser), agent.RunConfig{}) { if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) } } msg := genai.NewContentFromFunctionResponse(workflow.WorkflowInputFunctionCallName, map[string]any{"response": "approved"}, genai.RoleUser) var sawD bool for ev, err := range r.Run(ctx, "u", "s", msg, agent.RunConfig{}) { if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) } if ev.Author == "d" { sawD = true } } if !sawD { t.Fatal("D never executed; workflow root was not resumed after RequestInput") } } ```
Actual session history after the resume turn (from the test log): ```text before resume author=c ... waiting= before resume author=b ... waiting=&{b approve } after resume author=c ... waiting= after resume author=b ... waiting=&{b approve } # still waiting; nothing resolved ``` No event authored by `d` is ever produced. ### Expected vs actual Expected: the workflow root receives the `FunctionResponse`, `Workflow.Resume` resolves `b`, `b`'s output is forwarded, the native join reevaluates, and `d` executes. Actual: `Runner.Run` selects the prior child agent, the workflow root is bypassed, `Workflow.Resume` at the root is not reached, the native graph frontier does not advance, and `d` never executes. ### Second failing shape A multiple-wait diamond also fails: ```text A / \ B C ``` `b` and `c` both enter waiting state; resuming `b` does not correctly preserve/return the remaining `c` continuation through the expected root workflow path. (Reported from the same investigation; the attached module covers the join case above.) ### Observations (v2.1.0 line refs; same shape verified in v2.3.0) - `workflow/workflow.go:281` — `Workflow.Run` - `workflow/workflow.go:309` — `Workflow.RunNode` - `agent/workflowagent/workflow.go:96` — workflow-agent dispatch - `runner/runner.go:181` — `Runner.Run` - `runner/run_node.go:132` — state reconstruction / resume selection - `workflow/scheduler.go:822` — waiting/completion transition - `workflow/scheduler.go:855` — successor scheduling - `runner/runner.go:704-736` — `findAgentToRun` - `runner/runner.go:706-712` — `FunctionResponse`-associated event selects an agent - `agent/workflowagent/workflow.go:96-110` — `Workflow.Resume` dispatch - `agent/workflowagent/workflow.go:125-155` — `detectResume` Concretely, in v2.3.0 `runner/runner.go:1133` (`findAgentToRun`), `handleUserFunctionCallResponse` matches the `FunctionResponse` to `b`'s event and then `r.rootAgent.FindAgent(event.Author)` returns the child agent directly — so the root `WorkflowAgent` (and therefore `detectResume` → `Workflow.Resume`) is bypassed on the resume turn. ### Related work - Issue #1125 - PR #1129 — fixes a related nested-`WorkflowAgent` HITL resume problem in `runner/agent_node.go`, but does not fix this direct workflow-root graph/join case. ### Possible fix area (not guaranteed) Runner resume dispatch could detect when a `FunctionResponse` resolves a pending `RequestInput` owned by a workflow root/node, route the turn back through the root `WorkflowAgent`, preserve the current `FunctionResponse` input, let `workflowagent.detectResume` invoke `Workflow.Resume`, and retain unmatched pending waits/native join state. This is a suggested area to look, not a confirmed fix.
issues.triage_reason: Root cause is in runner/runner.go findAgentToRun, which returns the child agent instead of the workflow root, bypassing workflowagent detectResume/Workflow.Resume. Routing to the root is a small edit, but it risks regressing existing HITL paths in a high-fan-in package, and whether Workflow.Resume then restores join state correctly is unverified.

issues.title: Policy reported `Attached=False/Overridden` when it is only overridden on some of a Gateway's listeners
issues.body:
### kgateway version
main (`84b2d092e6`)

### Describe the bug
A policy can apply to several filter chains under one ancestor, for example a Gateway-wide ListenerPolicy on a Gateway with several HTTPS or TLS listeners. kgateway combines the per-chain attachment results into a single condition for that ancestor. If a `sectionName`-targeted policy overrides the gateway-wide one on some listeners, the gateway-wide policy is reported as:

```yaml
- type: Attached
  status: "False"
  reason: Overridden
  message: Overridden due to conflict with higher priority policy in target(s)
```

That happens even though it is still applied, unchanged, to the other listeners. Users reading status conclude the policy has no effect, when it's actually live on part of the Gateway.

Cause: `AncestorRefReport.SetAttachmentState` combines per-chain states with a bitwise OR (`pkg/reports/policy.go:43`). `addAttachmentCondition` (`pkg/reports/policy.go:254`) then checks `Overridden` before `Merged` and `Attached`, so one overridden chain hides every chain where the policy is attached.

### Expected behavior
A policy that is applied on at least one chain and overridden on another should report `Attached=True, reason: Merged` ("partially applied"), not `Attached=False`. `Attached=False/Overridden` should mean the policy is overridden everywhere under that ancestor.

### Steps to reproduce the bug
The existing translator golden test already shows it: `TestBasic` → "ListenerPolicy with per-listener transport socket connect timeout override".

- Input: `pkg/kgateway/translator/gateway/testutils/inputs/listener-policy/transport-socket-connect-timeout-per-listener.yaml`
  - Gateway with 3 HTTPS listeners on 8443 (tenant-a, tenant-b, tenant-c)
  - ListenerPolicy `gateway-wide`: `transportSocketConnectTimeout: 5s`
  - ListenerPolicies `tenant-a-override` (10s) and `tenant-b-override` (15s), targeted with `sectionName`
- Output (`outputs/listener-policy/transport-socket-connect-timeout-per-listener.yaml`):
  - The tenant-c filter chain has `transportSocketConnectTimeout: 5s`, which comes from `gateway-wide`.
  - `ListenerPolicy/default/gateway-wide` still reports `Attached=False, reason: Overridden`.

### Additional context
- This isn't specific to ListenerPolicy or to `transportSocketConnectTimeout`. Any policy merged per filter chain under a shared ancestor can hit it.
- A likely fix is in `addAttachmentCondition`: treat `Overridden` combined with `Attached` or `Merged` as `Merged`, and report `Overridden` only when it is the only bit set. The golden above, and any others showing `Overridden` for a partially applied policy, would need refreshing with `REFRESH_GOLDEN=true`.
- Found while reviewing #14859, which adds the same pattern for TCP/TLS listeners (`transport-socket-connect-timeout-tls-listener.yaml`).
issues.triage_reason: Reorder/adjust the switch in addAttachmentCondition (pkg/reports/policy.go) so Overridden combined with Attached/Merged reports Merged, then refresh affected translator goldens such as listener-policy/transport-socket-connect-timeout-per-listener.yaml; the golden diffs need checking.
issues.summary: addAttachmentCondition now reports Attached=True/Merged when Overridden is combined with Attached or Merged; Overridden only when it is the sole state. Refreshed affected translator goldens.
issues.pr_title: fix(reports): report Merged when a policy is only partly overridden
issues.pr_body:
# Description

Fixes #14861

A policy can apply to several filter chains under one ancestor, for example a Gateway-wide ListenerPolicy on a Gateway with several HTTPS listeners. The per-chain attachment states are combined into one condition. If a `sectionName`-targeted policy overrode the Gateway-wide one on some listeners, the Gateway-wide policy was reported as `Attached=False, reason: Overridden`, even though it was still applied on the other listeners.

`addAttachmentCondition` in `pkg/reports/policy.go` checked `Overridden` before `Merged` and `Attached`. It now reports `Attached=True, reason: Merged` when `Overridden` is combined with `Attached` or `Merged`. It reports `Overridden` only when that is the only state set.

The translator golden outputs that showed `Overridden` for a partly applied policy were refreshed with `REFRESH_GOLDEN=true`. These include `listener-policy/transport-socket-connect-timeout-per-listener.yaml` and several traffic-policy and delegation outputs.

Testing: added `TestAddAttachmentConditionPartiallyOverriddenReportsMerged` in `pkg/reports/policy_test.go`. It and the existing translator golden tests pass, along with the project's checks.

# Change Type

/kind fix

# Changelog

```release-note
Fix policy status reporting `Attached=False/Overridden` when the policy is overridden on only some of a Gateway's listeners. It now reports `Attached=True/Merged`.
```

# Additional Notes

None.

Điều này gây nhầm lẫn cho người dùng, nên tôi muốn trạng thái khớp với thực tế."},{"en":"The bug was small and clear, in one function, and it had a golden test that showed it. I thought I could fix it safely and make sure it does not come back.","vi":"Lỗi nhỏ và rõ ràng, nằm trong một hàm, và đã có golden test cho thấy lỗi. Tôi nghĩ mình có thể sửa an toàn và đảm bảo lỗi không quay lại."}]

issues.title: Decide whether SandboxTemplate metadata changes should reach claimed Sandboxes
issues.body:
Discovered while reviewing #1976. For a bound SandboxClaim, `reconcileActive` re-merges the current SandboxTemplate's `podTemplate.metadata` into the Sandbox on every reconcile ([sandboxclaim_controller.go#L609-L664](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/blob/70f0bdde88ab63d07c3537d4a43c528aab185141/extensions/controllers/sandboxclaim_controller.go#L609-L664)). Template updates don't enqueue bound claims (#1315, #1245), so template label/annotation edits reach claimed Pods only when the claim next reconciles for an unrelated reason. Template spec changes never reach them.

This came from the KEP-0174 implementation rather than a design decision, and it isn't tested. No user has reported problems, so for now #1976 doesn't document it. If someone hits this, decide whether claimed Sandboxes should stop picking up template metadata after binding, or whether template updates should propagate on purpose (note that the latter comes with performance impact).
issues.triage_reason: The issue asks for a maintainer design decision on whether reconcileActive in extensions/controllers/sandboxclaim_controller.go should keep merging SandboxTemplate podTemplate.metadata after a claim is bound. Either choice is a behavior change, and there is no user report to guide it.

issues.title: grok, commandcode, kimi and kiro readers still read each JSONL line whole
issues.body: Follow-on from #5414 (PR #5420), which moved the Claude path and `codexRoledBefore` onto `readLineBytes` in internal/sources/jsonl_stream.go: a 100 MB Claude tool-output line went from 925 MB to 36 MB peak RSS. The Grok, Command Code, Kimi and Kiro line readers still call `ReadBytes`, so one huge line there is held whole. Expected: they read through `readLineBytes`, with a test that a 16 MB line costs about what a 4 MB one does (compare the two, don't pin a limit; see `TestScanJSONLBytesHoldsALongLineByItsCut`).
issues.triage_reason: Replace ReadBytes with readLineBytes in grok.go (two loops) and commandcode.go:240; kimi and kiro already use scanJSONLFromOffset. Add 4 MB vs 16 MB allocation-comparison tests modelled on TestScanJSONLBytesHoldsALongLineByItsCut, which needs some judgement on fixtures and on the Grok substring prefilters.

issues.title: with DEJA_EXCLUDE_HARNESSES set, the patterns count and deja sources name the wrong cause
issues.body:
Two small wrong labels left after #5394 (PR #5400):
- cmd/deja/main.go around line 3746: the "N project patterns excluded" count subtracts harnesses excluded through `DEJA_EXCLUDE_HARNESSES`, so it miscounts when the env var is set.
- `deja sources`: the row of a store excluded through the env var names the exclude file as the reason.

Expected: the count covers project patterns only, and the sources row says `DEJA_EXCLUDE_HARNESSES` when that is what excluded it. Add a test for each.
issues.triage_reason: In cmd/deja/main.go, projectExcludePatterns subtracts env-excluded harnesses from the file pattern count, and the printSources excluded rows (~3961, ~4027) always name the exclude file; both are small, localized fixes testable with t.Setenv.
issues.feedback:
Attempt 1:
Reviewer rejected:
- The test's `deja sources` assertion is vacuous. It only checks lines that start with `claude\t`, and never fails if no such row is printed. The issue's second bug (the row naming the wrong cause) is therefore not reliably tested. Count matching rows and fail unless exactly one is found. It would also be stronger to assert the full `excluded — <cause>` text.
- The new exported functions `sources.ProjectPatternCount` and `sources.HarnessExcludedBy` are tested only from cmd/deja. internal/sources, which the change touches, gets no direct test. Add a table-driven test there that covers both functions with the exclude file, `DEJA_EXCLUDE_HARNESSES`, and both together.
- `HarnessExcludedBy` has a convoluted condition: it trims the prefix, compares, and then checks the prefix separately. Check `HasPrefix` first, then compare the trimmed name. The test also has no case where the file and the env var both exclude the same store, and no case for `DEJA_EXCLUDE_PROJECTS`.
issues.summary: Project-pattern count now counts only project patterns (sources.ProjectPatternCount), and `deja sources` names the real cause of an excluded store (sources.HarnessExcludedBy: exclude file line vs DEJA_EXCLUDE_HARNESSES). Added tests in cmd/deja (exactly-one-row, full 'excluded — cause' assertion) and internal/sources (file, env, both same store, DEJA_EXCLUDE_PROJECTS).
issues.pr_title: fix(sources): name the real cause of an excluded harness
issues.pr_body:
## Summary

Fixes #5401

Two labels were wrong when `DEJA_EXCLUDE_HARNESSES` is set:

- The "N project patterns excluded" count subtracted harnesses excluded through the env var. It now counts project patterns only (`sources.ProjectPatternCount`).
- `deja sources` named the exclude file as the reason for a store excluded through the env var. It now names the real cause: the exclude file line or `DEJA_EXCLUDE_HARNESSES` (`sources.HarnessExcludedBy`).

## Test plan

Added tests:

- `TestExcludeCauseIsNamedAndPatternsCountedApart` in `cmd/deja`. It checks that the store has exactly one row and that the row reads `excluded — <cause>`. It also checks the pattern count.
- `TestProjectPatternCountAndHarnessExcludedBy` in `internal/sources`. It covers the exclude file, the env var, both excluding the same store, and `DEJA_EXCLUDE_PROJECTS`.

The new tests and the project's checks pass.

## Notes

None.

issues.title: deja files and deja how say "in my/app only" for a project every other label calls proj/my-app
issues.body:
The scope line under `files` and `how` takes the first of `ProjectNameCandidates`, which is Claude's lossy encoded-dir name. For a directory with a hyphen it comes out as a name no row shows and `--project` does not accept.

```
$ cd ~/proj/my-app
$ deja files release
files touched while working on "release" — 2 sessions
  …/proj/my-app/notes.txt                               1 session
— in my/app only; `--all-projects` looks at every project
$ deja last
[claude] proj/my-app  Oct 17  bbbbbbbb-…000000000b  have a subagent write the release notes into …
$ deja files release --project my/app
No sessions mention "release" in project "my/app"
```

Control: the row labels' name works and the footer then repeats it:

```
$ deja files release --project proj/my-app
files touched while working on "release" — 2 sessions
  …/proj/my-app/notes.txt                               1 session
— in proj/my-app only; `--all-projects` looks at every project
```

Expected: the footer names the project the way the rows do, `proj/my-app`, a name `--project` takes. Actual: `my/app`.

Cause: `howScopeName` in cmd/deja/how.go:396 returns `scope[0]`, and `digest.ProjectNameCandidates` (internal/digest/digest.go:502) puts `sources.ClaudeProjectName(cwd)` first. The parent/base form it adds next is the one the labels use.

Where to start: change `howScopeName` to return the `parent/base` candidate (or `filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(cwd)) + "/" + filepath.Base(cwd)`) instead of the first entry; it also feeds the `Project` field of `--json` at cmd/deja/files.go:150, :299, :363. Copy the `captureRun(t, "files", ...)` pattern from `TestFilesPointsAtTheRecordsServedByRole` in cmd/deja/files_hint_test.go, with a store whose project dir has a hyphen, and assert the footer reads `in proj/my-app only`.
issues.triage_reason: Change howScopeName in cmd/deja/how.go to return the parent/base candidate from digest.ProjectNameCandidates, and add a table-driven test in cmd/deja/files_hint_test.go. The only judgement is keeping explicit --project scopes unchanged.

issues.title: Gemini --resume writes each tool result again, and deja shows and indexes it twice
issues.body:
On `--resume`, Gemini CLI 0.64 appends a `<turn id>_response` user record for every earlier tool call, carrying the same functionResponse (same call id) the original user record already holds. deja reads it as a new turn, so every tool output of a resumed session appears twice in `deja show` and is indexed twice.

Repro with a real 0.64 store from the harness (a parent session that made one write_file, then was resumed). Lines 9 and 14 of the chat file:

```
{"id":"f58871c3-…","timestamp":"2026-10-18T05:25:30.384Z","type":"user","content":[{"functionResponse":{"id":"write_file__write_file_1792301130300_0","name":"write_file",…}}]}
{"id":"33bd0ae1-…_response","timestamp":"2026-10-18T05:25:39.066Z","type":"user","content":[{"functionResponse":{"id":"write_file__write_file_1792301130300_0","name":"write_file",…}}]}
```

```
$ S=$(mktemp -d)
$ mkdir -p "$S/.gemini/tmp/proj-q/chats" && cp session-2026-10-18T05-25-ae2dcdfc.jsonl "$S/.gemini/tmp/proj-q/chats/"
$ HOME=$S XDG_CACHE_HOME=$S/.cache DEJA_INDEX_DIR=$S/.cache/deja DEJA_GEMINI_ROOT=$S/.gemini deja index
$ HOME=$S … deja show ae2dcdfc
Oct 18 08:25 +03:00 tool-output:
Successfully created and wrote to new file: …/proj-q/parent.txt. Here is the updated code:
PARENT_LINE QUOKKA7

Oct 18 08:25 +03:00 assistant:
Created `…/proj-q/parent.txt`.

Oct 18 08:25 +03:00 tool-output:
Successfully created and wrote to new file: …/proj-q/parent.txt. Here is the updated code:
PARENT_LINE QUOKKA7
$ HOME=$S … deja show ae2dcdfc | grep -c Successfully
2
```

Control: a session that was never resumed has no `_response` records and shows each output once. The exit-code path already handles the repeat: geminiNoteExits says "once: the result arrives on both records".

Expected: one tool-output per call id. Actual: one per record carrying it, so a session resumed N times repeats every earlier output N+1 times, and search counts the text that often.

Cause: internal/sources/gemini.go:327 appends any record with a new message id, and geminiWorkRecords (gemini.go:698) turns every functionResponse part into a tool-output without checking whether that call id was already answered.

Where to start: parseGeminiJSONLWith in internal/sources/gemini.go. Keep a set of functionResponse ids already seen and drop a repeated part (and a user record left empty by that) before appendGeminiMessages. TestParseGeminiJSONLWithRewind in internal/sources/gemini_test.go is the pattern: an inline JSONL with one write_file call, its user functionResponse, then a `<id>_response` record for the same call id; assert one RoleToolOutput.
issues.triage_reason: Dedup repeated functionResponse call ids in parseGeminiJSONLWith / appendGeminiMessages (internal/sources/gemini.go) and add a table-driven test modelled on TestParseGeminiJSONLWithRewind. The unread part is how raw content is filtered, and the snapshot/rewind interplay needs some care.

issues.title: pi: a resumed session that was compacted gets no digest when the compaction kept a per-prompt recall
issues.body:
The pi extension skips the start-of-session digest if the branch pi will send already holds a `deja-recall` message. The digest and the per-prompt recall share that customType, so after a compaction that dropped the digest but kept a later prompt recall, a resume gets no digest.

Reproduction (the check copied verbatim from the template into node, with the branch shapes pi writes):

```
$ node hr.mjs
compaction kept the prompt recall, not the digest: true
control, compaction kept neither:                false
```

Branch: digest `deja-recall` (a1), user message, prompt `deja-recall` (a3), user message, `compaction` with `firstKeptEntryId: "a3"`. pi sends the summary and a3 on; the digest is gone, but `holdsRecall` returns true at a3, so `before_agent_start` marks the session injected and never asks `hook-context`.

Expected: the digest is skipped only when the digest itself is among what pi sends. Actual: any deja message counts, so a compacted session resumes with no digest.

Cause: cmd/deja/install_pi.go:436 `holdsRecall` (and its twin `branchHoldsRecall`, extensions/pi/lib.mjs:76) match `customType === "deja-recall"`; both the digest (install_pi.go:565, extensions/pi/index.ts:190) and the prompt recall (install_pi.go:581, index.ts:206) are sent under it.

Where to start: mark the digest message, e.g. `details: { digest: true }` on the `hook-context` return, and have both checks look for that marker (falling back to the current rule for sessions written before it). The template and the package must stay in step (pi_package_parity_test.go). Add the branch above to `TestPiResumeAndForkGetNoSecondDigest` in cmd/deja/pi_resume_fork_test.go and to the `branchHoldsRecall` cases in extensions/pi/test/pure.test.mjs.

issues.title: uninstall leaves "./plugins/deja-status.tsx" in a commented tui.json after deleting the file it points to
issues.body:
With a commented `~/.config/opencode/tui.json`, deja won't edit the plugin list: install prints a note asking the user to add deja's status-line plugin, and uninstall deletes the plugin file and prints a note asking them to remove the entry. A user who followed the first note is left with a list entry pointing at a file that no longer exists.

Reproduction (sandbox HOME):

```
$ cat ~/.config/opencode/tui.json
{
  // my tui settings
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/tui.json",
  "theme": "tokyonight"
}
$ deja install opencode-auto --no-index --no-guidance
opencode-auto: updated ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json
               also created ~/.config/opencode/plugins/deja.js; also created ~/.config/opencode/plugins/deja-status.tsx — ~/.config/opencode/tui.json unchanged — add "./plugins/deja-status.tsx" to its plugin list to show deja's status line
# user adds  "plugin": ["./plugins/deja-status.tsx"]  as told
$ deja uninstall opencode-auto
opencode-auto: removed ~/.config/opencode/plugins/deja.js
               also removed ~/.config/opencode/plugins/deja-status.tsx — ~/.config/opencode/tui.json unchanged — remove "./plugins/deja-status.tsx" from its plugin list
$ cat ~/.config/opencode/tui.json
{
  // my tui settings
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/tui.json",
  "theme": "tokyonight",
  "plugin": ["./plugins/deja-status.tsx"]
}
$ ls ~/.config/opencode/plugins
ls: ~/.config/opencode/plugins: No such file or directory
```

Control: the same tui.json without the comment gets `"plugin": ["./plugins/deja-status.tsx"]` on install and comes back byte for byte on uninstall.

Expected: uninstall takes deja's entry out of the list as text and keeps the comment, as the other JSONC writers do. Actual: a note, and a dangling plugin path left for opencode to load at the next TUI start (what opencode does with the missing file is not checked here).

Cause: cmd/deja/install_opencode_tui.go:212 `installTUIPluginList` returns "unchanged" with a note for any commented file, because the only writer it has re-encodes the decoded object.

Where to start: in `installTUIPluginList`, for `commented && uninstall`, remove the string element from the `plugin` list span (`jsoncListValue`, cmd/deja/jsonc_entry.go:696) as text, and the `plugin` key with it when the list empties (`jsoncRemoveKey`). Copy `TestOpencodeAutoTakesACommentedTuiJSON` in cmd/deja/install_opencode_config_shapes_test.go and seed the commented file with deja's entry already listed. The element cutter is the one 25 needs; land them together.

issues.title: Clearing deja's hook from a commented Copilot settings.json drops the reader's comments inside that hook list
issues.triage_reason: In cmd/deja/install_copilot.go dropCopilotHooksJSONC, replace the json.Encoder re-encode with element-span cutting that reuses cutEntry and the jsoncListValue scanners, and extend TestClearingCopilotHooksKeepsTheReadersComment. Needs moderate care with commas and comments, but it is small and well specified.

issues.title: JSONC status-line round trip moves the reader's comment onto the opening brace
issues.body:
Installing and uninstalling deja's status line in a commented settings file doesn't give the file back: a line comment after the key deja replaced ends up on the `{` line, and a one-line block is reflowed.

Reproduction (sandbox HOME, Copilot's settings.json; no Copilot binary needed):

```
$ printf '{\n  "statusLine": null, // off until I pick one\n  "theme": "dark"\n}\n' > ~/.copilot/settings.json
$ deja install copilot-auto --no-index --no-guidance
copilot-auto: created ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json
              also created ~/.copilot/hooks/deja.json; also updated ~/.copilot/settings.json
$ deja uninstall copilot-auto
$ cat ~/.copilot/settings.json
{ // off until I pick one
  "theme": "dark"
}
```

Same with `"ui": { /* later */ }` and `ui.statusLine` (Qwen's shape): after the round trip it reads `"ui": {\n   /* later */ }`.

Control: a comment on its own line round-trips byte for byte (`{\n  // top\n  "a": 1\n  // bottom\n}\n` comes back unchanged; the "comment between the last two keys" row of TestAJSONCStatusLineRoundTripsEveryShape covers this).

Expected: the comment stays on the line it was on. Actual: it moves to the line of the object's brace, away from the key it described. Cosmetic, the file still parses. Dropping the `"statusLine": null` itself is intended and pinned by the "null under a comment" row of that test.

Cause: cmd/deja/jsonc_entry.go:206 `cutEntry` takes the newline and indent in front of the removed key along with it, so whatever trailed the key's line joins the line before. The install side (`jsoncSetEntry`, jsonc_entry.go:98) writes into a one-line block with a `"\n   "` tail that uninstall doesn't undo.

Where to start: `cutEntry` in cmd/deja/jsonc_entry.go. Add the two inputs above as rows to `TestAJSONCStatusLineRoundTripsEveryShape` in cmd/deja/install_copilot_jsonc_test.go (want = the input) and make them pass without breaking the existing rows.

issues.title: kimi-auto rewrites config.toml, then refuses a read-only tui.toml its pre-flight passed
issues.body:
The kimi-auto pre-flight accepts a file if it would be writable or unchanged under either the launcher path or the binary path. The writers then use the launcher. When the hooks name the binary (installed while ~/.config/deja/bin could not be written) and the launcher can now be written, the pre-flight passes on the binary, the writer moves config.toml to the launcher, and the read-only tui.toml is refused after that.

Reproduction (sandboxed HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$HOME/.config):

```
$ mkdir -p ~/.config/deja/bin && chmod 0555 ~/.config/deja/bin
$ deja install kimi-auto --no-index --no-guidance
kimi-auto: created ~/.kimi-code/mcp.json
           also created ~/.kimi-code/config.toml; also created ~/.kimi-code/tui.toml
$ chmod 755 ~/.config/deja/bin && chmod 0444 ~/.kimi-code/tui.toml
$ grep -c deja-hook ~/.kimi-code/config.toml
0
$ deja install kimi-auto --no-index --no-guidance
deja: install finished what it could; 1 target refused: kimi-auto: ~/.kimi-code/tui.toml is read-only, so deja left it as it was — check that path's permissions and run it again
$ grep -c deja-hook ~/.kimi-code/config.toml ~/.kimi-code/tui.toml
~/.kimi-code/config.toml:7
~/.kimi-code/tui.toml:0
```

Control, the same steps for grok-auto with ~/.grok/hooks/deja.json read-only: refused, and config.toml and user-settings.json keep their checksums. Grok's pre-flight asks `preflightHookExe` which path the writer will use instead of trying both.

Expected: refused before anything is written, as grok and cline do. Actual: config.toml hooks now run the launcher while the status line still runs the binary, and the target is reported refused.

Cause: `kimiAutoPreflight` (cmd/deja/install_auto.go:1355) checks `exes = []string{launcher, exe}` and stops at the first that passes, for both config.toml and tui.toml. `preflightHookExe` (cmd/deja/install_grok.go:155) is the shared answer to "which path will the writer name".

Where to start: in `kimiAutoPreflight`, replace the `exes` loops with one check against `preflightHookExe(exe)` (and plain `exe` on uninstall). Add a case to `TestKimiAutoRefusesAReadOnlyFileBeforeWriting` (cmd/deja/install_kimi_config_test.go:162): install with `dejaLauncherPath()`'s directory at 0555, open it, chmod tui.toml 0444, reinstall, and assert config.toml is unchanged.

issues.title: uninstall still deletes the reader's openclaw.json snapshot when their config names "deja" as a value: plugins.slots.memory
issues.body:
#5281 stopped uninstall from treating the reader's `"deja"` in a list (`plugins.allow`) as deja's wiring. A scalar value is still counted, so `"slots": {"memory": "deja"}` — OpenClaw's own way to pick deja as the memory plugin — makes the first uninstall write delete the snapshot, and the reader's one-line blocks come back split.

Reproduction (sandboxed HOME; the #5281 seed with a memory slot instead of the allow entry):

```
$ cat ~/seed.json
// user settings
{
  // top comment
  "agents": {"defaults": {"model": "anthropic/x"}},
  "plugins": {"allow": ["my-plugin"], "slots": {"memory": "deja"}, "entries": {"my-plugin": {"enabled": true}}, "load": {"paths": ["/opt/my-plugin"]}},
  "hooks": {"internal": {"enabled": true, "entries": {"session-memory": {"enabled": true}}}},
  "mcp": {"servers": {"zz-mine": {"command": "my-server"}}}
}
$ cp ~/seed.json ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json
$ deja install openclaw-auto --no-index --no-guidance
$ cmp ~/seed.json ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json.bak && echo bak==seed
bak==seed
$ deja uninstall openclaw-auto
$ ls ~/.openclaw
openclaw.json
$ diff ~/seed.json ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json
5,7c5,10
<   "plugins": {"allow": ["my-plugin"], "slots": {"memory": "deja"}, "entries": {"my-plugin": {"enabled": true}}, "load": {"paths": ["/opt/my-plugin"]}},
<   "hooks": {"internal": {"enabled": true, "entries": {"session-memory": {"enabled": true}}}},
<   "mcp": {"servers": {"zz-mine": {"command": "my-server"}}}
---
>   "plugins": {"allow": ["my-plugin"], "slots": {"memory": "deja"}, "entries": {
>    "my-plugin": {"enabled": true}}, "load": {"paths": ["/opt/my-plugin"]}},
>   "hooks": {"internal": {"enabled": true, "entries": {
>    "session-memory": {"enabled": true}}}},
>   "mcp": {"servers": {
>    "zz-mine": {"command": "my-server"}}}
```

Control: the same seed with `"allow": ["my-plugin", "deja"]` and no slot round-trips byte-exact and keeps openclaw.json.bak.

Expected: the reader's bytes back and their snapshot kept, as for the allow list. Actual: the snapshot is deleted and three blocks are reformatted. Content is the same.

Cause: `snapshotHoldsDejaWiring` (cmd/deja/install.go:1688) strips only list items through `withoutDejaListNames` (install.go:1700); a map value `"deja"` survives the re-marshal and matches the `"\"deja\""` marker in `mentionsDeja` (install.go:1821). Follow-on from #5281.

Where to start: in `withoutDejaListNames`, also drop map values that are the bare string "deja" (keys stay, since a key named deja is deja's entry). Add `{"memory slot naming deja", `{"plugins": {"slots": {"memory": "deja"}}}`, true}` to the table in `TestDropOwnBackupTellsTheReadersDejaFromDejas` (cmd/deja/install_snapshot_reader_deja_test.go), and run `TestEveryInstalledConfigIsRecognisableAsDejas` to make sure no target's own wiring relies on a scalar "deja" value to be recognised.

issues.title: Codex `cd sub && apply_patch` files the edit under the session's cwd: blame and files name a path that was never written
issues.body:
A Codex shell call `cd sub && apply_patch <<'EOF' ... *** Update File: parent.txt` edits sub/parent.txt. The reader resolves the patch header against the call's `workdir` or the session cwd and ignores the `cd`, so the files and wrote records say `/w/app/parent.txt`.

Repro: a throwaway test beside `TestCodexShellApplyPatchResolvesAgainstItsWorkdir` in internal/sources/codex_fork_context_test.go, two exec_command calls in one rollout with cwd /w/app: c1 is `cd sub && apply_patch <<'EOF' ... *** Update File: parent.txt ...`, c2 is the same patch without the `cd` and with `"workdir":"sub"`.

```
$ go test ./internal/sources -run TestZZTriageCdApplyPatch -v
    zz_triage_cd_test.go:25: files = "/w/app/parent.txt | /w/app/sub/parent.txt"
```

Control: c2 with `workdir` lands at /w/app/sub/parent.txt, as #5213 intended.

Expected: both calls file /w/app/sub/parent.txt. Actual: the `cd` form files /w/app/parent.txt, so `deja blame sub/parent.txt` finds no writer and a file of the same name at the root gets the credit.

Cause: internal/sources/codex.go:607-614 takes `dir` from cwd or workdir only. The hook does the same at cmd/deja/hook_tool.go:363 (applyPatchLine with the payload cwd), so the pre-edit file line looks up the wrong path too.

Where to start: codexCall in internal/sources/codex.go. Before the patch loop, take a leading `cd <dir> &&` (quoted or not) off in.Cmd and resolve it with resolveToolPath against dir. Copy TestCodexShellApplyPatchResolvesAgainstItsWorkdir and add a `cd sub && apply_patch` call; a `cd /abs && apply_patch` case covers the absolute form.

A Claude Task, a Qwen Code or Kimi Code agent, or a Cursor subagent writes ... skills/deja-search/SKILL.md:63:- Work a subagent did is in the index as its task, its answer and the edits it made, ... grep -c "goose's delegate runs" docs/guide/search.html 1 ``` Expected: the skill names the same harnesses as the guide.
