issues.title: cline uninstall deletes everything under ~/.cline/plugins/deja, including files deja never wrote
issues.body:
`deja uninstall cline-auto` removes the plugin directory with `os.RemoveAll`, so anything the user keeps there goes with deja's three files. On a read-only ~/.cline/plugins the same call empties the directory, then fails to unlink it and reports the target refused, with the plugin already gone.

Reproduction (sandboxed HOME):

```
$ deja install cline-auto --no-index --no-guidance
cline-auto: created ~/.cline/data/settings/cline_mcp_settings.json
            also created ~/.cline/plugins/deja/index.js — also created ~/.cline/plugins/deja
$ mkdir -p ~/.cline/plugins/deja/notes && echo mine > ~/.cline/plugins/deja/notes/todo.md
$ deja uninstall cline-auto
cline-auto: removed ~/.cline/plugins/deja/index.js
$ ls ~/.cline/plugins/deja
ls: ~/.cline/plugins/deja: No such file or directory
```

Read-only parent, same setup plus `chmod 0555 ~/.cline/plugins`:

```
$ deja uninstall cline-auto
deja: uninstall finished what it could; 1 target refused: cline-auto: unlinkat ~/.cline/plugins/deja: permission denied — check that path's permissions and run it again
$ find ~/.cline/plugins
~/.cline/plugins
~/.cline/plugins/deja
$ deja uninstall cline-auto
cline: not installed
cline-auto: not installed
```

Control: the other deja-owned plugin directories (goose recipe, command files) remove only deja's files and prune the directories deja recorded creating.

Expected: uninstall removes index.js, package.json and skills/deja-history/SKILL.md, then prunes the directories that are empty and recorded as deja's; notes/todo.md stays. On a read-only parent, either refuse before removing anything or leave an empty deja/ without calling it refused. Actual: the user's file is deleted, and on a read-only parent the plugin is removed while the run reports it refused.

Cause: `installClineAuto` (cmd/deja/install_cline.go:40) calls `os.RemoveAll(dir)` on ~/.cline/plugins/deja. The third part of the review note, doctor ignoring CLINE_GLOBAL_SETTINGS_PATH, is already fixed (cmd/deja/doctor_client_off.go:319).

Where to start: in `installClineAuto`'s uninstall branch, remove the three files by name, then `pruneCreatedDir` from skills/deja-history up to the plugins dir. Extend `TestInstallClineIsIdempotentAndRemovable` (cmd/deja/install_cline_test.go:67) with a user file under the plugin dir that must survive, and copy the chmod setup from `TestClineAutoRefusesAnUnwritablePluginDirBeforeWriting` (cmd/deja/install_cline_readonly_test.go:18) for the read-only case.

issues.title: kiro: after the deja binary moves, uninstall keeps deja's own steering text as deja.md.bak and calls it a config you already had
issues.body:
Files deja owns whole (Kiro's steering/deja.md, the Copilot Chat deja.prompt.md, the Kiro agent when it is still deja's shape) embed the binary path. A reinstall from a new path rewrites them, `writeIfChanged` snapshots deja's previous text as `.bak`, and uninstall removes the file but leaves the snapshot and reports it as the reader's.

Reproduction (sandboxed HOME; /tmp/hhtriage-bin2/deja is a copy of the same binary):

```
$ deja install kiro-auto --no-index --no-guidance
$ /tmp/hhtriage-bin2/deja install kiro-auto --no-index --no-guidance
           replaced the deja entry that was already here, which ran /tmp/hhtriage-bin/deja; also updated ~/.kiro/steering/deja.md
$ ls ~/.kiro/steering
deja.md  deja.md.bak
$ diff ~/.kiro/steering/deja.md ~/.kiro/steering/deja.md.bak
13c13
< Outside a session: /tmp/hhtriage-bin2/deja search -- "<query>".
---
> Outside a session: /tmp/hhtriage-bin/deja search -- "<query>".
$ deja uninstall kiro-auto
deja: kept 1 snapshot of configs you already had — ~/.kiro/steering/deja.md.bak — yours to remove
```

Control: two installs from the same path leave no .bak, and the goose recipe and command files (same "deja owns the file" shape) drop a backup holding deja's text on uninstall, per `TestUninstallRemovesTheGooseRecipeItWrote`.

Expected: uninstall removes a .bak that holds deja's own text, as it does for skills, command files and the goose recipe since #2600. Actual: deja's text is left in ~/.kiro and the user is told it is theirs.

The review note (N12) blamed a collision with kiro-cli's own `agent upgrade` backup name for ~/.kiro/agents/deja.json.bak; kiro-cli 2.22 on this machine has no `agent upgrade`, so that half is not confirmed. The captured case from the kiro-M round fits this bug as well: deja snapshotting its own agent file after kiro rewrote it.

Cause: `installTextFile` (cmd/deja/install_copilot_chat_prompt.go:77) removes only the file on uninstall; it never looks at the `.bak` that `writeIfChanged` (cmd/deja/install.go:2045) took on a rewrite. Callers: kiro steering (install_kiro.go:107), kiro agent fallbacks (install_kiro.go:229-242), kiro prompts (install_kiro.go:410), Copilot Chat prompt (install_copilot_chat_prompt.go:66).

Where to start: in `installTextFile`'s uninstall branch, call `restoreReplacedFile(path, ours)` (cmd/deja/guidance.go:787) with a predicate that recognises deja's text, e.g. the body with the exe line masked. Copy `TestUninstallRemovesTheGooseRecipeItWrote` (cmd/deja/goose_recipe_backup_test.go) with two installs from different exe paths before the uninstall, then assert no `kiroSteeringPath()+".bak"`.

issues.title: codex install says it updated "\"deja.old\"" on every run, including runs that changed nothing
issues.body:
When config.toml already runs deja under another name, install adopts that entry instead of adding a second one, which is right. But the note saying so prints on every later run next to "unchanged", and the key comes out quoted twice.

Reproduction (sandboxed HOME, CODEX_HOME=~/.codex):

```
$ printf '[mcp_servers."deja.old"]\ncommand = "/usr/local/bin/deja"\nargs = ["mcp"]\n' > ~/.codex/config.toml
$ deja install codex --no-index --no-guidance
codex: updated ~/.codex/config.toml
       updated "\"deja.old\"", which already ran deja, instead of adding a second entry
$ deja install codex --no-index --no-guidance
codex: unchanged ~/.codex/config.toml
       updated "\"deja.old\"", which already ran deja, instead of adding a second entry
```

The file itself is right after both runs: one `[mcp_servers."deja.old"]` block running the new binary. The duplicate block the review suspected comes only from the test binary being named deja.test, as the comment at the end of `TestInstallAdoptsTheEntryAlreadyRunningDeja` already says.

Control: claude-code over `"deja-vu": {"command": "/old/bin/deja", …}` says "replaced the deja entry that was already here" once, and the second run prints only "unchanged".

Expected: the note on the run that adopted the entry, naming the key as written (`"deja.old"`), and nothing on a run that changed nothing. Actual: the note repeats forever and reads `"\"deja.old\""`.

Cause: cmd/deja/install.go:3200 builds the note with `%q` over a key `tomlMCPHeader` has already quoted (install.go:3336), and sets it without looking at the action `writeIfChanged` returned.

Where to start: in `installTOML`, set the note only when `a != "unchanged"` and format the key with `%s`. Copy `TestInstallAdoptsTheEntryAlreadyRunningDeja` (cmd/deja/install_second_entry_test.go:19) for codex, calling `installTOML` directly with a block whose command basename is `deja` so the second run recognises it.

issues.title: codex install appends [mcp_servers.deja] under an existing [[mcp_servers.deja]] and leaves config.toml unparseable
issues.body:
A config.toml that spells deja's entry as an array of tables gets a second, plain-table `[mcp_servers.deja]` appended. TOML forbids declaring the same key as both, so the file stops loading.

Reproduction (sandboxed HOME, CODEX_HOME=~/.codex):

```
$ printf '[[mcp_servers.deja]]\ncommand = "/usr/local/bin/deja"\nargs = ["mcp"]\n' > ~/.codex/config.toml
$ deja install codex --no-index --no-guidance
codex: updated ~/.codex/config.toml
$ cat ~/.codex/config.toml
[[mcp_servers.deja]]
command = "/usr/local/bin/deja"
args = ["mcp"]

[mcp_servers.deja]
type = "stdio"
command = "/tmp/hhtriage-bin/deja"
args = ["mcp"]
$ python3 -c "import tomllib; tomllib.load(open('$HOME/.codex/config.toml','rb'))"
tomllib.TOMLDecodeError: Cannot declare ('mcp_servers', 'deja') twice (at line 5, column 18)
```

Control: the inline spellings of the same key (`[mcp_servers]` + `deja = {…}`, `mcp_servers.deja.command = …`) are refused with the file untouched, per #4554.

Expected: refuse the file and leave it as it was, like the inline shapes. Actual: deja turns a file Codex rejects on shape into one no TOML parser reads. Grok goes through the same `installTOML`.

Cause: `tomlInlineKey` (cmd/deja/install.go:3086) trims `[]` off any header, so `[[mcp_servers.deja]]` reads as the table deja is about to write and is skipped as "the same table". `tomlMCPHeader` (cmd/deja/install.go:3321) skips `[[` headers, so `installTOML` sees no deja block and appends one.

Where to start: in `tomlInlineKey`, treat a `[[...]]` header whose key path equals or prefixes `want` as a conflict and return the same inline error. Add the seed `"[[mcp_servers.deja]]\ncommand = \"/usr/local/bin/deja\"\n"` to the table in `TestInstallRefusesATOMLKeyWrittenInline` (cmd/deja/install_toml_inline_test.go:15) for codex and grok.

issues.title: goose: a refused /deja command still leaves deja-recipe.yaml behind
issues.body:
`installGooseCommand` writes the recipe file first and checks config.yaml's `slash_commands:` shape afterwards, so when it refuses the shape the recipe stays on disk with nothing pointing at it.

Reproduction (sandboxed HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$HOME/.config):

```
$ mkdir -p ~/.config/goose && printf 'slash_commands: []\n' > ~/.config/goose/config.yaml
$ deja install goose-auto --no-index
goose-auto: guidance created ~/.agents/skills/deja-history/SKILL.md
deja: install finished what it could; 1 target refused: goose-auto: ~/.config/goose/config.yaml: slash_commands: [] is on one line, and deja edits the block form — move it to a block and run this again — fix what it reports and run it again
$ ls ~/.config/goose
AGENTS.md  config.yaml  config.yaml.bak  deja-recipe.yaml
$ grep -c deja-recipe ~/.config/goose/config.yaml
0
```

Control: with `slash_commands:` absent the same install writes the recipe and a `- command: "deja"` entry naming it.

Expected: a refused command writes nothing. Actual: deja-recipe.yaml is created and only goes away on `deja uninstall goose-auto`.

Cause: cmd/deja/install_goose_command.go:174-185 writes the recipe before the refusals at :192 (duplicate key via `yamlTopKeyEnd`) and :221 (inline `slash_commands:` value).

Where to start: in `installGooseCommand`, move the recipe write after both checks, just before config.yaml is written. Add the inline-value case next to the "two slash_commands: keys accepted" check at the end of `TestInstallGooseEntryAroundCommentsAndTwoKeys` (cmd/deja/install_goose_entry_test.go:229) and assert `gooseRecipePath()` does not exist after the refusal.

issues.title: deja aider re-reads the whole chat history on every message when two aiders start together: 136 ms per message on a 46 MB history
issues.body:
When `deja aider` can't tell which session header in `.aider.chat.history.md` belongs to its run, `asker()` walks the whole history file again on every new message, inside aider's blocking read of the context pipe.

`asker()` caches the session id only once `AiderSessionAt` returns one. It returns "" in two cases: aider has not written its header yet, and two headers fall past the start offset within the same minute (two aiders started together on one history). In the second case it never resolves, so every message for the rest of the run pays a full walk of a file that only grows.

Reproduction (throwaway test in internal/sources, 2000 old sessions, then two headers stamped at launch):

```
$ go test ./internal/sources -run TestZZAiderSessionAtCost -v -count=1
    zz_triage_test.go:34: history 46 MB, AiderSessionAt returned "" each call, 136.325587ms per call
--- PASS: TestZZAiderSessionAtCost (1.53s)
```

Control: the same file with one header past the offset returns `aider-…-20261018T212027` on the first call, and `asker()` never scans again.

Expected: once the header window (launch to launch+1m) has closed, the answer is final and kept; the walk before the offset is done once, not per message.
Actual: a full read per message for the whole run, on the path aider waits on.

Cause: cmd/deja/aider_live.go:86 `asker()` only caches a non-empty id; internal/sources/aider_session_at.go:21 `AiderSessionAt` walks from byte 0 each call because the id counts every header before it.

Where to start: in `aiderLive.asker()`, remember that the lookup has given up once `time.Since(l.launch) > time.Minute` and fall back to `l.sid` without calling `AiderSessionAt` again. Optionally count the headers before `offset` once in `newAiderLive` so later calls read only past it. Copy the setup of `TestAiderSessionAtMatchesTheParser` in internal/sources/aider_session_at_test.go for a two-header history.

issues.title: Hermes on Postgres: a /branch copy and a delegate_task child read as sessions of their own, with no parent and project "hermes"
issues.body:
With `DEJA_HERMES_PG_DSN` set, deja reads Hermes' sessions table for cwd, source and parent_session_id only. It never reads `model_config._branched_from` or `_delegate_from`, which the SQLite path uses to file a branch as a fork and a delegate_task child as a sub-agent (#5141, #5248). On Postgres a branch is a full second copy of its source, and a child started under `--source tool`, the TUI or a gateway stands alone outside its parent's project.

Repro: a throwaway test next to `TestParseHermesPGReadsSessionKinds` in internal/sources/hermes_pg_test.go, with the fake store giving the sessions table a `model_config` column:

```go
columns:  `["id","source","parent_session_id","cwd","model_config"]`,
sessions: `[{"id":"s-src","source":"tui","cwd":"/w/app"},
  {"id":"s-br","source":"tui","model_config":"{\"_branched_from\":\"s-src\"}"},
  {"id":"s-del","source":"tui","model_config":"{\"_delegate_from\":\"s-src\"}"}]`,
```

```
$ go test ./internal/sources -run TestZZTriagePGBranchDelegate -v
    s-src kind="" parent="" project="w/app"
    s-br kind="" parent="" project="hermes"
    s-del kind="" parent="" project="hermes"
```

Control: the same three sessions in a SQLite state.db come out as `fork/s-src` and `subagent/s-src`, both under w/app (`TestAHermesBranchIsAForkOfItsSource`, `TestHermesSubagentHangsUnderItsParentAndFilesItsWritesThere` pass on main).

Expected: s-br is a fork of s-src, s-del a sub-agent of s-src, both in project w/app. Actual: both are top-level sessions in project "hermes", so recall from the branch answers with its own source's turns.

Cause: internal/sources/hermes_pg.go:159 selects only cwd, source and parent_session_id, and :178 builds hermesMeta from those three, dropping Branched and Delegated. The SQLite version is hermesSessionMetaWhere, internal/sources/hermes.go:463.

Where to start: hermesPGSessionMeta in internal/sources/hermes_pg.go. When `model_config` is in the column list, add `model_config::jsonb->>'_branched_from'` and `->>'_delegate_from'` as branched/delegated (guard the cast the way the SQLite query guards with json_valid), and copy both fields into hermesMeta. The test to copy is TestParseHermesPGReadsSessionKinds in hermes_pg_test.go; its fakePG answers any `from sessions` query with the canned rows, so put `"branched"`/`"delegated"` keys in them and assert kind, parent and project.

issues.title: hermes install refuses a config.yaml holding two copies of deja's own entry: "mcp_servers.deja is written 2 times"
issues.body:
When mcp_servers carries the deja key twice and both copies are deja's generated block (here spelled `deja:` and `'deja':`), install refuses instead of keeping the last copy, which is the one Hermes reads and the one deja would write anyway.

Reproduction (sandboxed HOME):

```
$ cat > ~/.hermes/config.yaml <<'EOF'
mcp_servers:
  deja:
    command: "/usr/local/bin/deja"
    args:
      - mcp
    enabled: true
  'deja':
    command: "/usr/local/bin/deja"
    args:
      - mcp
    enabled: true
EOF
$ deja install hermes --no-index --no-guidance
deja: install finished what it could; 1 target refused: hermes: ~/.hermes/config.yaml: mcp_servers.deja is written 2 times, and Hermes reads only the last — keep one and run this again — fix what it reports and run it again
```

Two identical reader-shaped copies (`args: [mcp]`, `timeout: 30`) give the same refusal. Control: the file with only the first block installs cleanly, and the #5172 shape (deja's block above a reader's block) is already collapsed to the reader's.

Expected: when every copy is the same entry, drop all but the last and edit that one; nothing about what Hermes runs changes. Actual: the target is refused and the user has to hand-edit.

Cause: `hermesEditEntry` (cmd/deja/install_hermes_entry.go:280) only collapses duplicates when exactly one entry is not `hermesGeneratedEntry`. Two generated copies leave `keep` empty, two reader copies leave it at two, and both fall through to the "written %d times" error at :304.

Where to start: in `hermesEditEntry`, before the `keep` filter, compare the copies' bodies (the lines between `e.start+1` and `e.end`); if they are all equal, cut every entry except the last. Add a case to the table in `TestInstallHermesEntryShapesFromReview` (cmd/deja/install_hermes_entry_test.go:252) next to "old installer's second key".

issues.title: cursor-auto on a read-only config dir writes mcp.json and hooks.json, then refuses the status line
issues.body:
The install pre-flight treats a config file that does not exist yet as writable, so when its directory cannot be created the target is refused only after the first two files are written. #5164 fixed the case where cli-config.json exists and is read-only; this is the case where it does not exist and its parent is read-only.

Reproduction (sandboxed HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$HOME/.config):

```
$ mkdir -p ~/.cursor ~/.config && chmod 0555 ~/.config
$ deja install cursor-auto --no-index --no-guidance
deja: install finished what it could; 1 target refused: cursor-auto: mkdir ~/.config/cursor: permission denied — check that path's permissions and run it again
$ ls ~/.cursor
hooks.json  mcp.json
```

Control, same steps with `chmod 755 ~/.config`:

```
cursor-auto: created ~/.cursor/mcp.json
             also created ~/.cursor/hooks.json; also created ~/.config/cursor/cli-config.json
```

Expected: a refused target writes nothing, as with a read-only cli-config.json. Actual: mcp.json and hooks.json are wired with hooks that point at a status line that was never written.

Cause: `configWritable` (cmd/deja/install.go:2034) returns nil for any error other than `fs.ErrPermission`, including "file not found", without checking that the file could be created. `cursorAutoPreflight` (cmd/deja/install.go:1333) reaches it through the dry-run in `installJSONStatusline` (cmd/deja/install_statusline_hosts.go:152). The same helper backs the pre-flights for hermes, grok, deepseek, cline and jsonc entries, so they share the gap.

Where to start: in `configWritable`, when the open fails with not-exist, walk up to the nearest directory that exists and check it is writable (e.g. create and remove a temp file there, or `unix.Access(dir, W_OK)` behind a build tag). Copy `TestCursorAutoRefusesAReadOnlyStatusLineFileBeforeWriting` in cmd/deja/install_cursor_config_test.go: chmod `filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(cursorCLIConfigPath()))` to 0555 instead of writing a 0444 file, and assert mcp.json and hooks.json are absent.

issues.title: proposal: mcp: add ClientSession.Discover to send server/discover on demand
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

In 2026-07-28 `ping` is removed, and `server/discover` is the spec's lightweight way to learn a server's identity, capabilities, supported versions and cache hints (`ttlMs`/`cacheScope`). Servers MUST implement it, and clients MAY call it at any time. go-sdk sends it only inside `Client.Connect`, and there's no public way to send it afterwards:

- `ClientSession` has no `Discover` method. The result is folded into `InitializeResult()`, and the `DiscoverResult` cache fields are dropped.
- `mcp.AddSendingCustomMethod` refuses the method:

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/mcp"
)

type discoverParams struct{ mcp.ParamsBase }
type discoverResult struct {
	mcp.ResultBase
	SupportedVersions []string `json:"supportedVersions"`
}

func main() {
	c := mcp.NewClient(&mcp.Implementation{Name: "repro", Version: "0.0.1"}, nil)
	err := mcp.AddSendingCustomMethod[*discoverParams, *discoverResult](c, "server/discover")
	fmt.Println("AddSendingCustomMethod(server/discover):", err)
}
```

Output (v1.8.0 and `main` @ 3ebc6d1):

```
AddSendingCustomMethod(server/discover): mcp: AddSendingCustomMethod: "server/discover" shadows a standard MCP method
```

Concrete uses we have:
1. **Health and liveness on a modern session.** `Ping` is gone on 2026-07-28 sessions (and after #1378 it fails fast there). `ListTools` isn't a substitute, because the SDK answers it from its own `ttlMs` cache without contacting the server. Today we open a *second* transport connection and write raw JSON-RPC, which for stdio means spawning a second server process.
2. **Refreshing server metadata** (capabilities, instructions, `serverInfo`) after the `DiscoverResult` `ttlMs` expires, without reconnecting.
3. **Diagnostics**, such as "which versions does this server support?", in an `integration test`-style command.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

```go
// Discover sends a server/discover request on the session's transport and
// returns the server's result, including Cacheable fields. It is valid on
// sessions negotiated at 2026-07-28 or later.
func (cs *ClientSession) Discover(ctx context.Context, params *DiscoverParams) (*DiscoverResult, error)
```

- It uses the session's negotiated version and `_meta` triple, like other requests.
- On a legacy (≤ 2025-11-25) session it returns an error without sending anything, the way `Ping` is handled on modern sessions in #1378.
- It returns `*DiscoverResult` unchanged, so callers see `SupportedVersions`, `Capabilities`, `Instructions`, `TTLMs`/`CacheScope` and `serverInfo` in `_meta`.
- Optionally, `Client.Connect` could use the same internal path, so behavior stays identical.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Allow `AddSendingCustomMethod` for `server/discover` only. It's untyped and contradicts the "standard method" guard, so it's worse than a typed method.
- Keep using a second raw connection. That works, but costs a process spawn per probe on stdio and duplicates `_meta` construction outside the SDK.

**Additional context**

- MCP 2026-07-28 `server/discover`: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/discover ("Calling `server/discover` is optional for clients… useful… for presenting server information")
- MCP 2026-07-28 Versioning ("Servers MUST implement `server/discover`. Clients MAY call it…"): https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning#protocol-version-negotiation
- Environment: go-sdk v1.8.0 and `main` @ 3ebc6d1; `go version go1.27.2 linux/amd64`.
issues.triage_reason: It adds a new exported method, ClientSession.Discover in the mcp package. Under the project rules that needs an accepted proposal, and the issue is still only a proposal.
issues.skip_reason: triage: not feasible: It adds a new exported method, ClientSession.Discover in the mcp package. Under the project rules that needs an accepted proposal, and the issue is still only a proposal.

issues.title: mcp: Client.Connect falls back to initialize after a 401 on server/discover, running the authorization flow twice
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

With an `OAuthHandler` on `StreamableClientTransport`, `Client.Connect` sends `server/discover` first. If that request is still unauthorized after `Authorize` ran, or `Authorize` itself fails, `Connect` treats the failure as "legacy server" and falls back to `initialize` (`mcp/client.go:376-378`: "fall back to the legacy initialize handshake on any non-modern error"). The `initialize` POST gets the same 401, so the transport calls `OAuthHandler.Authorize` a **second time** (`mcp/streamable.go:2325`).

With `auth.AuthorizationCodeHandler`, each `Authorize` is a full flow: PRM and AS discovery, registration, and a browser consent prompt. So one `Connect` shows the user **two consent prompts**. Before #1419 (merged today) it also created **two DCR clients** at the AS. #1419 now reuses the registration, but the second interactive authorization still happens on `main`. It happens whenever the first authorization doesn't produce a token the server accepts:

- the user denies or cancels consent (`Authorize` returns an error), and is asked again immediately;
- the AS issues a token the resource server rejects (we hit this with an AS that ignores RFC 8707 `resource`, so the token has no audience and a strict RS rejects it);
- the account lacks access.

A 401/403 isn't an era signal. The 2026-07-28 Streamable HTTP binding says a client should inspect a **400** body before falling back. A legacy server that requires auth would 401 `initialize` just the same, so falling back can't help and only repeats the prompt.

**To Reproduce**

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"sync/atomic"

	"github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/mcp"
	"golang.org/x/oauth2"
)

// countingHandler stands in for auth.AuthorizationCodeHandler; each Authorize
// call represents one full flow (discovery, registration, browser consent).
type countingHandler struct {
	authorizeCalls atomic.Int32
	fail           bool // simulate the user denying consent
}

func (h *countingHandler) TokenSource(context.Context) (oauth2.TokenSource, error) {
	return oauth2.StaticTokenSource(&oauth2.Token{AccessToken: "example-token", TokenType: "Bearer"}), nil
}

func (h *countingHandler) Authorize(ctx context.Context, req *http.Request, resp *http.Response) error {
	n := h.authorizeCalls.Add(1)
	fmt.Printf("  Authorize #%d for JSON-RPC method %q\n", n, req.Header.Get("Mcp-Method"))
	if h.fail {
		return errors.New("access_denied: user declined consent")
	}
	return nil
}

func run(name string, fail bool) {
	// Resource server that rejects every token.
	rs := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		w.Header().Set("WWW-Authenticate", `Bearer error="invalid_token", resource_metadata="https://rs.example/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"`)
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusUnauthorized)
	}))
	defer rs.Close()

	h := &countingHandler{fail: fail}
	c := mcp.NewClient(&mcp.Implementation{Name: "repro", Version: "0.0.1"}, nil)
	fmt.Println(name)
	_, err := c.Connect(context.Background(), &mcp.StreamableClientTransport{Endpoint: rs.URL, OAuthHandler: h}, nil)
	fmt.Printf("  Connect error: %v\n  Authorize calls: %d (want 1)\n", err, h.authorizeCalls.Load())
}

func main() {
	run("case 1: authorization succeeds but the token is still rejected", false)
	run("case 2: authorization fails (user denies consent)", true)
}
```

**Actual behavior** (v1.8.0 and `main` @ 3ebc6d1)

```
case 1: authorization succeeds but the token is still rejected
  Authorize #1 for JSON-RPC method "server/discover"
  Authorize #2 for JSON-RPC method ""
  Connect error: calling "initialize": sending "initialize": Unauthorized
  Authorize calls: 2 (want 1)
case 2: authorization fails (user denies consent)
  Authorize #1 for JSON-RPC method "server/discover"
  Authorize #2 for JSON-RPC method ""
  Connect error: calling "initialize": sending "initialize": rejected by transport: access_denied: user declined consent
  Authorize calls: 2 (want 1)
```

(The second call is the `initialize` POST, which carries no `Mcp-Method` header.)

**Expected behavior**

One `Authorize` call. `Connect` returns the `server/discover` authorization error, such as "Unauthorized" or the handler's `access_denied`, without trying `initialize`. The error is also more accurate: today it names `initialize`, a method the modern server never needed.

**Environment**
- go-sdk v1.8.0; also reproduced on `main` at 3ebc6d1 (which includes #1419)
- `go version go1.27.2 linux/amd64`
- Seen end to end with `auth.AuthorizationCodeHandler` + DCR against Ory Hydra v26.2.0 and a `RequireBearerToken`-protected stateless go-sdk server: two registrations and two consent prompts per `Connect` on v1.8.0.

**References**
- MCP 2026-07-28 Streamable HTTP → Backward Compatibility ("On `400 Bad Request`, the client SHOULD inspect the response body before falling back"): https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#backward-compatibility
- MCP 2026-07-28 Versioning → Backward Compatibility (HTTP: "attempt a modern request and inspect the body of a `400 Bad Request` before falling back"; legacy detection is "a `4xx` without a recognized modern error body"): https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning#backward-compatibility-with-initialization-based-versions
- The "any error" fallback comes from #1014. The 401 case doesn't seem to have been considered there.
- Related: #1416 / #1419 (duplicate DCR registration, fixed); #1332 / #1334 (same fallback loop on stdio, the timeout case).

**Suggested fix**

In `Client.Connect`, don't fall back when the `server/discover` failure is an authorization failure. Return it instead. Concretely:
- In `streamableClientConn.Write`, when the response is still 401/403 after `Authorize` (or `Authorize` returned an error), return an error that wraps an identifiable sentinel or type. That could be unexported, or a new exported `ErrUnauthorized` via a proposal.
- In `Connect`, if `errors.Is(err, thatSentinel)`, `cs.Close()` and return the error. Don't run the `initialize` fallback.

A legacy server behind auth still works. The first 401 runs `Authorize`, the retried `server/discover` reaches the legacy server with a valid token and gets its non-modern 400/404, and the fallback proceeds as today, so only one authorization happens. Tests: the two cases above should each assert exactly one `Authorize` call, plus a "legacy server behind auth" case that still connects through `initialize`.

**Additional context**

Our workaround is to run a single pre-flight authorization (401 → PRM → `Authorize`) before calling `Connect`. If it doesn't yield an accepted token, we don't call `Connect` at all.
issues.triage_reason: Add an unexported unauthorized sentinel in streamableClientConn.Write (mcp/streamable.go) and have Client.Connect (mcp/client.go) skip the initialize fallback on it; no exported API change, but it needs care around checkResponse/ErrRejected wrapping and new tests.

issues.title: oauthex: RegisterClient fails when the registration response carries "jwks" as a JSON object
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`oauthex.ClientRegistrationMetadata.JWKS` is declared as `string` (`oauthex/dcr.go:80` in v1.8.0, still the same on `main`):

```go
JWKS string `json:"jwks,omitempty"`
```

RFC 7591 §2 defines `jwks` as a JSON object: "The value of this field MUST be a JSON object containing a valid JWK Set." The client information response (§3.2.1) MUST echo all registered metadata. So a spec-conforming authorization server that returns `jwks`, even an empty `{}`, makes `RegisterClient` fail with a decode error, and dynamic client registration through `auth.AuthorizationCodeHandler` fails with it.

We hit this with Ory Hydra v26.2.0, which includes `"jwks": {}` in every DCR response, so DCR against Hydra never succeeds. The same type is used when *sending* a registration request, so a caller can't send a by-value JWK Set correctly either: it would be marshalled as a JSON string.

**To Reproduce**

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"

	"github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/oauthex"
)

func main() {
	// Registration endpoint returning an RFC 7591 response whose "jwks" is an
	// object (shape mirrors Ory Hydra v26.2.0).
	as := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusCreated)
		fmt.Fprint(w, `{
		  "client_id": "example-client-id",
		  "redirect_uris": ["http://127.0.0.1:7777/callback"],
		  "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none",
		  "jwks": {}
		}`)
	}))
	defer as.Close()

	res, err := oauthex.RegisterClient(context.Background(), as.URL+"/register",
		&oauthex.ClientRegistrationMetadata{
			ClientName:   "repro",
			RedirectURIs: []string{"http://127.0.0.1:7777/callback"},
		}, as.Client())
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Println("RegisterClient error:", err)
		return
	}
	fmt.Println("registered client_id:", res.ClientID)
}
```

**Expected behavior**

`registered client_id: example-client-id`

**Actual behavior** (v1.8.0 and `main` @ 3ebc6d1)

```
RegisterClient error: failed to decode successful registration response: json: cannot unmarshal "{}\n\t\t}" into Go struct field struct { ClientIDIssuedAt int64 "json:\"client_id_issued_at,omitempty\""; ClientSecretExpiresAt int64 "json:\"client_secret_expires_at,omitempty\""; *oauthex.alias }.jwks of type string (<response body>)
```

(I've cut the response body that the error appends. That echo is being reported separately through the security advisory process.)

**Environment**
- go-sdk v1.8.0; also reproduced on `main` at 3ebc6d1
- `go version go1.27.2 linux/amd64` (repro module declares `go 1.25.0`)
- Authorization server where we found it: Ory Hydra v26.2.0 (dev mode)

**References**
- RFC 7591 §2, Client Metadata, `jwks`: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7591#section-2
- RFC 7591 §3.2.1, Client Information Response: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7591#section-3.2.1
- RFC 7517 §5, JWK Set Format (a JSON object with a `keys` member): https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7517#section-5
- MCP 2026-07-28, Client Registration → Dynamic Client Registration: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/client-registration

**Suggested fix**

Changing the field's type is a breaking change under CONTRIBUTING's versioning policy, so here are two options:

1. **No API change (minimal):** decode `jwks` leniently. In `ClientRegistrationResponse.UnmarshalJSON`, shadow `jwks` in the aux struct as `json.RawMessage`. If it's a JSON string, unquote it. Otherwise store the raw JSON text in `JWKS`. On marshal, emit `JWKS` as raw JSON when it holds a JSON object. Document `JWKS` as "the JWK Set as JSON text."
2. **Proper typing (proposal):** add a `JWKSet json.RawMessage` field (or a typed JWK Set), deprecate `JWKS string`, and have both marshal and unmarshal use the new field.

Either way, a regression test should decode `{"client_id":"x","jwks":{}}` and `{"client_id":"x","jwks":{"keys":[]}}`.

**Additional context**

Our workaround is an `http.RoundTripper` on `AuthorizationCodeHandlerConfig.Client` that rewrites `"jwks":{…}` out of registration responses before the SDK decodes them.
issues.triage_reason: Lenient jwks decoding via a json.RawMessage shadow field in oauthex/dcr.go (ClientRegistrationResponse.UnmarshalJSON/MarshalJSON) needs no API change and is easy to test. Risk: maintainers may prefer a proposal for a typed field, and the metadata request-side marshalling needs extra handling.

issues.title: SandboxClaim adopts a crash-looping warm-pool Sandbox and reports Ready=True between restarts
issues.body:
### What happened?

A `SandboxClaim` binds to a warm-pool Sandbox whose container is crash-looping, then reports `Ready=True` for a few seconds after every restart. A caller waiting for Ready gets a broken sandbox.

`getCandidate` (`extensions/controllers/sandboxclaim_controller.go`) prefers a Ready member but falls back to an unready one, so a crash-looping member is adopted either way. Since #1439 it reads only `Sandbox.status`, which has no restart signal, so it can't tell a restarted member from a healthy one.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

`EXTENSIONS=true make deploy-kind`, then:

```yaml
apiVersion: extensions.agents.x-k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: SandboxTemplate
metadata:
  name: crash-tpl
spec:
  podTemplate:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3; echo boom; exit 1"]
---
apiVersion: extensions.agents.x-k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: SandboxWarmPool
metadata:
  name: crash-pool
spec:
  replicas: 1
  sandboxTemplateRef:
    name: crash-tpl
```

Wait until the pool's Pod has restarted twice, then create a `SandboxClaim` with `warmPoolRef: {name: crash-pool}` and watch its `Ready` condition:

```
07:56:37 bound to crash-pool-2nlkn  False  "Pod is Running but not Ready"  restarts=2
07:56:55                            True   "Pod is Ready"                  restarts=3
07:56:59                            False  "Pod is Running but not Ready"
07:57:54                            True   "Pod is Ready"                  restarts=4
```

### Version

`main` at 305e970 (v1.0.7-34), kind with Kubernetes v1.37.0.

### Anything else we need to know?

Proposed fix, once #1998 adds a restart signal to `Sandbox.status`:

1. `getCandidate` doesn't adopt a member whose containers have restarted, Ready or as fallback. The claim cold-starts instead.
2. The warm-pool controller replaces such members instead of holding them. Replacement should be rate-limited, or paused when every member is crash-looping, so a broken template doesn't churn; that state should show on the pool's status.

Both change default adoption behavior, so I'd like agreement before a PR. I'd leave `Ready` semantics alone. Happy to take this.
issues.triage_reason: The fix depends on a new restart signal in Sandbox.status (#1998, an API/CRD change needing make generate) and changes default adoption behavior in getCandidate (extensions/controllers/sandboxclaim_controller.go). The author explicitly wants maintainer agreement first, and the warm-pool replacement and rate-limiting part is large.
issues.skip_reason: triage: not feasible: The fix depends on a new restart signal in Sandbox.status (#1998, an API/CRD change needing make generate) and changes default adoption behavior in getCandidate (extensions/controllers/sandboxclaim_controller.go). The author explicitly wants maintainer agreement first, and the warm-pool replacement and rate-limiting part is large.

issues.title: Trace: a rename inside an amend or a squash loses the AI line attribution
issues.body:
A rename inside an amend or a squash of a session commit loses the AI line attribution. All the lines of the renamed file count as human.

Spec issue-3639 R-007 says: "Attribution MUST survive a file rename, amend, rebase, squash, and cherry-pick in the same clone. The CLI MUST match lines by content."

## Steps to reproduce

1. On a feature branch, an agent session writes `greeting.txt` with three lines, commits it, and pushes.
2. A human runs `git mv greeting.txt hello.txt`, then `git commit --amend --no-edit`, then `git push --force`.

## Expected

The stored session evidence lists the amended commit, and `hello.txt` has 3 AI lines and 0 human lines.

## Actual

The evidence lists the amended commit, but `hello.txt` has 0 AI lines and 3 human lines.

## Cause

The amended commit has no parent that holds `greeting.txt`, so git sees no rename: the commit creates `hello.txt`. The ledger of the session holds the line fingerprints under `greeting.txt` only. The push matches the lines of a file against the ledger of the same path and of the old paths of a rename, so no line of `hello.txt` matches. A squash that folds a rename into the session commit has the same result.

A rename in a separate commit keeps the AI lines, and an amend with no rename keeps them too.

## Evidence

The end-to-end suite found this (spec issue-3635). The first version of the Renames and rewrites check in #3685 used this flow. #3685 documents the gap in the Trace README and tests the amend and the rename separately.
issues.triage_reason: Fix is in attribution/enrich.go (the `take` pool lookup at line 377): add a content-based fallback to other ledger paths for added files with no OldPath. It is unit-testable in enrich_test.go but needs judgement to avoid false matches and keep the split of duplicate lines stable.

issues.summary: When git reports no OldPath (rename folded into an amend/squash), Enrich now matches the added lines of a new file against the session ledger's other paths by content, so renamed files keep AI attribution. README gap note updated. Regression test passes (run with GOTOOLCHAIN=auto since go.mod needs 1.27.3).
issues.repro_notes: Case 'a file renamed inside an amend matches the ledger by content': the ledger holds 3 lines under old.go and the commit adds a.go with no OldPath. Enrich gives 0 AI and 3 human added lines; 3 AI and 0 human are expected, because there is no content-based fallback to other ledger paths.

issues.title: bug: HPA analyzer rejects lowercase scaleTargetRef.kind (e.g. "statefulset") as "not an option"
issues.body:
## Expected Behavior

The HPA analyzer should accept `scaleTargetRef.kind` values regardless of letter case, the same way the Kubernetes API and the HPA controller do. An HPA whose `scaleTargetRef.kind` is `statefulset` (lowercase) works normally in the cluster, so k8sgpt should look up the StatefulSet target and run the usual checks on it.

## Current Behavior

`pkg/analyzer/hpa.go` compares `scaleTargetRef.Kind` with an exact-match `switch` (`"Deployment"`, `"ReplicationController"`, `"ReplicaSet"`, `"StatefulSet"`). A lowercase kind falls into the `default` branch and is reported as:

```
HorizontalPodAutoscaler uses statefulset as ScaleTargetRef which is not an option.
```

This is a false positive. The HPA is healthy (`AbleToScale=True`, `ScalingActive=True`) and the controller scales the StatefulSet normally.

It also creates a blind spot. Because the target is never looked up, the "target does not exist" and "does not have resource configured" checks are silently skipped for these HPAs.

The Grafana Alloy Helm chart produces exactly this manifest. Its HPA template renders `kind: {{ .Values.controller.type }}`, and `controller.type` is `statefulset` / `deployment` in lowercase (`operations/helm/charts/alloy/templates/hpa.yaml`). Every Alloy install that enables autoscaling therefore gets this finding.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a StatefulSet named `demo`.
2. Create an HPA that targets it with a lowercase kind:
   ```yaml
   apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
   kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
   metadata:
     name: demo
   spec:
     scaleTargetRef:
       apiVersion: apps/v1
       kind: statefulset
       name: demo
     minReplicas: 1
     maxReplicas: 3
     metrics:
       - type: Resource
         resource:
           name: cpu
           target:
             type: Utilization
             averageUtilization: 80
   ```
3. Check `kubectl get hpa demo -o yaml`. The conditions show `AbleToScale=True` and `ScalingActive=True`, which means the controller resolved the target.
4. Run `k8sgpt analyze --filter HorizontalPodAutoscaler`, or look at the operator's Result CRs. The "which is not an option" failure is reported.

## Environment

- **k8sgpt version:** v0.4.40 (also checked `main` at the time of writing; the `switch` is unchanged)
- **Kubernetes version:** v1.35 (EKS)
- **AI Backend/Provider:** OpenAI-compatible backend (not relevant to this bug)
- **OS/Platform:** k8sgpt-operator v0.2.29

## Additional Context

A possible fix is to normalize the kind before the `switch`, so that the existing cases match regardless of case:

```go
switch strings.ToLower(scaleTargetRef.Kind) {
case "deployment":
case "replicationcontroller":
case "replicaset":
case "statefulset":
```

The KEDA ScaledObject analyzer (`pkg/integration/keda/scaledobject_analyzer.go`) uses the same exact-match `switch` and probably has the same issue.

I searched the existing issues and PRs and could not find this reported. #1729 and #1831 handle unsupported kinds, but not letter case.
issues.triage_reason: Normalize scaleTargetRef.Kind with strings.ToLower in the switch in pkg/analyzer/hpa.go (AnalyzeHPA) and lowercase the case labels, plus a small test; the KEDA analyzer at pkg/integration/keda/scaledobject_analyzer.go:46 has the same switch and can be fixed alongside or separately.

issues.title: feat(trace): skip agent hooks when the Chainloop CLI is unavailable
issues.body:
Claude Code and Cursor hooks invoke `chainloop trace hook …` directly. If a developer opens a repository with these hooks installed but the Chainloop CLI is absent from PATH, the shell exits with code 127 before Chainloop's best-effort error handling can run.

Git hooks already check `command -v chainloop` before invoking the CLI. The OpenCode plugin catches process-start failures and lets the agent continue.

Add the same missing-CLI handling to the generated Claude Code and Cursor hook commands: check whether `chainloop` is available, exit successfully if it is missing, and execute the hook when it is present.

Example Claude Code hook entry:

```json
{
  "hooks": [
    {
      "type": "command",
      "command": "sh -c 'if ! command -v chainloop >/dev/null 2>&1; then exit 0; fi; exec chainloop trace hook claude post-tool-use'"
    }
  ]
}
```

For Cursor, apply the same guard to its existing `chainloop trace hook cursor …` commands, keeping the Cursor hook configuration format.

The guard returns success only when the CLI is unavailable. `exec` forwards stdin and output and preserves the CLI's exit status when it is available.

Acceptance criteria:

- Missing Chainloop CLI: agent hooks exit successfully without a command-not-found error.
- CLI available: preserve stdin, JSON stdout, and the hook command's exit status.
- Existing user hooks remain unchanged; installation remains idempotent.
- Re-running `chainloop trace init` updates existing Chainloop hook entries.
- Cover both missing and available CLI cases with tests.
- Keep Git pre-push `requireTrace` enforcement unchanged.

Codex support for this behavior is being added in #3684. This issue tracks the remaining Claude Code and Cursor hooks.
issues.triage_reason: Copy the Codex approach (hookCommandPrefix and marker matching in codex/hooks.go) into claude/hooks.go and cursor/hooks.go, update their tests, and add tests for the missing-CLI and CLI-present cases.

+	run := func(t *testing.T, pathDir, command string) (string, error) {
+		cmd := exec.Command("/bin/sh", "-c", command)
+		cmd.Env = []string{"PATH=" + pathDir}
+		cmd.Stdin = bytes.NewBufferString("input")
+		out, err := cmd.Output()
+		return string(out), err
+	}
+
+	for _, command := range commands {
+		t.Run("missing CLI exits successfully: "+command, func(t *testing.T) {
+			_, err := run(t, t.TempDir(), command)
+			require.NoError(t, err)
+		})
+
+		t.Run("available CLI keeps stdin, stdout and exit status: "+command, func(t *testing.T) {
+			dir := t.TempDir()
+			script := "#!/bin/sh\nread line\nprintf '%s' \"$line\"\nexit 3\n"
+			require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "chainloop"), []byte(script), 0o700))
+			out, err := run(t, dir, command)
+			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
+			require.ErrorAs(t, err, &exitErr)
+			assert.Equal(t, 3, exitErr.ExitCode())
+			assert.Equal(t, "input", out)
+		})
+	}
+}
issues.repro_notes: Installed Claude hook commands run `chainloop trace hook claude ...` directly, so with chainloop missing from PATH the shell exits 127 instead of 0. The test fails for that reason. It also checks that, with a stub CLI on PATH, stdin, stdout and exit status are preserved. Run from the app/cli module directory with GOTOOLCHAIN=auto because the local toolchain is older than go.mod requires; the pkg value is relative to that directory (./internal/trace/claude).

issues.title: Sandbox reports Ready=True while its Pod is terminating (computeReadyCondition ignores DeletionTimestamp)
issues.body:
### What happened?

A Sandbox (and the SandboxClaim bound to it) keeps reporting `Ready=True` for the whole time its backing Pod is terminating, which can be up to `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`.

During that window the Pod is already gone from the Service: EndpointSlices mark a terminating endpoint `ready: false`, so the headless Service's DNS stops resolving it. A client that waits for `Ready=True` and then connects by the Sandbox's Service hostname gets DNS misses or connection refusals, while `Ready` says the sandbox is usable.

We see this whenever a sandbox Pod is deleted (node drain, eviction, manual delete). Clients see roughly 30 to 70 seconds of connection failures while the claim reports Ready.

`computeReadyCondition` derives readiness from `pod.Status.Phase` and the Pod's `Ready` condition, and never checks `pod.DeletionTimestamp`. The kubelet keeps a terminating Pod in `Running` with `Ready=True` until its containers stop:
https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/blob/8b782ef6c2/controllers/sandbox_controller.go#L682-L705

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a Sandbox whose container ignores SIGTERM for a while, so termination is slow and the gap is easy to see:

   ```yaml
   apiVersion: agents.x-k8s.io/v1beta1
   kind: Sandbox
   metadata:
     name: sbx-demo
   spec:
     podTemplate:
       spec:
         terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60
         containers:
         - name: app
           image: busybox
           command: ["sh", "-c", "trap 'sleep 50' TERM; while true; do sleep 1; done"]
   ```

2. Wait for `Ready=True`, then delete the Pod: `kubectl delete pod sbx-demo --wait=false`.
3. Watch both:

   ```sh
   kubectl get pod sbx-demo -o jsonpath='{.metadata.deletionTimestamp}{"\n"}'
   kubectl get sandbox sbx-demo -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Ready")].status}{"\n"}'
   ```

**Expected:** `Ready=False` as soon as the Pod has a deletionTimestamp.
**Actual** (v1.0.4, sampled every ~3s), `Ready=True` for the full 60s grace period:

```
t=0s   pod uid=938ad5b1 deletionTimestamp=set phase=Running podReady=True  sandbox Ready=True/DependenciesReady
t=30s  pod uid=938ad5b1 deletionTimestamp=set phase=Running podReady=True  sandbox Ready=True/DependenciesReady
t=59s  pod uid=938ad5b1 deletionTimestamp=set phase=Running podReady=True  sandbox Ready=True/DependenciesReady
t=62s  pod uid=33cd28df (recreated)           phase=Pending podReady=False sandbox Ready=True/DependenciesReady
t=64s  pod uid=33cd28df (recreated)           phase=Running podReady=True  sandbox Ready=True/DependenciesReady
```

A SandboxClaim bound to the Sandbox mirrors the same status.

### Version

Seen on v1.0.4. The same code is in v1.0.7 and on `main` (8b782ef6c2).

### Anything else we need to know?

**Proposed fix.** In `computeReadyCondition`, after the Pod phase checks, add:

```go
if pod != nil && !pod.DeletionTimestamp.IsZero() {
	readyCondition.Reason = sandboxv1beta1.SandboxReasonPodTerminating
	readyCondition.Message = "Pod is terminating"
	return readyCondition
}
```

The suspended path already returns earlier, so this doesn't affect suspend. `SandboxReasonPodTerminating` would be a new constant with the value `"PodTerminating"`, the string the Suspended condition already uses and the one #1761 adds for `PodScheduled`.

**Related:**
- #1748 / #1761: the same missing lifecycle signal, but for the warm pool's unschedulable hold, through `PodScheduled`. That doesn't cover `Ready` for a scheduled Pod.
- #1872: a client-side opt-in for stale claim readiness after a spec change. That's a different staleness, about generation, not Pod termination.

**Current workaround:** clients read the Pod directly and treat a deletionTimestamp as not ready.
issues.triage_reason: Add a DeletionTimestamp check in computeReadyCondition (controllers/sandbox_controller.go) that returns Ready=False/PodTerminating, plus a fake-client unit test. The existing constant already has the needed value, so no generated code changes.

issues.title: benchmark lanes: chrome-sandbox image build fails intermittently (systemd postinst under arm64 emulation)
issues.body:
The kops benchmark presubmits build every example image before the benchmark runs. The `examples/chrome-sandbox` build fails intermittently at `RUN apt-get update && apt-get install --yes --no-install-recommends chromium` (exit code 100) on PRs that do not touch the example:

| run | lane | PR |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-16 10:59 UTC | benchmarks-kops-gcp-cilium | #1954 |
| 2026-10-20 21:30 UTC | benchmarks-kops-gcp-kindnet | #1991 |
| 2026-10-21 04:12 UTC | benchmarks-kops-gcp-cilium | #1856 |

Build log (same in all three):

```
#27 167.4 Initializing machine ID from random generator.
#27 167.9 Failed to take /etc/passwd lock: Invalid argument
#27 168.0 dpkg: error processing package systemd (--configure):
#27 168.0  installed systemd package post-installation script subprocess returned error exit status 1
#27 168.1 E: Sub-process /usr/bin/dpkg returned an error code (1)
```

`chromium` on `debian:13-slim` pulls in `systemd` as a dependency, and the systemd post-install script fails under QEMU user-mode emulation (the `@INC` paths in the same log show `aarch64-linux-gnu`, so this is the arm64 leg of the multi-arch `docker buildx build`). It looks intermittent only because the step is normally served from the per-project registry build cache; a fresh boskos project with no `chrome-sandbox:buildcache` rebuilds the layer and hits it.

Options, smallest first:
1. Build `chrome-sandbox` for the host platform only in the benchmark lanes (it is never run on arm64 there).
2. Keep `systemd` out of the image: `apt-get install --no-install-recommends chromium` still installs it as a hard dependency, so this needs an `apt` pin or `equivs` stub.
3. Mask the systemd post-install under emulation.

The e2e presubmit builds the same image and has not failed this way, which supports the cache-miss explanation.

issues.title: trace: expand same-call attribution beyond foreground Claude Bash
issues.body:
## Context

Follow-up to [#3625](https://github.com/chainloop-dev/chainloop/issues/3625) and [PR #3631](https://github.com/chainloop-dev/chainloop/pull/3631). The PR is intentionally scoped to a foreground native Claude Code Bash call, following [maintainer review](https://github.com/chainloop-dev/chainloop/pull/3631#issuecomment-6262967627).

It currently uses Claude Code's [hook input update mechanism](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/hooks) to export an opaque call token into the command before Git hooks run.

## Scope

Investigate and implement broader runtime support for same-call commit attribution:

- background Bash calls whose process can outlive `PostToolUse`;
- coexistence with another hook that also rewrites `updatedInput`;
- narrow Bash permission matchers that can behave differently after command rewriting;
- Cursor, OpenCode, and other providers that do not expose the same pre-execution command-rewrite contract;
- explicit capability reporting when exact call correlation is unavailable.

## Expected behavior

Every supported provider/runtime has a documented, tested way to correlate a Git hook with the exact command call that made the staged change. Unsupported combinations fail visibly or remain explicitly documented as unsupported instead of silently losing attribution.

## Acceptance criteria

- Background-call lifecycle and snapshot retention are defined and tested.
- Multiple input-rewriting hooks have deterministic composition or a documented incompatibility.
- Narrow permission configurations retain their intended behavior.
- Each provider's capability matrix entry matches observable support.
- Unsupported runtimes surface a clear limitation or warning.
- Integration tests cover every provider/runtime combination declared supported.
issues.triage_reason: Large, vague multi-provider investigation in app/cli/internal/trace (background lifecycle, hook composition, permission matchers, Cursor/OpenCode support) that needs maintainer design decisions and real runtimes to test.
issues.skip_reason: triage: not feasible: Large, vague multi-provider investigation in app/cli/internal/trace (background lifecycle, hook composition, permission matchers, Cursor/OpenCode support) that needs maintainer design decisions and real runtimes to test.

issues.title: trace: safely snapshot tracked paths below ignored directories
issues.body:
## Context

Follow-up to [#3625](https://github.com/chainloop-dev/chainloop/issues/3625) and [PR #3631](https://github.com/chainloop-dev/chainloop/pull/3631). The PR is restoring the existing worktree snapshot behavior from `main` while narrowing its same-call fix, following [maintainer review](https://github.com/chainloop-dev/chainloop/pull/3631#issuecomment-6262967627).

The existing walker prunes directories matched by [`.gitignore`](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitignore). A force-added tracked file below such a directory can therefore be absent from the snapshot.

## Scope

- include tracked regular files below ignored directories without scanning unrelated ignored content;
- keep untracked ignored paths excluded;
- define the interaction with intent-to-add entries tracked in [#3698](https://github.com/chainloop-dev/chainloop/issues/3698);
- reject symlinked path components and final symlinks;
- avoid opening FIFOs, devices, sockets, and other non-regular files;
- keep every read confined to the checkout root.

## Expected behavior

Tracked regular files receive correct before/after snapshots even below ignored directories. Expanding coverage must not allow path traversal outside the checkout or block on special files.

## Acceptance criteria

- A force-added tracked file below an ignored directory is snapshotted and compared.
- An untracked ignored sibling is not snapshotted.
- Intent-to-add paths follow the semantics decided in #3698.
- Escaping and in-repository symlink ancestors are not followed.
- FIFOs and other non-regular files are checked before open and skipped.
- Race-enabled tests cover ignored-directory and path-safety behavior.
issues.triage_reason: The change is in the snapshot walker in app/cli/internal/trace/git/gogit.go. It needs tracked-path enumeration under ignored dirs, symlink and special-file safety, and root confinement. It also depends on the undecided #3698 intent-to-add semantics and on in-flight PR #3631.

issues.title: trace: make same-call worktree comparison Git-clean aware
issues.body:
## Context

Follow-up to [#3625](https://github.com/chainloop-dev/chainloop/issues/3625) and [PR #3631](https://github.com/chainloop-dev/chainloop/pull/3631). The PR is being narrowed to a raw staged-blob versus worktree-byte comparison, as requested in [maintainer review](https://github.com/chainloop-dev/chainloop/pull/3631#issuecomment-6262967627).

That conservative comparison can keep a pending range when Git would consider the worktree clean. This issue tracks complete [`gitattributes`](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitattributes) and clean-conversion behavior separately.

## Scope

- honor attribute precedence across system, global, repository, nested, and `.git/info/attributes` sources;
- honor `core.attributesFile`;
- reproduce text and EOL normalization, including `text`, `-text`, `eol`, and `core.autocrlf`;
- define safe behavior for `filter.<driver>.clean` and `filter.<driver>.process` without unexpectedly executing repository-controlled commands;
- include relevant mode comparison semantics.

## Expected behavior

Same-call checkpoint reconciliation should distinguish a real unstaged edit from bytes that differ only because Git's clean conversion changes the indexed representation. Attribution must stay conservative when a configured transformation cannot be reproduced safely.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tests cover global, local, nested, and info attribute sources.
- CRLF/LF behavior matches Git for text and binary paths.
- No-op and transforming clean filters have explicit, tested behavior.
- Repository-controlled filters are not executed implicitly without an approved security design.
- A documented fallback keeps uncertain paths pending instead of consuming attribution.
issues.triage_reason: Large, design-heavy scope (gitattributes precedence, autocrlf/EOL, clean/process filter security) in app/cli/internal/trace/git; depends on unmerged PR #3631 and needs maintainer decisions.

issues.title: trace: support advanced Git index semantics for same-call attribution
issues.body:
## Context

Follow-up to [#3625](https://github.com/chainloop-dev/chainloop/issues/3625) and [PR #3631](https://github.com/chainloop-dev/chainloop/pull/3631). This scope was intentionally deferred while narrowing the PR to the normal-index foreground Claude Bash case, following [maintainer review](https://github.com/chainloop-dev/chainloop/pull/3631#issuecomment-6262967627).

## Scope

Support same-call attribution when Git does not use the repository's normal stage-0 index:

- honor [`GIT_INDEX_FILE`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git#Documentation/git.txt-codeGITINDEXFILEcode), including [`git commit --only <path>`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit#Documentation/git-commit.txt---only);
- exclude [intent-to-add entries](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-add#Documentation/git-add.txt--intent-to-add) that are not committed content;
- detect conflict-stage to stage-0 resolution without missing a changed path;
- read the exact object recorded by the index without being redirected by [replacement refs](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-replace).

## Expected behavior

The pre-call and commit-time snapshots use the index Git is actually committing. Only content newly staged by that Bash call is attributed, and special index states cannot add or omit session attribution incorrectly.

## Acceptance criteria

- A same-call `git commit --only <path>` receives the correct session trailer.
- Pre-existing normal-index content is not claimed by a temporary-index commit.
- Intent-to-add paths do not receive attribution unless committed.
- Resolving an unmerged path changes the index signature even when stage 0 reuses an existing blob.
- Indexed blob reads remain exact in repositories with `refs/replace/*`.
- Race-enabled lifecycle tests cover the temporary-index commit path.
issues.triage_reason: The same-call attribution code from PR #3631 isn't on main under app/cli/internal/trace (git/exec.go, attribution/), and the issue bundles four subtle Git index behaviors plus lifecycle tests. That is too large and vague for a small focused change.

issues.body:
## Problem

The compatibility matrix marks Pi skills tracking as `No`. Pi can load project skills, but its provider does not implement `trace.SkillTracker`, so evidence contains no skill package or use records.

## Scope

Implement Pi skill tracking through the shared `SkillTracker` contract. Detect completed filesystem skill loads from the live Pi transcript at hook time, snapshot the skill package once, and retain push-time fallback behavior for missed loads.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Implement `NewSkillLoads`, `SessionSkills`, and `SkillRoots` for Pi with compile-time interface coverage.
- [ ] Detect no-use, repeated-use, and multiple completed skill loads in first-use order.
- [ ] Classify project, user, organization, and plugin roots consistently with shared packaging.
- [ ] Snapshot skill contents at use time so later edits do not silently replace the recorded version.
- [ ] Preserve the existing warning when a snapshot can only be made at push.
- [ ] Ignore incomplete or failed load attempts.
- [ ] Add provider/action regressions and a live Pi skill scenario that inspects stored evidence.
- [ ] Update the compatibility matrix from measured results.

## Non-goals

- Redesigning the shared skill evidence schema.
- Tracking skills that Pi never exposes through filesystem or transcript records.

## References

- Shared skills design: #3540.
- Baseline Pi support: #3704.
issues.triage_reason: Pi needs a new skills.go in app/cli/internal/trace/pi modelled on codex/opencode skills.go, but the live e2e scenario and measured matrix can't be produced here, and the Pi transcript format for skill loads needs inference.

issues.title: Trace: capture Pi subagent evidence from a pinned result format
issues.body:
## Problem

Pi support records only the selected root session. The compatibility matrix marks Pi subagents as `No`, so child conversations, tool activity, and usage are absent from `CHAINLOOP_AI_CODING_SESSION` evidence.

## Scope

Support the commit-pinned result format of Pi's official subagent example extension. Map identifiable child messages and usage into deterministic subagent evidence and raw-session streams.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pin the supported official Pi subagent extension commit and supporting files.
- [ ] Parse single, parallel, and chained child results with deterministic child IDs and raw streams.
- [ ] Preserve child conversation content and tool results, not only aggregate token counts.
- [ ] Count child input, output, cache, and cost exactly once under the normalized accounting contract from #3706.
- [ ] Handle failed children and malformed optional result details without blocking push.
- [ ] Exclude abandoned root branches and unrelated extension records.
- [ ] Add provider/parser/action regressions and a live Pi E2E scenario.
- [ ] Update the Pi compatibility cell from measured results, using `Partial` if only the pinned official format is supported.

## Non-goals

- Inferring subagents from `parentSession` alone.
- Supporting arbitrary third-party Pi extensions.
- Changing Pi's root session-tree selection contract.

## Dependencies

- #3706 must define Pi cache and total-token semantics before child usage is aggregated.
- Baseline Pi support shipped in #3704.
issues.triage_reason: Large multi-part feature in app/cli/internal/trace/pi (parse.go, provider.go). It depends on #3706 accounting semantics, an external pinned extension format and a live Pi E2E scenario, so it needs maintainer decisions and real external tooling.
issues.skip_reason: triage: not feasible: Large multi-part feature in app/cli/internal/trace/pi (parse.go, provider.go). It depends on #3706 accounting semantics, an external pinned extension format and a live Pi E2E scenario, so it needs maintainer decisions and real external tooling.

issues.title: Trace: normalize Pi cache token totals
issues.body:
## Problem
Pi v1 evidence used Pi's supplied `totalTokens`, which can include cache reads and writes. That inflates the reported total even when native input, output, and cache fields are separate.

## Scope
Pi token normalization only. The implementation is already under review in PR #3719; this focused tracker makes that slice explicit under the broader cross-provider audit #3706.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pi evidence version distinguishes cache-exclusive totals from historical v1 totals.
- [ ] Preserve native input, output, cache-read, cache-write, and provider-reported cost. Set total to input + output, excluding cache.
- [ ] Handle malformed and overflowing usage deterministically and count only the selected branch, including resumed history.
- [ ] Independently compare stored evidence with raw Pi counters in an actual cache-active run and update only the Pi compatibility cell.
- [ ] Verify the signed Pi-scoped PR and document any remaining broader #3706 gaps without closing the parent issue.

## Non-goals
- Changing Codex, Claude, Cursor, or OpenCode accounting.
- Repricing provider cost or changing the shared evidence schema.
issues.triage_reason: The code change belongs in app/cli/internal/trace/pi/parse.go (total = input + output, with an evidence version bump). PR #3719 already covers it, and the acceptance criteria include a live cache-active run, signed-PR verification, and branch/resume handling. A bot can't do those, and a duplicate PR would likely be rejected.

### Linked issue

- Closes: #1539

Fixes #1539

**Problem:**
The error-body scrub in `auth/gcp` removes the request's `UserID` and `ContinueURI` from service error text. When the `UserID` is a substring of the `ContinueURI` and the service echoes the URI with escapes such as `\/`, the scrub cannot match the whole URI. It matches the short `UserID` inside it and writes `[redacted]` in the middle. A reader sees most of the redirect URI. For example, `https://my-app.test/oauth/callback` with `UserID` `app` came back as `https:\/\/my-[redacted].test\/oauth\/callback`.

**Solution:**
A new check, `splitsContainer`, runs in `redactedForError`. It detects the case where one secret sits inside a longer secret, and the longer one appears only in an escaped spelling (found by decoding the text). In that case the response is withheld, the same as other text the scrub cannot clean safely. Bodies that name only the `UserID`, and bodies that echo the URI unescaped, are still scrubbed and shown. I updated the doc comment on `redactedForError`, which described this gap as a known limitation.

### Behavior change

When the `UserID` is a substring of the `ContinueURI` and the service echoes the URI in an escaped spelling, the error now carries the withheld text instead of a partly visible URI. Other error text is unchanged.

### Testing Plan

**Unit Tests:**

- [x] All unit tests pass locally.

Added tests in `auth/gcp/client_test.go`:

- `TestContinueURISurvivesTheUserIDMarker`: escaped, unicode-escaped, partly escaped and plain bodies must not show any 8-byte piece of the URI. A body naming only the `UserID` must still come back with the `UserID` redacted and the rest shown.
- `TestRedactedForErrorWithholdsEscapedContainer`: checks which bodies are withheld and which are shown, including case differences and an unrelated escape.

**With your source change reverted and your tests kept, which test fails?**

`TestContinueURISurvivesTheUserIDMarker` (the escaped subtests) and `TestRedactedForErrorWithholdsEscapedContainer` fail without the change.

**Manual End-to-End (E2E) Tests:**

Not run. The change touches only local error-text handling, with no live API call.

Fixes #14447

RBAC CEL matcher expressions were only parsed (`env.Parse`) and never type-checked. An expression that uses a function Envoy does not support, such as `.split(' ')`, was accepted by kgateway. Envoy then rejected it when it loaded the xDS config.

What changed:
- Expressions are now compiled with `env.Compile` in one shared env (`newCELEnv`).
- The env declares the Envoy attribute roots (for example `metadata` and `filter_state`) as `dyn`, so valid expressions still compile.
- Unsupported functions such as `split` now fail during translation with a clear error. They no longer reach Envoy.

The `.split(' ')` example on the external docs site is still wrong and needs a separate fix. This PR does not change `docs/`.

# Change Type

/kind fix

# Changelog

```release-note
RBAC CEL matchExpressions in TrafficPolicy are now compiled when the policy is translated. Expressions that use functions Envoy does not support, such as `split`, are reported as errors. Before, Envoy rejected them when it loaded the config.
```

- `TestTranslateRBACRejectsUnsupportedCELFunctions` checks that `.split(' ')` fails with the expected error.
- `TestTranslateRBACCELCompileErrors` checks compile errors, and that valid expressions, including ones that use `filter_state`, still translate.

These tests and the project checks pass.

- Added `TestDiagRestoreNoZstd` in `internal/sources` for the new helper.
- The regression test and the project's checks pass.

## Notes

No data was lost before this change. The only effect was an extra index rewrite on the second run.

{"parsed":{"title":"fix(llm): re-send completion once on net error after 200 headers","body":"Fixes #1789

## Description

A non-streaming OpenAI completion now gets one re-send when reading a 2xx response body fails with a `*net.OpError`, such as a connection reset by peer. Before this change, only `io.ErrUnexpectedEOF` was re-sent, so a reset after the headers failed the request at once.

- The re-send follows the same rules as the existing EOF recovery. It happens once only, the `ctx.Err()` checks stay, and the first attempt is revised to `network` / `response_decode`.
- Context errors are excluded, so an expired deadline still ends the call without a replay.
- `classifyBoundaryError` now recognizes `*net.OpError`. A reset on the re-send is recorded as an error attempt and not as a success.
- Scope is non-streaming Chat Completions only. The streaming, Anthropic and Responses paths are unchanged.

{"parsed":{"title":"fix(reports): report Merged when a policy is only partly overridden","body":"# Description

Fixes #14861

A policy can apply to several filter chains under one ancestor, for example a Gateway-wide ListenerPolicy on a Gateway with several HTTPS listeners. The per-chain attachment states are combined into one condition. If a `sectionName`-targeted policy overrode the Gateway-wide one on some listeners, the Gateway-wide policy was reported as `Attached=False, reason: Overridden`, even though it was still applied on the other listeners.

`addAttachmentCondition` in `pkg/reports/policy.go` checked `Overridden` before `Merged` and `Attached`. It now reports `Attached=True, reason: Merged` when `Overridden` is combined with `Attached` or `Merged`. It reports `Overridden` only when that is the only state set.

The translator golden outputs that showed `Overridden` for a partly applied policy were refreshed with `REFRESH_GOLDEN=true`. These include `listener-policy/transport-socket-connect-timeout-per-listener.yaml` and several traffic-policy and delegation outputs.

Testing: added `TestAddAttachmentConditionPartiallyOverriddenReportsMerged` in `pkg/reports/policy_test.go`. It and the existing translator golden tests pass, along with the project's checks.

# Change Type

/kind fix

# Changelog

```release-note
Fix policy status reporting `Attached=False/Overridden` when the policy is overridden on only some of a Gateway's listeners. It now reports `Attached=True/Merged`.
```

### Linked issue

- Closes: #848

**Problem:**
`adkgo deploy agentEngine` had no way to pass custom environment variables to the deployed agent.

**Solution:**
Add a repeatable `--env NAME=VALUE` flag. The value is split at the first `=`, so values may contain `=`. The flags are merged with the built-in default variables and applied on both create and update. If a name matches a built-in variable, the `--env` value is used. On update, the env field and its update mask entry are added only when `--env` is given, so existing deployments keep their current env when the flag is not used.

### Behavior change

Nothing changes unless `--env` is passed. Without it, create and update send the same env and update mask as before.

- [x] All unit tests pass locally.

- `TestEnvFlag_IsRepeatable`: the command has a repeatable `--env` flag.

- `TestDeploymentEnvAndUpdate`: env is merged on create, and on update the env is touched only when `--env` is given.

The new tests fail to build or run without the change, since they need the `--env` flag and the new helpers (`envVars`, `deploymentEnv`, `setUpdateEnv`).

Not run. Deployment needs a real Google Cloud project.
